Purpose, Function • The fuel pump control module controls the voltage applied to the fuel pump for reducing fuel pump load and improving fuel economy. • Controls the voltage applied to the fuel pump based on the control signal from the PCM. Construction • The fuel pump control module is located on the left side in the trunk compartment. Operation • Controls the voltage applied to the fuel pump based on the control signal from the PCM. • In addition, an on-board diagnostic function is equipped, and if there is a malfunction in the fuel pump control module, a diagnostic signal is sent to the PCM. • The PCM stores a DTC if necessary according to the received diagnostic signal. • For the fuel pump control module, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See FUEL PUMP CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fail-safe P025B:00 • Stops the fuel pump control (when overheating is detected). P0629:00 • Stops the fuel pump control.

Outline • In the direct fuel injection system, the temperature in the combustion chamber is lowered by injecting fuel directly into the combustion chamber using multi-hole injectors and atomizing the fuel. In addition, improved engine output and fuel economy have been realized by increasing the air density during compression. • High response has been realized because there is no time lag from when the fuel injection starts until the fuel is provided to the combustion chamber. Structure • The direct fuel injection system consists of the following parts. Part name Reference High pressure fuel pump (See HIGH PRESSURE FUEL PUMP [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fuel injector (See FUEL INJECTOR [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fuel distributor (See FUEL DISTRIBUTOR [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fuel pressure sensor (See FUEL PRESSURE SENSOR [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Relief valve ― Operation • Fuel from the high pressure fuel pump injects fuel directly into the cylinder using the fuel injector via the fuel distributor. Injected, atomized fuel during the intake stroke is diffused uniformly in the combustion chamber by the flow of intake air, achieving a uniform air-fuel mixture. For the fuel injection control, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM, FUEL INJECTION CONTROL. (See FUEL INJECTION CONTROL SYSTEM [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) • The fuel pressure sensor detects the fuel pressure in the fuel distributor and sends a fuel pressure signal to the PCM. Based on the signal from the fuel pressure sensor, the PCM controls the high pressure fuel pump so that the fuel pressure is in accordance with the driving conditions. For the high pressure fuel pump control, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See HIGH PRESSURE FUEL PUMP CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) • Fuel pressure is adjusted by the spill valve control solenoid valve, and a relief valve is equipped to ensure safety in case of a malfunction. If the fuel pressure in the high pressure fuel pump reaches the set pressure, the relief valve is mechanically opened and fuel is returned to the fuel tank side.

Purpose, Function • The fuel pump unit supplies fuel in the fuel tank to the high pressure fuel pump. • Based on the control signal from the PCM, the fuel pump operates by the operation of the fuel pump relay and the fuel pump control module. Construction • The fuel pump unit is located on the fuel tank. • The fuel pump unit consists of a fuel pump, fuel filter (low-pressure) fuel filter (high-pressure), pressure regulator, and lower cover. Operation • Based on the control signal from the PCM, the fuel pump suctions fuel in the lower cover and pumps it to the high pressure fuel pump. After fuel is sufficiently filtered through the fuel filter (low-pressure) and fuel filter (high-pressure), fuel pressure is adjusted to approx. 450 kPa {4.59 kgf/cm 2 , 65.3 psi} (European (L.H.D.), General (L.H.D.) specs.) approx. 430 kPa {4.38 kgf/cm 2 , 62.4 psi} (Except European (L.H.D.), General (L.H.D.) specs.) by the pressure regulator. • For fuel pump control details, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM. (See FUEL PUMP CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fail-safe • Function not equipped.

Outline • To reduce fuel evaporation in the fuel tank, the returnless fuel system adjusts the fuel amount (fuel pressure) ejected from the fuel pump and prevents fuel warmed in the engine compartment from returning. System Diagram Structure • The returnless fuel system consists of the following parts: Part name Reference Fuel filter (low-pressure) (See FUEL PUMP UNIT [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fuel filter (high-pressure) Pressure regulator Fuel pump Operation • Fuel in the fuel tank is pumped out through the fuel filter (low-pressure) by the fuel pump, filtered by the fuel filter (high-pressure), and then regulated to a specified pressure by the pressure regulator. The regulated fuel is sent to the high pressure fuel pump, and unnecessary regulated fuel is returned from the pressure regulator to the fuel tank.

Purpose, Function • The fuel tank stores fuel safely. Construction • The fuel tank is located under the rear seat. • The fuel tank is made of plastic. • The following parts are integrated in the fuel tank. ― Non-return valve (See NON-RETURN VALVE [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) ― Rollover valve (See ROLLOVER VALVE [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .)

Purpose, Function • Atomization of the fuel decreases vaporization heat in the combustion chamber by injecting it from multiple holes, decreasing the air temperature in the combustion chamber. In addition, engine output and fuel economy have been improved by increasing the air density in the combustion chamber during compression. • Injects fuel according to the control signal from the PCM. Construction • The fuel injectors are located on the cylinder heads. • Multi-hole injectors have been adopted for the fuel injectors. • The fuel injectors have six injection holes in section A shown in the figure. Operation • Injects fuel according to the signal from the PCM. The fuel injection time is determined by the energization time of the coil. • For fuel injection control details, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See FUEL INJECTION CONTROL SYSTEM [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fail-safe • Function not equipped.

Purpose, Function • The fuel pump relay controls the fuel pump on/off according to control signals from the PCM. • Operates the fuel pump only at engine start or while the engine is running to improve safety. Construction • The fuel pump relay is located on the relay and fuse block. Operation • The contact point is on when the coil is energized based on the signals from the PCM, and battery voltage is supplied to the fuel pump control module. Fail-safe • Function not equipped.

Purpose, Function • The fuel injector relay supplies voltage to the PCM for the fuel injectors and the spill valve control solenoid valve operation. Construction • The fuel injector relay is located on the relay and fuse block. • A normally open relay has been adopted for the fuel injector relay. When electric current flows to the coil, the contact point is drawn by the generated electromagnetic power and switches on. Operation 1. The contact point is on (1) when the fuel injector relay coil is energized by the battery power from the main relay. 2. Power is supplied (2) to the PCM for the fuel injector and the spill valve control solenoid valve operation. Fail-safe • Function not equipped.

Purpose, Function • The fuel distributer distributes fuel pumped from the high pressure fuel pump to each fuel injector. Construction • The fuel distributor is located on the cylinder head. • The fuel distributor is integrated with the fuel pressure sensor.

Purpose, Function • The non-return valve enhances safety by preventing fuel from returning to the fuel filler opening. Construction • The non-return valve is located on the fuel tank. • A single valve type has been adopted for the non-return valve. Operation • Normally, the valve is closed as shown by the dotted line in the figure. When refueling, it opens as shown by the solid line due to the force caused by the flow of fuel. When refueling is finished, the valve returns to the normal valve position by spring force.

Purpose, Function • The high pressure fuel pump applies pressure to fuel sent from the fuel pump equipped on the fuel tank, and then pumps it to the fuel distributor. Construction • The high pressure fuel pump is located on the exhaust camshaft with the vacuum pump. • The high pressure fuel pump consists of a spill valve control solenoid valve, spill valve, piston, and spring. Operation • Fuel is suctioned and pumped by the up and down movement of the piston caused by the rotation of the cam installed to the rear end of the camshaft (exhaust side). • Based on the control signal from the PCM, the spill valve solenoid valve opens and closes in the high pressure fuel pump. • For the high pressure fuel pump control details, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See HIGH PRESSURE FUEL PUMP CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Warning • Fuel line spills and leakage from the pressurized fuel system are dangerous. Fuel can ignite and cause serious injury or death and damage. To prevent this, complete the following inspection with the engine stopped. • Fuel is very flammable liquid. If fuel spills or leaks from the pressurized fuel system, it will cause serious injury or death and facility breakage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”, while referring to the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before performing work on the fuel system, discharge static electricity by touching the vehicle body. Caution • Disconnecting/connecting the quick release connector without cleaning it may possibly cause damage to the fuel pipe and quick release connector. Always clean the quick release connector joint area before disconnecting/connecting using cloth or soft brush, and make sure that it is free of foreign material. 1. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 3. Disconnect the quick release connector as shown in the figure. (See QUICK RELEASE CONNECTOR REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 4. Turn the lever of the SST parallel to the hose as shown in the figure. 5. Insert the SST quick release connector into the fuel pipe until a click is heard. 6. Verify that the quick release connector is firmly connected by pulling it by hand. 7. Start the fuel pump using the following procedure. Using M-MDS 1. Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. 3. Using the simulation function “FP”, start the fuel pump. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC TEST [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Without using M-MDS 1. Remove the fuel pump relay. Caution • Short the specified terminals because shorting the wrong terminal of the relay and fuse block may cause malfunctions. 2. Using a jumper wire, short fuel pump relay terminals C and D in the relay and fuse block. 3. Connect the negative battery cable and operate the fuel pump. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 8. Operate the fuel pump for 10 s . 9. Measure the fuel line pressure. • If not within the specification, inspect the following: If it less than the specification: ― Fuel pump unit ― Fuel line for restriction or leakage If it exceeds the specification: ― Fuel line restriction Fuel pressure 425—505 kPa {4.34—5.14 kgf/cm 2 , 61.7—73.2 psi} 10. Stop the fuel pump using the following procedure. Using M-MDS 1. Using the simulation function “FP”, stop the fuel pump. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC TEST [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Without using M-MDS 1. Disconnect the negative battery cable to stop the fuel pump. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 11. Measure the fuel hold pressure after 5 min . • If not within the specification, inspect the following: ― Fuel line leakage Fuel hold pressure 250 kPa {2.55 kgf/cm 2 , 36.3 psi} or more 12. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 13. Disconnect the SST . 14. Connect the quick release connector. (See QUICK RELEASE CONNECTOR REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 15. Complete the “AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .)

High Pressure Fuel Pipe Removal Note Caution • When removing the high pressure fuel pipe, the end of the high pressure fuel pipe may be damaged because the clearance between the high pressure fuel pump and the high pressure fuel pipe is small. The high pressure fuel pipe and fuel distributor must be replaced if they are damaged. Always remove the high pressure fuel pipe before removing the high pressure fuel pump. 1. Remove the high pressure fuel pipe. Rear Housing Removal Note 1. Remove the vacuum pump. (See VACUUM PUMP REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Remove the rear housing. When installing the high pressure fuel pipe to the high pressure fuel pump, be very careful while handling the end of the high pressure fuel pipe. • If parts are exposed to fuel, their function may be decreased or a fire may occur. Always wipe off any leaked fuel using a clean rag. • Do not let foreign materials enter into the high pressure fuel pipe. • Install a new high pressure fuel pipe because it cannot be reused. 1. Temporarily tighten the nuts on both ends. 2. Temporarily tighten the high pressure fuel pipe bracket installation bolt. 3. Tighten the nuts on both ends. High pressure fuel pipe tightening torque 24—35 N·m {2.5—3.5 kgf·m, 18—25 ft·lbf} 4. Tighten the high pressure fuel pipe bracket installation bolt. High pressure fuel pipe bracket installation bolt tightening torque 8—11 N·m {82—112 kgf·cm, 71—97 in·lbf} Fuel Leakage Inspection After High Pressure Fuel Pump Installation 1. Verify that the high pressure fuel pump is assembled securely. 2. Verify that there is no fuel leakage around the high pressure fuel pump.

Warning • Fuel is very flammable liquid. If fuel spills or leaks from the pressurized fuel system, it will cause serious injury or death and facility breakage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”, while referring to the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before draining fuel, make sure to discharge static electricity by touching the vehicle body. Caution • Disconnecting/connecting the quick release connector without cleaning it may cause damage to the fuel pipe and quick release connector. Always clean the quick release connector joint area before disconnecting/connecting using a cloth or soft brush, and make sure that it is free of foreign material. Quick Release Connector Position Removal 1. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Move the retainer upward using a small flathead screwdriver or a similar tool. 3. Pull out the fuel hose straight from the fuel pipe and disconnect it. 4. Cover the disconnected quick release connector and fuel pipe with vinyl sheeting or a similar material to prevent it from getting scratched or dirty. Installation Note • If the quick release connector O-ring is damaged or has slipped, replace the fuel hose. • A checker tab is integrated with the quick release connector for new fuel hoses. Remove the checker tab from the quick release connector after the connector is completely engaged with the fuel pipe. 1. Inspect the fuel hose and fuel pipe sealing surface for damage and deformation. • If there is any malfunction, replace it with a new one. 2. Apply a small amount of clean engine oil to the sealing surface of the fuel pipe. 3. Install the quick release connector. • Insert the fuel pipe straight to the end of the quick release connector. • Push down the retainer using a finger. ― If the retainer cannot be pushed down, push the fuel pipe further to the quick release connector. 4. Lightly pull and push the quick release connector a few times by hand, and then verify that it is connected securely. 5. Complete the “AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .)

Warning • Fuel is highly flammable and dangerous. Fuel line spills and leakage can cause serious injury or death, and damage to equipment. If fuel comes into contact with the skin and eyes it will cause irritation. To prevent this, perform the following inspections with the engine stopped. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before performing work on the fuel system, discharge static electricity by touching the vehicle body. Fuel Leakage Inspection Using M-MDS 1. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. 2. Switch the ignition to ON (engine off). 3. Using the simulation function “FP”, start the fuel pump. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC TEST [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 4. Verify that there is no fuel leakage from the serviced parts. Standard There shall be no leakage after 5 min. 5. In the case of fuel leakage, replace the following components and then recheck using the fuel leakage checking procedure. • If there is leakage, replace the fuel hoses and clips. • If there is damage on the seal on the fuel pipe side, replace the fuel pipe. Without using M-MDS 1. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Remove the fuel pump relay. Caution • Short the specified terminals because shorting the wrong terminal of the relay and fuse block may cause malfunctions. 3. Using a jumper wire, short fuel pump relay terminals C and D in the relay and fuse block. 4. Connect the negative cable and operate the fuel pump. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 5. Verify that there is no fuel leakage from the serviced parts. Standard There shall be no leakage after 5 min. 6. In the case of fuel leakage, replace the following components and then recheck using the fuel leakage checking procedure. • If there is leakage, replace the fuel hoses and clips. • If there is damage on the seal on the fuel pipe side, replace the fuel pipe.

Warning • Fuel vapor is hazardous. It can very easily ignite, causing serious injury and damage. Always keep sparks and flames away from fuel. • Fuel line spills and leakage from the pressurized fuel system are dangerous. Fuel can ignite and cause serious injury or death and damage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before performing work on the fuel system, discharge static electricity by touching the vehicle body. Caution • If foreign matter enters the fuel passage, it could cause serious damage to the fuel injection related parts. When removing/installing the fuel injection related parts, pay close attention so that foreign matter does not enter the fuel passage. Fuel Line Safety Procedure 1. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Remove the fuel-filler cap to release the pressure inside the fuel tank. 3. Remove the fuel pump relay. 4. Disconnect the high pressure fuel pump connector. 5. Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 6. Start the engine. 7. After engine stall, crank the engine 2 to 3 times repeatedly and verify that the engine idling condition is not maintained. (to relieve pressure in fuel pipe) 8. Switch the ignition to off. 9. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 10. Install the fuel pump relay. 11. Connect the high pressure fuel pump connector.

Warning • Fuel is very flammable liquid. If fuel spills or leaks from the pressurized fuel system, it will cause serious injury or death and facility breakage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”, while referring to the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before draining fuel, make sure to discharge static electricity by touching the vehicle body. Note • The rollover valve built into the fuel tank, and the check valve integrated with the rollover valve are inspected in this inspection. 1. Level the vehicle. 2. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 3. Drain the fuel. (See FUEL DRAINING PROCEDURE [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 4. Remove the fuel tank and fuel pump unit as a single unit. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] ) 5. Perform the following procedure to verify fuel tank airtightness. (1) Plug the fuel pump unit pipe, and ports B and C. (2) Apply pressure of 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} to port A and wait for a while. (3) Verify that there is no change in the pressure and no air leakage from the fuel tank. • If there is air leakage, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 6. Remove the port C plug. 7. Place the fuel tank in a level position. 8. Close port A and apply 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} of pressure to port C, and leave it in this condition momentarily. 9. Open port A and verify that the pressure decreases from 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} . • If it cannot be verified, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 10. Close port A and apply -2.0 kPa {-15 mmHg, -0.59 inHg} vacuum to port C, and leave it in this condition momentarily. 11. Open port A and verify that the -2.0 kPa {-15 mmHg, -0.59 inHg} negative pressure condition restores to near positive pressure. • If it cannot be verified, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 12. Turn the fuel tank upside down. 13. Apply pressure of 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} to port A and wait for a while. 14. Verify that there is no change in the pressure and no air leakage from the port C. • If there is air leakage, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .)

Warning • Fuel is very flammable liquid. If fuel spills or leaks from the pressurized fuel system, it will cause serious injury or death and facility breakage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”, while referring to the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Fuel Siphoning Procedure Using Fuel Pump Caution • Disconnecting/connecting the quick release connector without cleaning it may possibly cause damage to the fuel pipe and quick release connector. Always clean the quick release connector joint area before disconnecting/connecting using cloth or soft brush, and make sure that it is free of foreign material. 1. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Disconnect the quick release connector as shown in the figure. (See QUICK RELEASE CONNECTOR REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 3. Connect a long hose to the disconnected quick release connector and drain the fuel into a container used for collecting gasoline. 4. Drain the fuel from the fuel tank using the following procedure: Caution • The fuel pump could be damaged if it is operated while there is no fuel in the fuel tank. Verify the amount of fuel being discharged from the hose and stop operation of the fuel pump when essentially no fuel is being discharged. Using M-MDS 1. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. 2. Using the simulation function “FP”, start the fuel pump. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC TEST [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) ― If the fuel pump cannot be operated, remove the fuel using the procedure in the reference. (See Fuel Siphoning Procedure Not Using Fuel Pump .) Without using M-MDS 1. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Remove the fuel pump relay. Caution • Short the specified terminals because shorting the wrong terminal of the relay and fuse block may cause malfunctions. 3. Using a jumper wire, short fuel pump relay terminals C and D in the relay and fuse block. 4. Connect the negative battery cable and operate the fuel pump. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) ― If the fuel pump cannot be operated, remove the fuel using the procedure in the reference. (See Fuel Siphoning Procedure Not Using Fuel Pump .) 5. Stop the fuel pump using the following procedure. Using M-MDS 1. Using the simulation function “FP”, stop the fuel pump. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC TEST [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) Without using M-MDS 1. Remove the jumper wire to stop the fuel pump. 2. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) Fuel Siphoning Procedure Not Using Fuel Pump 1. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 2. Perform the following procedure (1) to (3) if the fuel gauge value is 3/4 or more. If the fuel gauge value is 3/4 or less, go to Step 3. Caution • If an excessive length of hose is inserted into the fuel-filler pipe, the hose will push the non-return valve and the hose may enter the fuel tank. If the hose enters the fuel tank, the hose may get stuck on the non-return valve when the hose is pulled and the non-return valve could be damaged. Do not insert the hose more than the specified length. Note • When removing the hose from the fuel-filler opening, use a rag to prevent fuel spatter. • Cut the tip of the hose diagonally so that it can be inserted into the fuel-filler pipe smoothly. • When inserting the hose into the fuel-filler pipe, the hose may get stuck. In such cases, rotate the hose so that the hose can be inserted easily. • The pump siphons all the fuel that leaked out of the non-return valve and was trapped in the joint hose, then it suctions the air. After siphoning the fuel, wait several seconds until the air is suctioned out, then resume siphoning. 1. Cut the tip of the hose diagonally and place a mark at the position of the specified hose insertion length. Hose insertion length (specified value) 1240 mm {48.82 in} Hose type (reference) Oil-resistant plastic hose of 10 mm {0.4 in} outer diam. × 6 mm {0.2 in} inner diam. or equivalent 2. Insert the hose from the fuel-filler opening by rotating it to the marked position. 3. Using a pump, siphon the fuel until the fuel gauge value reaches 3/4 or less . 3. Remove the fuel pump unit. (See FUEL PUMP UNIT REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) 4. Drain the fuel. 5. Remove the hose using a rag.

Purpose, Function • The fuel injectors inject fuel in the cylinder over a wide area, intake air and fuel are mixed efficiently, and the optimum air-fuel mix are formulated according to the driving conditions. Construction • The fuel injectors are located on the cylinder heads. • Solenoid-type injectors have been adopted for the fuel injectors. Operation Fuel injection mechanism • Fuel is injected by opening/closing the control valve based on the ON/OFF signal from the PCM. The fuel injection time is determined by the energization time for the solenoid. The injection times can be controlled by intermittently energizing the solenoid. Before injection (while injection stopped) ― Because the control valve is pressed down when there is no energization to the solenoid, the passage sending fuel from the intermediate space is closed.Because the pressurized fuel sent from the injection pipe fills the control space, and pressure for pressing down the nozzle is applied, fuel injection is not performed. Injection starts (nozzle rises) ― When energization to the solenoid starts, the control valve is pulled up and fuel in the control space passes through the OUT orifice and flows out. When the fuel flows out, the pressure of the control space decreases, the nozzle is pressed up, and fuel injection is started. Injection stops (nozzle lowers) ― When energization to the solenoid stops, the control valve is pressed down, the pressure in the intermediate space increases, and the control plate is pressed down. The IN orifice is opened by the lowering of the control plate, and the high pressure fuel flows into the control space. The nozzle is closed instantaneously by increasing the pressure in the control space and the fuel injection is stopped. • For the fuel injection control, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM. (See FUEL INJECTION AMOUNT CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) (See MULTIPLE FUEL INJECTION CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) (See FUEL INJECTION TIMING CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) Purpose, Outline • The common rail fuel injection system stores fuel pressurized by the supply pump in the common rail and injects the fuel into each cylinder using the fuel injectors based on the control by the PCM. ― Fuel is atomized by the extremely high fuel injection pressure, and the generation of particulate matter is reduced by the dissipation of unburnt fuel. ― There is a high degree of flexibility in the fuel injection amount, fuel injection timing and fuel injection pattern, and NOx/PM is reduced by controlling the fuel conditions according to the conditions. Purpose, Function • The fuel filter removes foreign matter and dirt in the fuel. Construction • The fuel filter is installed between the fuel tank and the supply pump and it is located next to fuel tank. • The fuel filter consists of the fuel warmer and the cartridge.

Purpose, Function • If fuel for the summer season is used in the winter season, the wax component in the fuel may become greasy when the temperature is cold. After the engine is started, the fuel warmer melts the greasy wax component to prevent a clogging in the fuel filter. Construction • The fuel warmer is located in the fuel filter. • Consists of the thermistor switch and fuel warmer. Operation • When the temperature in the fuel passage is approx. -2 °C {28 °F} or less, the thermistor switch turns on and power is supplied to the fuel warmer heater. The greasy wax component is heated and melted by the fuel warmer heater. When the temperature inside the fuel passage returns to approx. 5 °C {41 °F} or more, the thermistor switch is turned off and the power to the fuel warmer heater is cut.

Purpose, Function • The common rail stores high pressure fuel from the supply pump and distributes it to the fuel injectors. Construction • The common rail is located on the intake manifold. • The common rail has an integrated fuel pressure relief valve and fuel pressure sensor. Fuel pressure relief valve • The fuel pressure relief valve discharges fuel and decreases fuel pressure to control the pressure in the common rail at the target value. For details on the fuel pressure relief valve, refer to the FUEL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE. (See FUEL PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) Fuel pressure sensor • The fuel pressure sensor detects the fuel pressure in the common rail. For details on the fuel pressure sensor, refer to the FUEL PRESSURE SENSOR. (See FUEL PRESSURE SENSOR [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Purpose, Function • An electronically controlled supply pump has been adopted for the supply pump which pumps high compression fuel to the common rail using low drive torque. Construction • The supply pump is located on the engine (rear). Operation • Fuel supplied by the feed pump built in the supply pump passes the suction control valve which controls the intake amount. The fuel is then sent to the high pressure chamber formed by the TDC of the plunger and passes through the intake valve. • When the plunger approaches TDC of the high compression chamber, the fuel sent to the high pressure chamber is passed through a compression pipe and sent to the delivery valve, supplying pressure to the common rail. • The outer cam is driven eccentrically by the rotation of the camshaft to produce the reciprocating movement of the cam ring. The exterior surface of the outer ring rubs against the plunger and they move together in a reciprocating motion.

Purpose, Function • By controlling the supply pump intake amount, the suction control valve controls the pressure pump feed amount and the pressure inside the fuel distribution pipe. Construction • The suction control valve is located in the supply pump. • The suction control valve consists of the valve, valve body, and armature. Operation • The solenoid drive current is duty controlled and the intake amount is adjusted by the change in the valve opening angle. When the solenoid drive current is small, the intake volume increases, and when it is large the intake volume decreases. De-energized (open) • The solenoid inner port is opened and fuel is sent into the control chamber. • The port in the valve opens and sends fuel to the high pressure chamber. Energized (closed) • The solenoid inner port is closed. Purpose, Function • The fuel pressure relief valve discharges fuel to control the pressure in the common rail at the target value. Construction • The fuel pressure relief valve is located in the common rail. • The fuel pressure relief valve consists of the spring, ball, and push rod. Operation • The coil is energized and the push rod is operated to open the fuel passage according to the control signal from the PCM. • The fuel passage opens and the pressure in the common rail flows to the lower case side. Warning • Fuel is very flammable liquid. If fuel spills or leaks from the pressurized fuel system, it will cause serious injury or death and facility breakage. Fuel can also irritate skin and eyes. To prevent this, always complete the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure”, while referring to the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. Caution • Disconnecting/connecting the quick release connector without cleaning it may cause damage to the fuel pipe and quick release connector. Always clean the quick release connector joint area before disconnecting/connecting using a cloth or soft brush, and make sure that it is free of foreign material. Quick Release Connector Position Removal 1. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 2. Move the retainer upward using a small flathead screwdriver or a similar tool. 3. Pull out the fuel hose straight from the fuel pipe and disconnect it. 4. Cover the disconnected quick release connector and fuel pipe with vinyl sheeting or a similar material to prevent it from getting scratched or dirty. Installation Note • If the quick release connector O-ring is damaged or has slipped, replace the fuel hose. 1. Inspect the fuel hose and fuel pipe sealing surface for damage and deformation. • If there is any malfunction, replace it with a new one. 2. Install the quick release connector. • Insert the fuel pipe straight to the end of the quick release connector. • Push down the retainer using a finger. ― If the retainer cannot be pushed down, push the fuel pipe further to the quick release connector. 3. Lightly pull and push the quick release connector a few times by hand, and then verify that it is connected securely. 4. Complete the "AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION". (See AFTER SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Warning • Fuel is highly flammable and dangerous. Fuel line spills and leakage can cause serious injury or death, and damage to equipment. If fuel comes into contact with the skin and eyes it will cause irritation. Always complete the “Fuel Hose Installation Procedure” when installing the fuel hose. (See Fuel Hose Installation Procedure .) • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before servicing the fuel system, make sure to discharge static electricity by touching a vehicle. Fuel line air bleeding 1. Verify that the fuel hose which has been serviced is connected securely. Caution • Prolonged cranking may damage the battery and the starter. To prevent this, continuously crank the engine for only a maximum of 10 s. 2. Crank the engine until it starts. • If the engine starts, verify that it does not stop during a period of 20 to 30 seconds. ― If the engine does not stop, the procedure is completed. ― If the engine stops, go to the next step. • If the engine does not start, go to the next step. Note • If the fuel filter is replaced with a new one, air will penetrate the fuel system because the fuel is syphoned through the filter paper in the filter. As a result, fuel is not supplied normally, and even if the engine starts, it will stop afterwards. In this case, cranking the engine several times (approx. 10 s intervals) will restore normal fuel supply and the engine can be started. 3. Wait for 20 s . Caution • Prolonged cranking may damage the battery and the starter. To prevent this, continuously crank the engine for only a maximum of 10 s. 4. Crank the engine until it starts. • If the engine starts, the procedure is completed. • If the engine does not start, go to the next step. 5. Remove the blind cap. 6. Install the vacuum pump, container, and the transparent hose as shown in the figure. 7. Drain fuel until the air is bled out. 8. Remove the vacuum pump and install the blind cap. (See Blind Cap Installation Note .) Caution • Prolonged cranking may damage the battery and the starter. To prevent this, continuously crank the engine for only a maximum of 10 s. 9. Crank the engine until it starts. • If the engine starts, the procedure is completed. • If the engine does not start, return to Step 5. Fuel Hose Installation Procedure 1. When connecting the fuel hose and fuel pipe, verify that there is no damage or deformity on the fuel pipe and no cracking on the fuel hose. 2. When installing the fuel hose, verify the main and return sides and install it to the specified position. Blind Cap Installation Note 1. Install the blind cap as shown in the figure.

Warning • Always keep sparks and flames away from fuel. Fuel can be easily ignited which could cause serious injury or death, and damage to equipment • Fuel line spills and leakage from the pressurized fuel system are dangerous. Fuel can ignite and cause serious injury or death, and damage to property and facilities. Fuel can also irritate the skin and eyes. To prevent this, always execute the following line safety procedure. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before servicing the fuel system, make sure to discharge static electricity by touching a vehicle. Caution • If foreign matter enters the fuel passage, it could cause serious damage to the fuel injection related parts. When removing/installing the fuel injection related parts, pay close attention so that foreign matter does not enter the fuel passage. Note • When the engine is stopped, fuel in the fuel system is pressurized. Fuel line safety procedure 1. To prevent fuel spatter and leakage of the fuel system, perform the following procedure: (1) Remove the fuel-filler cap to decrease the pressure between the supply pump (low pressure side) and the fuel tank. (2) Cover the disconnection area of the fuel hose with a cloth and slowly disconnect it. (3) Plug the hose after disconnection. 2. If any servicing between the supply pump and the fuel injector (high pressure side) is performed, perform the following procedure. Note • The pressure between the supply pump and the fuel injector (high pressure side) can be released by loosening one of the injection pipe nuts. (1) Cover the injection pipe nut with a cloth when disconnecting the injection pipe. (2) Slowly loosen the injection pipe nut until the fuel pressure is released completely to decrease the pressure between supply pump and the fuel injector (high pressure side).

Warning • Fuel is highly flammable and dangerous. Fuel line spills and leakage can cause serious injury or death, and damage to equipment. If fuel comes into contact with the skin and eyes it will cause irritation. To prevent this, always perform the “Fuel Line Safety Procedure” referring to the “BEFORE REPAIR PROCEDURE”. • A person charged with static electricity could cause a fire or explosion, resulting in death or serious injury. Before draining fuel, make sure to discharge static electricity by touching a vehicle. Note • The rollover valve built into the fuel tank, and the check valve integrated with the rollover valve are inspected in this inspection. 1. Level the vehicle. 2. Complete the “BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION”. (See BEFORE SERVICE PRECAUTION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 3. Drain the fuel. (See FUEL DRAINING PROCEDURE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 4. Remove the fuel tank and the fuel gauge sender unit as a single unit. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 5. Perform the following procedure to verify fuel tank airtightness. (1) Plug the fuel gauge sender unit pipe, and ports B and C. (2) Apply pressure of 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} to port A and wait for a while. (3) Verify that there is no change in the pressure and no air leakage from the fuel tank. • If there is air leakage, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 6. Remove the port C plug 7. Place the fuel tank in a level position. 8. Close port A and apply 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} of pressure to port C, and leave it in this condition momentarily. 9. Open port A and verify that the pressure decreases from 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} . • If it cannot be verified, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 10. Close port A and apply -2.0 kPa {-15 mmHg, -0.59 inHg} vacuum to port C, and leave it in this condition momentarily. 11. Open port A and verify that the -2.0 kPa {-15 mmHg, -0.59 inHg} negative pressure condition restores to near positive pressure. • If it cannot be verified, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 12. Turn the fuel tank upside down. 13. Apply pressure of 5.9 kPa {44 mmHg, 1.7 inHg} to port A and wait for a while. 14. Verify that there is no change in the pressure and no air leakage from the port C. • If there is air leakage, replace the fuel tank. (See FUEL TANK REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

(See COMMON RAIL REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Purpose, Function • The main silencer reduces exhaust noise. Construction • The main silencer is located at the rear of the vehicle, under the trunk compartment. • The main silencer consists of the filter, stuffing, stuffing holder and set plate.

SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-1 exhaust system) Purpose, function • The exhaust manifold suppresses noise and vibration by gathering exhaust gas from each cylinder and sending it to the exhaust pipe. Construction • The exhaust manifold is located behind the engine. In addition, it is integrated with the catalytic converter (WU-TWC). SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-2-1 exhaust system) Purpose, function • By lengthening the exhaust passage, the transmission of exhaust pressure waves to other cylinders can be delayed, therefore the amount of exhaust gas forced back into the combustion chamber is reduced. By reducing the residual gas, the temperature inside the combustion chamber is lowered and the occurrence of knocking is suppressed even at a high compression ratio. Construction • The exhaust manifold is installed to the rear of the engine. In addition, the catalytic converter (WU-TWC) is integrated (WU-TWC). Residual gas occurrence mechanism 1. When exhaust gas is exhausted from the cylinder, a pressure wave occurs inside the exhaust pipe. 2. The pressure wave reaches each cylinder and the high-temperature exhaust gas in the exhaust manifold is pushed back into the cylinder, which is in overlap. 3. The exhaust valve closes and the exhaust gas pushed back into the cylinder remains in the cylinder (Residual gas increases the temperature inside the cylinder and causes engine knocking). Advantages of 4-2-1 exhaust pipes • Suppresses engine knocking by reducing the residual gas and preventing the temperature inside the cylinder from increasing. A high compression ratio has been realized by suppressing engine knocking. • With conventional short exhaust pipes, the pressure wave which occurs during the exhaust stroke of the No. 3 cylinder reaches the No.1 cylinder, which is in overlap. Because the exhaust valve of the No.1 cylinder is open while in overlap, high-temperature exhaust gas in the exhaust manifold is pushed back into the No.1 cylinder. With the 4-2-1 exhaust pipes, because the length of the pipes is long, it takes time for the pressure wave to reach each cylinder. When the pressure wave occurring from the No.3 cylinder reaches the No.1 cylinder, the exhaust valve has already been closed, therefore the amount of exhaust gas which is pushed backed at almost all engine speeds is reduced.

Outline SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-1 exhaust system) • By integrating the exhaust manifold and the catalytic converter (WU-TWC), the distance from the combustion chamber to the catalytic converter has been shortened. Because the high temperature exhaust gas passes the catalytic converter, early activation of the catalytic converter improves exhaust gas purification. SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-2-1 exhaust system) • A high compression ratio has been realized by adopting 4-2-1 exhaust pipes and reducing residual gas in the cylinders. • The loop structure of the exhaust pipes for the 4-2-1 system takes up less space. Purpose, Function • The purge solenoid valve introduces evaporative gas absorbed by the charcoal canister to the intake manifold. • The purge solenoid valve opens according to the control signal from the PCM. Construction • The purge solenoid valve is located in the engine compartment. • The purge solenoid valve consists of a coil, spring, and plunger. Operation • According to the control signal from the PCM, the coil is energized and the plunger is operated to open/close the purge solenoid valve. • When the purge solenoid valve is open, evaporative gas flows from the charcoal canister to the intake manifold side. Purge solenoid valve open/closed view • For evaporative purge control details, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See PURGE CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) Fail-safe • Function not equipped.

Purpose, Function • The fuel-filler cap releases evaporative gas from the fuel tank if there is a malfunction in the evaporative gas passage between the fuel tank and the intake manifold. As a result, deformation of the fuel tank caused by evaporative gas pressure is prevented. Construction • The fuel-filler cap is located on the fuel-filler opening. • The fuel-filler cap consists of a valves, retainer, and springs. Operation • When there is positive pressure in the fuel tank due to evaporative gas, evaporative gas is released into the atmosphere. When there is negative pressure, air is introduced to the fuel tank.

Purpose, Function • The charcoal canister absorbs the evaporative gas generated inside the fuel tank to prevent release of the gas into the atmosphere. Construction • The charcoal canister is located near the fuel tank. • The charcoal canister has activated charcoal to absorb evaporative gas. Operation • When the purge solenoid valve is open, evaporative gas, which is absorbed by the activated charcoal, is released by the intake manifold vacuum and the gas flows to the intake manifold.

Purpose, Function • The rollover valve prevents fuel flow into the evaporative gas passage during sudden cornering or vehicle rollover. Construction • The rollover valve is built into the fuel tank. • The rollover valve consists of a float, O-ring and spring. Operation • The rollover valve utilizes a combination of float weight, spring force, and buoyancy. When the float is immersed in the fuel, the float (valve) closes to block the sealing surface of the passage.

Purpose, Function • The PCV valve prevents release of blow-by gas (unburnt gas) into the atmosphere. • The PCV valve is open/closed by the intake manifold vacuum. Construction • The PCV valve is located on the oil separator. • The PCV valve consists of a spring and valve. Operation • When the valve is pulled by the intake manifold vacuum, blow-by gas flows to the intake manifold. • The blow-by gas flow amount is determined by the balance of the intake manifold vacuum and the spring force.

Purpose, Function • The catch tank suppresses pulsation occurring before evaporative gas is inducted into the intake manifold. Construction • The catch tank is located in the engine compartment. Operation • When evaporative gas flows from the charcoal canister to the purge solenoid valve, pulsation is suppressed by passing the evaporative gas through the hollowing of the catch tank.

Purpose, Function • The check valve adjusts and maintains the pressure in the fuel tank at a constant pressure. Construction • The check valve is built into the rollover valve. Operation • The valve moves in response to the difference in air pressure between the fuel tank side and the atmospheric side, thereby changing the path of airflow. • When the pressure in the fuel tank becomes negative due to fuel consumption or other factors, the path opens, drawing atmospheric air into the fuel tank.

Purpose, Function • The catalytic converter purifies contaminants in the exhaust gas by utilizing the chemical reactions of the three-way catalytic converter. • A WU-TWC and a TWC have been adopted. Construction WU-TWC • The catalytic converter (WU-TWC) is located behind the engine. SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-1 exhaust system) SKYACTIV-G 1.5 (with 4-2-1 exhaust system) • The WU-TWC is integrated with the exhaust manifold. TWC • The catalytic converter (TWC) is located behind the catalytic converter (WU-TWC). Operation • Contaminants in the exhaust gas (HC, CO, NOx) are purified by oxidization and deoxidization while they are passing through the catalytic converter. ― Oxidization process • Noxious hydrocarbon (HC) and carbon monoxide (CO) are bound with oxygen and converted to non-noxious carbon dioxide and water. O 2 +HC+CO→CO 2 +H 2 O ― Deoxidization process • Noxious nitrogen oxide (NOx) is converted to non-noxious nitrogen and oxygen. A part of the oxygen generated in this process is used in the oxidization process. NOx→N 2 +O 2

Purpose, Function • Releases evaporative gas from the fuel tank if there is a malfunction in the evaporative gas passage between the fuel tank and the intake manifold. Construction • The fuel-filler cap is located on the fuel-filler opening. • The fuel-filler cap consists of valves, retainer, and springs. Purpose, Function • The rollover valve prevents fuel flow into the evaporative gas passage during sudden cornering or vehicle rollover. Construction • The rollover valve is built into the fuel tank. • The rollover valve consists of a float, O-ring and spring. Operation • The rollover valve utilizes a combination of float weight, spring force, and buoyancy. When the float is immersed in the fuel, the float (valve) closes to block the sealing surface of the passage.

Purpose, Function • The evaporative chamber prevents water penetrating the atmospheric air inlet. Construction • The evaporative chamber is located on the rollover valve. Operation • There partitions protect the fuel tank by preventing flooding as atmospheric air enters from the airflow holes.

Purpose, Outline • The catalytic converter recirculates the exhaust gas in the combustion chamber and lowers the combustion temperature. By recirculating the exhaust gas, the NOx generated largely when the combustion temperature is high is reduced. • The HP-EGR system *1 and LP-EGR system *2 are used concurrently to perform optimum control according to the engine operation conditions. *1 :The HP-EGR system circulates/recirculates exhaust gas in the intake manifold prior to it passing the turbine of the variable geometry turbocharger. Because the exhaust gas is recirculated immediately, responsiveness to the necessity of nitrous oxide concentration adjustment and the temperature increasing ability during engine warm-up are excellent. *2 :The LP-EGR system sends/recirculates exhaust gas to the variable geometry turbocharger inlet after it passes the variable geometry turbocharger turbine. Because the intake air and exhaust gas are charged together, even high volumes in the charge region of the exhaust gas can be recirculated. System diagram Structure • The exhaust gas recirculation system consists of the following parts: Part, system name Reference HP-EGR control valve Intake shutter valve (See INTAKE SHUTTER VALVE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) HP-EGR control valve (See HP-EGR CONTROL VALVE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) LP-EGR control valve Exhaust shutter valve (See EXHAUST SHUTTER VALVE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) LP-EGR control valve (See LP-EGR CONTROL VALVE [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) EGR cooler (See EGR COOLER [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) Operation • The exhaust gas recirculation system operates the HP-EGR and LP-EGR systems according to the engine load. Ignition switched off (IG-OFF) • The open/closed condition of each valve when the ignition is switched off is as follows. HP-EGR system ― HP-EGR control valve: Fully closed ― Intake shutter valve: Fully open LP-EGR system ― LP-EGR control valve: Fully closed ― Exhaust shutter valve: Fully open Light engine load • During light engine loads (except during diesel particulate filter regeneration), exhaust gas is recirculated by the HP-EGR system according to the request flow amount from the PCM to promote engine warming and assure responsiveness. • The open/closed condition of each valve during light engine loads is as follows. HP-EGR system ― HP-EGR control valve: Open (duty control) ― Intake shutter valve: Closed (duty control) LP-EGR system ― LP-EGR control valve: Fully closed ― Exhaust shutter valve: Fully open Medium engine load • During medium engine loads (except during diesel particulate filter regeneration), exhaust gas is recirculated by both the LP-EGR and HP-EGR systems according to the request flow amount from the PCM. • The open/closed condition of each valve during medium engine loads is as follows. HP-EGR system ― HP-EGR control valve: Open (duty control) ― Intake shutter valve: Open (duty control) LP-EGR system ― LP-EGR control valve: Open (duty control) ― Exhaust shutter valve: Closed (duty control) High engine load • During high engine loads (except during diesel particulate filter regeneration), the exhaust gas is recirculated by the LP-EGR system according to the request flow amount from the PCM to promote charging. • The open/closed condition of each valve during high engine loads is as follows. HP-EGR system ― HP-EGR control valve: Fully closed ― Intake shutter valve: Fully open LP-EGR system ― LP-EGR control valve: Open (duty control) ― Exhaust shutter valve: Open (duty control) During diesel particulate filter regeneration • During diesel particulate filter regeneration, exhaust gas is recirculated by both the LP-EGR systems according to the request flow amount from the PCM. • The open/closed condition of each valve during diesel particulate filter regeneration is as follows. HP-EGR system ― HP-EGR control valve: Fully closed (constantly) ― Intake shutter valve: Open (duty control) (during light engine load/medium engine load) *1 LP-EGR system ― LP-EGR control valve: Open (duty control) (during light engine load/medium engine load) *2 ― Exhaust shutter valve: Fully open (constantly) *1 :During high engine loads, the intake shutter valve is fully open due to the large amount of air volume required. *2 :Because the exhaust gas temperature is high during compulsory diesel particulate filter regeneration or under high engine load conditions, the LP-EGR control valve is fully closed to prevent combustion difficulties caused by the exhaust gas being recirculated. • For details on the exhaust gas recirculation system, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM. (See EGR CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) (See INTAKE SHUTTER VALVE CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) (See EXHAUST SHUTTER VALVE CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Purpose, Function • The EGR cooler cools the exhaust gas recirculated to the variable geometry turbocharger. • By cooling the recirculated exhaust gas, a greater amount of exhaust gas can be recirculated due to the reduced volume. As a result, the combustion temperature of the exhaust gas recirculated to the combustion chamber is suppressed, and the NOx generated largely when the combustion temperature is high is reduced. Construction • The EGR cooler is located at the rear of the engine compartment. • The EGR cooler consists of the exhaust gas recirculation passage and engine coolant passage. • The EGR cooler has an integrated filter.

Purpose, Function • The EGR pipe is the passage for recirculating the exhaust gas to the intake air side. Construction HP-EGR control valve side • The EGR pipe is located between the intake manifold and HP-EGR control valve. LP-EGR control valve side • The EGR pipe is located between the variable geometry turbocharger and the LP-EGR control valve. • The end of the pipe has holes (slits) to facilitate mixing of the exhaust gas and intake air.

Purpose, Function • The check valve adjusts and maintains the pressure in the fuel tank at a constant pressure. Construction • The check valve is built into the rollover valve. Operation • The valve moves in response to the difference in air pressure between the fuel tank side and the atmospheric side, thereby changing the path of airflow. • When the pressure in the fuel tank becomes negative due to fuel consumption or other factors, the path opens, drawing atmospheric air into the fuel tank.

Purpose, Function • The diesel particulate filter collects and removes particulate matter (PM) in the exhaust gas. Construction • The DPF is integrated inside the catalytic converter (DPF). Operation • Diesel particulate filter is a silicon carbide honey-comb type filter. The filter ends are blocked in sequence and small holes on the wall inside the filter collect PM, and the collected PM is burned and eliminated. (See DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER REGENERATION CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Purpose, Function • The intake shutter valve facilitates recirculation induction of the exhaust gas by adjusting the intake air volume and channeling the airflow to the intake manifold side. • The intake air amount to the engine is reduced to increase the exhaust gas temperature easily while the DPF is carrying out combustion. Due to this, the particulate matter (PM) collected in the DPF is burned and eliminated. • The valve is closed to cut the intake air when the engine switch is off to reduce the shock when the engine is turned off. Construction • The intake shutter valve is located on intake manifold. • The intake shutter valve consists of the shutter valve, valve shaft, valve, spring, valve gear, mid gear, DC motor, and pinion. • The intake shutter valve has an integrated intake shutter valve position sensor. For details on the intake shutter valve position sensor, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM. (See INTAKE SHUTTER VALVE POSITION SENSOR [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) Operation • The intake shutter valve is opened to the valve opening angle according to the energization current flowing to the DC motor from the PCM. • The intake shutter valve performs coordinated control with the LP-EGR control valve, HP-EGR control valve, and exhaust shutter valve. For details on the exhaust shutter valve, refer to the CONTROL SYSTEM. (See INTAKE SHUTTER VALVE CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) • If the shutter valve has a malfunction and the DC motor control is disabled, the shutter valve is opened to the fully open position by the return spring. As a result, the air amount necessary to keep the vehicle moving is assured. Purpose, Function • The catalytic converter (oxidation catalyst) utilizes chemical reactions to purify contaminants in the exhaust gas. Construction • The catalytic converter is located behind the engine. Operation • The catalytic converter (oxidation catalyst) converts the noxious carbon monoxide and hydrocarbon in the exhaust gas to non-noxious carbon dioxide and water. Oxidization process O 2 + HC + CO = CO 2 + H 2 O • For details on the catalytic converter (oxidation catalyst), refer to the DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER. (See DIESEL PARTICULATE FILTER [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Generator current inspection Note • Since the charging current decreases rapidly after starting the engine, carry out the following procedure quickly, and read the maximum current value. 1. Verify that the battery is fully charged. (See BATTERY INSPECTION .) 2. Verify that the assembly condition of the drive belt is normal. (See DRIVE BELT INSPECTION [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) 3. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 6. Turn off all electrical loads. 7. Start the engine. In this case, cool down the generator and recheck. 8. Step Action 1 Switch the ignition ON (engine off). 2 Shift the selector lever to the N position. (ATX) Shift the shift lever to the neutral position. Battery Condition Initial setting (i-stop setting) Procedure Caution • If the engine is started with the bonnet open, the i-stop function will not operate until the engine is restarted with the bonnet closed (not system malfunction). If the engine is started with the bonnet open, close the bonnet and restart the engine after the ignition is switched off once. • If a vehicle with an i-stop non-operation condition is brought in, the malfunction will not be resolved by simply performing the battery condition initial setting (i-stop setting). Verify the PID “BATT_SOC” value and if the value is less than 75%, recharge the battery. (See BATTERY RECHARGING .) • If the “BATT_SOC” value has not been verified before disconnecting the negative battery cable, perform battery condition initial setting (i-stop setting) after performing the battery inspection. • The “BATT_SOC” value is displayed “0%” because the battery charge condition is not stabilized after connecting the negative battery cable (it is necessary to leave battery undisturbed for approx. 6 to 48 h to stabilize battery charge condition). • If the negative battery cable is disconnected, specific information stored in the PCM will be erased. Therefore, perform the following procedure after reconnecting. Battery Condition Initial setting (i-stop setting) flow (SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5) Purpose Step Procedure Caution/Note Prior verification of PCM and battery condition 1 Verify the value (BATT_SOC) measured before disconnecting the negative battery cable. When BATT_SOC value is 75% or more. • Go to the next step. When BATT_SOC value is not verified or the value is less than 75% • Perform battery inspection. (See BATTERY INSPECTION .) — 2 Verify that 5 min or more have elapsed since the negative battery cable was disconnected. Caution • It is necessary to leave the battery undisturbed for 5 min or more because the voltage is not stabilized, depending on the battery usage condition, and the PCM cannot determine the “BATT_SOC” value correctly. 3 Disconnect the current sensor connector. If the current sensor connector has already been disconnected, go to the next step. — Battery condition verification /completion verification 4 Connect the negative battery cable and wait for 10 s or more. Caution • negative battery cable terminal tightening torque: 4.0—6.0 N·m {41—61 kgf·cm, 36—53 in·lbf} Note • Connect the negative battery cable before connecting the current sensor connector. If the current sensor connector is connected first, the PCM may mistakenly recognize a signal from the current sensor and learn the battery condition incorrectly. 5 Connect the current sensor connector. — 6 Switch the ignition ON (engine off) and wait for 15 s or more (within 1 min.). — 7 Vehicles with i-ELOOP • Display the DC-DC converter (i-ELOOP) voltage reduction circuit operation status (PID: CONV_STAT) using the M-MDS data monitor function. (See PID/DATA MONITOR INSPECTION [i-ELOOP] .) Power Output (Normal) is displayed ― Go to the next step. Other than Power Output (Normal) is displayed ― Charge the capacitor. (See CAPACITOR (i-ELOOP) RECHARGING [i-ELOOP] .) Note • To enable i-stop operation, it is necessary to return the i-ELOOP operation conditions to normal. 8 VERIFY i-stop INDICATOR LIGHT (GREEN) AND i-stop WARNING LIGHT (AMBER) FLASHING CONDITION • Press the i-stop OFF switch for 10 s and verify the flashing condition of the i-stop indicator light (green) and i-stop warning light (amber). When i-stop indicator light (green) flashes ― Go to the next step. When i-stop warning light (amber) flashes ― Perform the battery inspection. (See BATTERY INSPECTION .) When i-stop warning light (amber) illuminates ― Procedure is performed incorrectly. Switch the ignition off and repeat the procedure from Step 1 (Prior verification of PCM and battery condition). Note • When the i-stop OFF switch is pressed, the illumination condition of the i-stop warning light (amber) changes to flashing of either the i-stop indicator light (green) or the i-stop warning light (amber). 9 Switch the ignition off. — ISC learning 10 Close the bonnet. Note • If the engine is not warmed up completely the ISC learning will not finish. ― Warm-up is not completed even if the low engine coolant temperature indicator light (blue) turns off. As a guide, apply pressure to the radiator hose and if the radiator has warmed up, engine warming is complete. 11 Start the engine. 12 Warm up the engine completely with no electrical load. Steering angle sensor initialization setting 13 Turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock. Note • The steering wheel angle is set to the initial value by disconnecting the negative battery cable. 14 Switch the ignition off. ISC learning verification 15 Perform the following procedure within 25 s. 1. Switch the ignition ON (engine off) and within 5 s, long-press the i-stop OFF switch for 3 s or more. Purpose, Function • The generator operates by obtaining drive force from the engine via the drive belt and generates the required electricity for electronic devices. Construction • The generator is located on the left front side of the engine. • Output control is performed by the PCM resulting in the elimination of the IC regulator and the simplification of the construction. • Two delta connection type stator coils have been adopted. • The two stator coils form the circuit having a phase difference, and magnetic pull, which operates between the rotor and stator coil by the phase difference, is theoretically eliminated. Due to this, electromagnetic vibration and generator operation noise (electromagnetic noise) have been reduced. • Pulsation occurring through voltage rectifying using two stator coils having a phase difference is minimized and stable voltage output is supplied. Operation • For generator control details, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See GENERATOR CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) This is due to current flowing to the starter motor through the pull-in coil to turn the starter motor, and does not indicate an abnormality. 1. Verify that the starter motor pinion is extended while battery positive voltage is connected to terminal S and the starter body is grounded. • If the starter motor pinion is not extended, repair or replace the starter. Return test 1. Disconnect the motor wire from terminal M. 2. Connect battery positive voltage to terminal M and ground the starter body. 3. Pull out the drive pinion with a screwdriver. Verify that it returns to its original position when released. • If it does not return, repair or replace the starter. Pinion Gap Inspection (Without i-stop) 1. Pull out the drive pinion with the battery positive voltage connected to terminal S and the starter body grounded. Caution • Applying power for more than 10 s can damage the starter. Do not apply power for more than 10 s. 2. Measure the pinion gap while the drive pinion is extended. • If not as specified, adjust with an adjustment washer (between drive housing front cover and magnetic switch). Verify that there is no continuity between the commutator and the core at each segment using a ohmmeter. • If there is continuity, replace the armature. 2. Verify that there is no continuity between the commutator and the shaft using a ohmmeter. • If there is continuity, replace the armature. 3. Place the armature on V-blocks, and measure the runout using a dial indicator. • If not within specification, replace the armature. Starter armature runout 0.1 mm {0.004 in} max. 4. Measure the commutator diameter. • If not within the minimum specification, replace the armature. Starter commutator diameter Standard: 29.4 mm {1.16 in} Minimum: 28.8 mm {1.13 in} 5. Measure the segment groove depth of the commutator. • If not within the minimum specification, undercut the grooves to the standard depth. Segment groove depth of starter commutator Standard: 0.5 mm {0.02 in} Minimum: 0.2 mm {0.008 in} Magnetic switch 1. Inspect for continuity between terminals S and M using a ohmmeter. • If there is no continuity, replace the magnetic switch. 2. Inspect for continuity between terminal S and the body using a ohmmeter. • If there is no continuity, replace the magnetic switch. 3. Verify that there is no continuity between terminals M and B using a ohmmeter. • If there is continuity, replace the magnetic switch. Brush and brush holder 1. Verify that there is no continuity between each insulated brush and plate using a ohmmeter. • If there is continuity, replace the brush holder. 2. Measure the brush length. • If any brush is worn almost to or beyond the minimum specification, replace all of the brushes. Starter brush length Standard: 12.3 mm {0.484 in} Minimum: 5.5 mm {0.22 in} 3. Measure the brush spring force using a spring balance. • If not within the minimum specification, replace the brush and brush holder component. Purpose, Function • The starter rotates the crankshaft via the ring gear of the dual-mass flywheel (MTX)/drive plate (ATX) and it serves as a trigger to start the engine. Construction • The starter is located on the left rear side of the engine. • The starter is a coaxial reduction type which can obtain high torque. Operation • For starter cut-off control details, refer to CONTROL SYSTEM. (See STARTER CUT-OFF CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • The starter relay operates by the signal from the start stop unit and the PCM control, and it supplies battery power to the starter. Construction • The starter relay is located on the relay and fuse block. Operation • The signal from the start stop unit is sent to the starter relay. When a ground is established in the PCM circuit by the PCM control, electric current flows to the coil, the contact point is drawn by the generated electromagnetic force, and it switches on. When the contact point switches on, battery power is supplied to the starter. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • The starter interlock switch mechanism prevents vehicle surge when the engine is started, enhancing safety. The engine cannot be started unless the clutch is depressed. Construction • The starter interlock switch is located on the clutch pedal. Operation • The starter interlock switch rod is pressed by the depression of the clutch pedal. At this time, the starter interlock switch is turned on, and by establishing a circuit, engine starting (from starter) permission is transmitted to the PCM and start stop unit. Fail-safe DTC No. Fail-safe function P176E:00 • Inhibits engine-stop by operating the i-stop function.

Outline • Enables driving at a constant speed by setting the vehicle speed with the cruise control switch instead of operating the accelerator pedal. • The PCM controls the throttle valve actuator to maintain the vehicle at a constant speed. Component and function Component Function DSC HU/CM (CAN communication: Vehicle speed signal) The vehicle speed signal is sent to the PCM from the DSC HU/CM. Cruise control switch ON The cruise control system main switch. The cruise control system goes on standby with the operation of the switch. OFF The cruise control system main switch. The cruise control system is turned off with the operation of the switch. SET (+) • If the switch is pressed when the vehicle speed exceeds 25 km/h {16 mph} with the system on standby, the vehicle speed at the point when the switch is pressed is stored in the PCM and the system initiates the cruise control. • The PCM controls acceleration by the pressing of the switch or when the switch is continuously pressed during cruise control. SET (−) • If the switch is pressed when the vehicle speed exceeds 25 km/h {16 mph} with the system on standby, the vehicle speed at the point when the switch is pressed is stored in the PCM and the system initiates the cruise control. • The PCM controls deceleration by the pressing of the switch or when the switch is continuously pressed during cruise control. RESUME If the switch is pressed when the vehicle speed exceeds 25 km/h {16 mph} with the system on standby and the previous pre-set vehicle speed is stored in the PCM, the system initiates the cruise control so that the vehicle speed is the pre-set vehicle speed stored in the PCM. CANCEL If the switch is pressed during cruise control, the cruise control system goes on standby (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). Brake switch Depressing the brake pedal during cruise control switches the cruise control system to standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). CPP switch (MTX) Depressing the clutch pedal during cruise control switches the cruise control system to standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). Neutral switch No.1 (MTX) Shifting to neutral during cruise control switches the cruise control system to standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). TCM (ATX) (CAN communication: gear signal) If the following operation is performed during cruise control, the cruise control system goes on standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). • The selector lever is shifted from D position to N position. DSC HU/CM (CAN communication: Brake pressure) If the brake pressure exceeds 0.3 MPa {3 kgf/cm 2 , 44 psi} , the cruise control system goes on standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). Parking brake switch If the parking brake is applied, the cruise control system goes on standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). TCM (ATX) (CAN communication: diagnostic signal) If there is a malfunction with the ATX, the cruise control system goes on standby mode (pre-set vehicle speed is stored). PCM The cruise control system is executed or stopped according to the cruise control switch signals. The throttle valve actuator is operated so that the vehicle speed is the pre-set vehicle speed during cruise control. Throttle valve actuator The duty signal sent from the PCM adjusts the throttle valve opening angle. Outline • The drive selection system can switch the vehicle’s drive mode. • When the sport mode is selected, the drive force response corresponding to the accelerator pedal operation is enhanced. Function • The sport mode can be selected/canceled by operating the drive selection switch. Block Diagram Operation When sports mode is selected 1. When the sports mode is selected using the drive selection switch (1), the instrument cluster sends a drive selection signal to the TCM and the PCM via CAN communication (2). At the same time, it turns the select mode indicator light on (3). 2. When the PCM sends a drive selection signal to the TCM, the TCM will change the shift points. (4) 3. When the PCM receives the drive selection signal, it switches the control corresponding to the accelerator opening angle (5). Drive selection switch inhibition conditions • If any of the following conditions is met, the mode is not switched even if the drive selection switch is operated. ― During sudden maneuvering ― During DSC control ― During ABS control • If the drive selection switch has been operated with a drive selection switching inhibition condition being met, the PCM sends a sport light flash request signal to the instrument cluster. • The instrument cluster flashes the sport lamp to notify the driver that drive selection is currently prohibited. Drive selection stop conditions • If any of the following conditions is met while in sport mode, the drive mode is canceled. ― Ignition is switched off ― During cruise control operation ― Malfunction with PCM control-related part

The instrument cluster detects the sports mode selection condition based on the open/close of contact switches SW1 and SW2 of the drive selection switch. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Construction • Instrument cluster with built-in select mode indicator light have been adopted. Operation 1. The instrument cluster receives (1) the select mode indicator light illumination/flashing request signal via CAN communication from the PCM. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) intermittently for the select mode indicator light flash request signal. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) continuously for the select mode indicator light llumination request signal. 4. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the select mode indicator light flashes (3). 5. When the transistor is turned on continuously, the select mode indicator light illuminates (3).
