Description The seat warmer does not warm up even if the seat warmer switch is turned on. Possible Causes • Seat warmer switch malfunction • Seat warmer control unit power supply circuit malfunction ― Short to ground in wiring harness between SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal O ― Short to ground in wiring harness between SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal M ― Open circuit in wiring harness between SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal O ― Open circuit in wiring harness between SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal M ― SEAT WARM 20 A fuse malfunction ― Short to ground in wiring harness between C/U IG1 15 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal A ― Open circuit in wiring harness between C/U IG1 15 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal A ― C/U IG1 15 A fuse malfunction • Open circuit in wiring harness between the following terminals: ― Seat warmer control unit terminal L and body ground • Malfunction in wiring harness between seat warmer control unit and indicator unit terminal I ― Short to ground in wiring harness between seat warmer control unit terminal J and indicator unit terminal D ― Open circuit in wiring harness between seat warmer control unit terminal J and indicator unit terminal D • Indicator unit malfunction • Seat warmer unit malfunction • Seat warmer control unit malfunction • Connector poor contact or terminal damage Diagnostic Procedure Step Inspection Action 1 DETERMINE MALFUNCTION SYMPTOM • Operate the seat warmer switches on the driver and passenger sides to turn on the seat warmer system for the driver and passenger sides. • Does a malfunction occur with the seat warmer system on both sides? Yes Go to Step 8. No Go to the next step. 2 INSPECT SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT CONNECTOR AND SEAT WARMER UNIT CONNECTOR • Switch the ignition OFF (LOCK). • Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) • Disconnect the seat warmer control unit connector and the seat warmer unit connector on the side which does not operate. • Inspect the connector engagement and connection condition, and inspect the terminals for damage, deformation, corrosion, or disconnection. • Is the connector normal? Yes Go to the next step. No Repair or replace the connector, then go to Step 11. 3 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT POWER SUPPLY CIRCUIT • Verify that the seat warmer control unit connector is disconnected. • Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) • Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). • Measure the voltage at the following terminals (vehicle wiring harness side). ― Seat warmer control unit terminal O ― Seat warmer control unit terminal M • Is the voltage B+ ? Yes Go to the next step. No Inspect the SEAT WARM 20 A fuse. If the fuse is blown: • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common wiring harness between the following terminals. ― SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal O ― SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal M If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for short to ground to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which is shorted to ground. • Replace the fuse. If the fuse is damaged: • Replace the fuse. If the fuse is normal: • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common wiring harness between the following terminals. ― SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal O ― SEAT WARM 20 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal M If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for an open circuit to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has an open circuit. Go to Step 11. 4 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT POWER SUPPLY CIRCUIT • Verify that the seat warmer control unit connector is disconnected. • Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) • Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). • Measure the voltage at the following terminals (vehicle wiring harness side). ― Seat warmer control unit terminal A • Is the voltage B+ ? Yes Go to the next step. No Inspect the C/U IG1 15 A fuse. If the fuse is blown: • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common wiring harness between the following terminals. ― C/U IG1 15 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal A If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for short to ground to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which is shorted to ground. • Replace the fuse. If the fuse is damaged: • Replace the fuse. If the fuse is normal: • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common wiring harness between the following terminals. ― C/U IG1 15 A fuse and seat warmer control unit terminal A If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for an open circuit to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has an open circuit. Go to Step 11. 5 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS OPEN CIRCUIT IN WIRING HARNESS BETWEEN SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT AND BODY GROUND • Switch the ignition OFF (LOCK). • Verify that the seat warmer control unit connector is disconnected. • Inspect for continuity between the following terminals (vehicle wiring harness side) and body ground. ― Seat warmer control unit terminal L • Is there continuity? Yes Go to the next step. No • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common connector between the following terminals and body ground. ― Seat warmer control unit terminal L If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for an open circuit to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has an open circuit. • Go to Step 11. 6 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS SHORT CIRCUIT TO GROUND IN WIRING HARNESS BETWEEN SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT AND INDICATOR UNIT • Verify that the seat warmer control unit connector is disconnected. • Disconnect the indicator unit connector. • Inspect for continuity between seat warmer control unit terminal J (vehicle wiring harness side) and body ground. • Is there continuity? Yes • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common connector between seat warmer control unit terminal J and indicator unit terminal D. If there is a common connector: ― Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for short to ground to determine the malfunctioning location. ― Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: ― Repair or replace the wiring harness which is shorted to ground. • Go to Step 11. No Go to the next step. 7 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS OPEN CIRCUIT IN WIRING HARNESS BETWEEN SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT AND INDICATOR UNIT • Verify that the seat warmer control unit connector and the indicator unit connector are disconnected. • Inspect the wiring harness for continuity between seat warmer control unit terminal J and indicator unit terminal D (vehicle wiring harness side). • Is there continuity? Yes Go to the next step. No • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify if there is a common connector between seat warmer control unit terminal J and indicator unit terminal D. If there is a common connector: ― Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for an open circuit to determine the malfunctioning location. ― Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: ― Repair or replace the wiring harness which has an open circuit. • Go to Step 11. 8 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS SEAT WARMER UNIT • Inspect the seat warmer unit on the side which has a malfunction. (See SEAT WARMER UNIT INSPECTION .) • Is the seat warmer unit normal? Yes Go to the next step. No Replace the seat warmer unit (front seat cushion pad or front seat back pad) which has a malfunction, then go to Step 11. (See FRONT SEAT BACK TRIM REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (See FRONT SEAT CUSHION TRIM REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 9 DETERMINE IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS INDICATOR UNIT • Inspect the indicator unit. (See INDICATOR UNIT INSPECTION .) • Is the indicator unit normal? Yes Go to the next step. No Replace the indicator unit, then go to Step 11. (See INDICATOR UNIT REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 10 DETERMINE IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT • Reconnect all the disconnected connectors. • Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) • Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). • Operate the seat warmer switch to turn on the seat warmer system. • Does the seat warmer system operate normally? Yes Go to the next step. No Replace the seat warmer control unit, then go to the next step. (See SEAT WARMER CONTROL UNIT REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 11 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS CORRECTED • Operate the seat warmer switch to turn on the seat warmer system. • Does the seat warmer system operate normally? Yes Troubleshooting completed. (Explain the contents of the servicing to the customer.) No Verify the malfunction symptom in the symptom troubleshooting chart and perform the other applicable malfunction diagnosis. (See SYMPTOM TROUBLESHOOTING [SEAT WARMER SYSTEM] .)

Possible Causes • Parking sensor control module power supply malfunction With i-stop system ― Open circuit in wiring harness between IGNITION relay and parking sensor control module terminal W ― Short to ground in wiring harness between IGNITION relay and parking sensor control module terminal W Without i-stop system ― Open circuit in wiring harness between IG1 relay and parking sensor control module terminal W ― Short to ground in wiring harness between IG1 relay and parking sensor control module terminal W ― C/U IG1 15 A fuse damage, burnt out • Malfunction in parking sensor control module ground ― Open circuit in wiring harness between parking sensor control module terminal A and body ground ― Ground point lifting or loosening • Volume adjustment of buzzer is at minimum • Buzzer circuit malfunction ― Open or short circuit in wiring harness between parking sensor control module terminal R and parking sensor buzzer terminal B ― Open or short circuit in wiring harness between parking sensor control module terminal T and parking sensor buzzer terminal A • R position (ATX)/reverse position (MTX) signal malfunction ― Open or short circuit in wiring harness between parking sensor control module terminal N and electrical supply unit (ESU) terminal 2Q • Parking sensor buzzer malfunction • Parking sensor control module malfunction • Customer misunderstanding Diagnostic Procedure Step Inspection Action 1 VERIFY IF MALFUNCTION CAUSE IS OTHER THAN OPERATION PERMISSION CONDITION • Verify the parking sensor system operation by an obstruction approaching the ultrasonic sensor/corner ultrasonic sensor with all the following conditions met. ― Ignition switched ON (engine on) ― Selector lever is in R position (ATX) ― Shift lever is in reverse position (MTX) ― Vehicle speed 10 km/h or less • Does the parking sensor system operate correctly? Yes System is normal. (Explain the parking sensor system operation conditions to the customer.) No Go to the next step. 2 INSPECT PARKING SENSOR CONTROL MODULE POWER SUPPLY • Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). • Measure the voltage at parking sensor control module terminal W. • Is the voltage B+? Yes Go to the next step. No With i-stop • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify whether or not there is a mid-connector between IGNITION relay terminal C and parking sensor control module terminal W. If there is a mid-connector ― Determine the malfunctioning part by inspecting the mid-connector and the terminal for corrosion, damage, or pin disconnection, and the mid-wiring harness for a open circuit or short to ground. ― Repair or replace the wiring harness which has a malfunction. If there is no mid-connector ― Repair or replace the wiring harness which has a malfunction. Without i-stop • Inspect the C/U IG1 15 A fuse. If the fuse is burned out: • Inspect and repair the wiring harness between the C/U IG1 15 A fuse and parking sensor control module terminal W for a short circuit to the ground system. If the fuse is not damaged or burned out: • Refer to the wiring diagram and verify whether or not there is a mid-connector between IG relay terminal C and parking sensor control module terminal W. If there is a mid-connector • Determine the malfunctioning part by inspecting the mid-connector and the terminal for corrosion, damage, or pin disconnection, and the mid-wiring harness for a open circuit. • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has a malfunction. If there is no mid-connector • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has a malfunction. 3 ADJUST BUZZER VOLUME • Adjust the buzzer volume. Structural View

Purpose • The following structures have been adopted to absorb impact efficiently in the event of a collision and to suppress cabin deformation. ― Straight structure which achieves both high strength and weight reduction ― Multi-load path structure which assures a high level of collision absorption ― Ring structure which enhances overall rigidity • A cross-shaped sectional front bumper reinforcement crush can and front side frames have been adopted which effectively absorb impact energy during a frontal collision and suppress cabin deformation. Structural View Construction Straight structure • The straight-shape frames create a continuous configuration from the front to the rear. Multi-load path structure • Impact energy in a collision is dispersed in multiple directions and absorbed effectively. • To disperse and absorb frontal impact energy at the engine compartment, the following three paths have been established at the vehicle front (front frame). Upper path ― The upper path disperses and absorbs frontal impact energy from the front frame to A-pillar. Mid path ― The mid path disperses and absorbs frontal impact energy from the front frame to the side body and floor. Lower path ― Not only the body parts, the front crossmember is also used to absorb impact energy. The lower path disperses and abosrbs frontal impact energy from the front frame to B frame. Cross sectional shape • Even using a steel plate of the same thickness, the strength can be enhanced by increasing the number of ridges. By utilizing this characteristic, the cross-section of the front bumper reinforcement crush can and front side frames is cross-shaped, achieving both high impact energy absorption and weight reduction. Ring structure • Overall body rigidity has been improved using four ring structures created by the upper body including the roof rail and B-pillar combined with the underbody reinforcements. • Cabin deformation in a collision is suppressed by creating a ring structure. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • The bonnet has slits to reduce injury to pedestrians in a collision. Construction • By adopting slits to the bonnet inner, rigidity between the slits is lowered and the bonnet crushes easily when impact is applied. The bonnet crushes and absorbs impact to pedestrians in a collision. • By positioning the bonnet stiffener reinforcement at the front of the bonnet inner, impact to a pedestrian during a collision is absorbed preventing the pedestrian from contacting the bonnet striker and body. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • A front fender bracket with a shock-absorbing structure has been adopted to reduce impact to pedestrians in a collision. Function • If a pedestrian contacts the bonnet or the front fender in a collision, the front fender bracket deforms to reduce impact to the pedestrian. Construction • The front fender bracket is located under the front fender panel. • The front/back vertical wall of the front fender bracket each contain a hole which causes the bracket to deform easily in a collision with a pedestrian. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • A bumper stiffener lower has been adopted to reduce injury to a pedestrian's legs caused by the pedestrian's legs going under the vehicle in a collision. Function • The bumper stiffener lower prevents the pedestrian from going under the vehicle in a collision by lifting the pedestrian's legs toward the vehicle front side so that the pedestrian falls on the bonnet. Note • The bumper stiffener lower has optimal rigidity so that the deformation amount in a collision is small. Compared to the small deformation amount of the bumper stiffener lower, the deformation amount of the vehicle upper part such as the front bumper and bonnet is large so that the pedestrian falls on the bonnet in a collision. • The bumper stiffener lower is located under the front bumper so that the wind-flow while the vehicle is moving flows to the condenser and radiator. Construction • The bumper stiffener lower is located under the front bumper. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The pedestrian protection is for reducing impact and injury to pedestrians in a collision with the vehicle. Construction Head protection • An impact energy absorbing structure has been adopted for the following parts to reduce impact to pedestrians in a collision. ― Bonnet ― Cowl grille ― Front fender bracket ― Front fender junction • The impact energy absorbing structure of each part reduces impact to the pedestrian's head. • A clearance has been assured between the bonnet and the engine so that the bonnet can deform. Bonnet • The bonnet has an impact energy absorbing structure so that impact to pedestrians can be reduced in a collision. For details, refer to the [BONNET]. (See BONNET .) Cowl grille • The cowl grille has an impact energy absorbing structure so that impact to pedestrians can be reduced in a collision. For details, refer to [COWL GRILLE]. (See COWL GRILLE .) Front fender bracket • The front fender bracket has an impact energy absorbing structure so that impact to pedestrians can be reduced in a collision. For details, refer to [FRONT FENDER BRACKET]. (See FRONT FENDER BRACKET .) Front fender junction • The front fender junction has an impact energy absorbing structure so that impact to pedestrians can be reduced in a collision. For details, refer to [FRONT FENDER JUNCTION]. (See FRONT FENDER JUNCTION .) Leg protection • The following parts have been adopted to the vehicle frontal area to reduce injury to a pedestrian's legs. ― Energy-absorbing foam ― Bumper stiffener lower Energy-absorbing foam • The energy-absorbing foam is equipped to the front of the front bumper reinforcement to reduce impact to a pedestrian's legs. For details, refer to [ENERGY-ABSORBING FOAM]. (See ENERGY-ABSORBING FORM .) Bumper stiffener lower • The bumper stiffener lower reduces injury to a pedestrian's legs caused by the pedestrian's legs going under the vehicle. For details, refer to [BUMPER STIFFENER LOWER]. (See BUMPER STIFFENER LOWER .)

Purpose, Function • An energy-absorbing foam has been adopted to prevent a pedestrian from contacting the high-rigidity front bumper reinforcement in a collision. Construction • The energy-absorbing foam is located in front of the front bumper reinforcement. • If the vehicle hits a pedestrian, air holes and the hollowed area of the foaming agent are crushed thus the energy-absorbing foam functions as a cushion. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • A front fender junction with a shock-absorbing structure has been adopted to reduce impact to pedestrians in a collision. Function • If a pedestrian contacts the bonnet or the front fender in a collision, the front fender junction deforms to reduce impact energy. Construction • The front fender junction is located under the front fender panel. • The front/back vertical wall of the front fender junction each contains a hole which causes the bracket to deform easily in a collision with a pedestrian. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • A door beltline reinforcement and side impact bars have been adopted to prevent the doors from intruding into the cabin in a side collision. Construction • Waveform (double-hat shape cross section) shape has been adopted to the following side impact bars: Front door ― Side impact bar lower Rear door ― Side impact bar lower • By adopting the waveform (double-hat shape cross section) side impact bars, strength can be assured even with thinner steel plates, achieving both high rigidity and weight reduction. • For the door beltline reinforcement of the front door, an optimal cross-sectional shape has been adopted which satisfies both mass and strength, and achieves weight reduction. • The door beltline reinforcement and side impact bars disperse the impact during a side collision. • Intrusion of a front door during a side collision is suppressed by positioning the door beltline reinforcement and lower side impact bars of the front door so that they overlap the hinge pillar and center pillar. • Intrusion of a rear door during a side collision is suppressed by positioning the lower side impact bars of the rear door so that they overlap the center pillar and side sill. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The switch turns on/off in conjunction with the user's power window subswitch operation and switches the power window open/close circuit contact point. Function • The power window subswitch switches the contact point according to the switch operation and switches the circuit to the power window motor. Construction • The power window subswitch is located on the front passenger's side and rear side. Operation (Example: close operation) • When the power window subswitch is operated for close operation, the close-side contact point is on. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The door glass opens/closes electrically when the power window main switch or the power window subswitch is operated. Function Manual open/manual close function • When the power window main switch or subswitch is operated for manual operation, the front door glass/rear door glass performs manual open/manual close operation. Auto open/auto close function • When the power window main switch is operated for auto operation, the driver's side front door glass performs auto open/auto close operation. IG OFF timer function • The driver's side power window can be operated using the power window main switch for approx. 40 s after the ignition is switched from ON (engine on or off) to ACC or OFF. Auto reverse pinch protection function • If an obstruction by a foreign object is detected during the auto close operation, the operation changes from close to open. Fully-closed position record function • The power window control module records the fully-closed position of the driver's side front door glass so that the auto reverse pinch protection function does not operate when the driver's side front door glass is fully closed. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Operation of driver's side manual open/close function (Example: manual close operation) 1. When the power window main switch is operated for manual close operation, the manual close switch is switched (1). 2. When the power window control module detects a manual close signal, current flows to the close relay (2) and the close relay turns on (3). 3. When the close relay turns on, the power window motor (driver's side) performs close operation (4). Operation of auto open/close function (Example: auto open operation) 1. When the power window main switch is operated for auto open operation, the auto switch and the manual open switch are switched (1). 2. When the power window control module detects an auto open signal, current flows to the open relay (2) and the open relay turns on (3). 3. When the open relay turns on, the power window motor (driver's side) performs auto open operation (4). Operation of front passenger's side and rear manual open/close function (Example: front passenger's side close operation) 1. When the power window subswitch is operated for close operation, the close switch switches (1). 2. When the close switch is on, the power window motor (passenger's side) performs close operation (2). Operation of IG OFF timer function • When the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to ACC or OFF, the IG OFF timer function of the power window control module is turned on, and the power window main switch can be operated for approx. 40 s after IG OFF is detected. Operation of auto reverse pinch protection function • If the power window control module detects a change in the pulse signal from the power window motor for 0.3 s during auto close operation, it reverses the power window motor operation and opens the door glass approx. 200 mm {7.87 in} . Fully-closed position record function • When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on), and the switch is pulled and held for approx. 2 s after the driver's side door glass is fully closed from the fully opened position, the power window control module records the driver's side door glass position. Note • Performing the following procedures will reset the initial setting and disables auto operation. Re-perform the initial setting. ― Negative battery cable is disconnected ― Power window main switch connector is disconnected ― Power window system power supply fuse is removed

Purpose • Transmits the power window main switch operation of the driver to the power window control module. Function Manual • When the power window main switch is operated for manual open/close operation, it sends a manual open/close signal to the power window control module. Auto • When the power window main switch is operated for auto open/close operation, it sends an auto open/close signal to the power window control module. Power cut • When the power-cut switch is on (contact point: Open), the open/close operation of the front passenger seat and rear seat windows is disabled. Construction • The power window main switch consists of the following parts: ― Driver's side switch ― Passenger's side switch ― Rear side switch (LR) ― Rear side switch (RR) ― Power cut switch Operation Power window main switch operation • Contact points for door glass opening/closing can be changed by operating the power window main switch. Power-cut switch operation • When the power-cut switch of the power window main switch is on (contact point: Open), current from each power window subswitch is interrupted. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The power window motor transmits rotation force to the power window regulator. • The power window motor (driver's side) outputs pulse to the power window control module to input motor operation status. Function The power window motor rotates clockwise/counterclockwise when it receives an open/close signal from the power window main switch or the power window subswitch. Construction • The power window motor consists of the following parts: ― Motor ― Connector ― Gear • The power window motor (driver's side) has two Hall effect switches. ― The Hall effect switches output pulse to the power window control module. Operation Open operation • When the power window motor receives an open signal from the power window main switch or power window subswitch, the motor rotates counterclockwise. Close operation • When the power window motor receives a close signal from the power window main switch or power window subswitch, the motor rotates clockwise. Hall effect switch operation • The Hall effect switch utilizes magnets set on a rotating axis to detect the motor rotation, and outputs one pulse cycle for each rotation of the motor rotation axis. • The high and low pulse points of Hall effect switches 1 and 2 are different during opening and closing because the phase difference shifts by approx. 90° . Fail-safe • When the power window motor is operated continuously for a certain period of time, the power window motor operation is stopped temporarily to protect the power window motor inner circuit.

Purpose • The power window regulator moves the carrier plate up and down to open/close the door glass using the rotation force transmitted from the power window motor. Function • The power window regulator transmits the rotation force from the power window motor to the inner wire and moves the carrier plate up and down. Construction • The inner wire is assembled to the inner side of the regulator guide and wrapped around the drum housing. • The carrier plate is fixed with the inner wire pinched. Operation 1. When the drum housing of the power window regulator receives the rotation force from the power window motor, it rotates in the same rotation direction as the power window motor. 2. When the drum housing rotates, the inner wire is pulled in the direction the drum housing rotates. 3. The carrier plate moves up and down according to the direction the inner wire is pulled. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • Driver can operate the outer mirror remotely using the power outer mirror switch. Function Outer mirror glass adjustment function • Outer mirror glass can be adjusted up/down and left/right electrically by operating the power outer mirror switch. IG OFF timer function • The power outer mirror switch can be operated for approx. 40 s after the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to OFF. Structural View System Wiring Diagram With retractable outer mirror Without retractable outer mirror Operation (With retractable outer mirror) Outer mirror glass adjustment operation (Example: adjusting left outer mirror upward) 1. When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on) or the IG OFF timer function is operating and the upward switch is turned on (1) , the power outer mirror control module turns the transistor on (2). 2. The FET turns on when the transistor turns on and current flows (3). 3. When the FET turns on, the up/down adjustment motor operates upward (4) and the outer mirror operates upward. Outer mirror glass retract/return operation (Example: retracting outer mirrors) 1. When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on) or the IG OFF timer function is operating and the retraction direction switch is turned on (1), the power outer mirror control module turns the transistor on (2). 2. The FET turns on when the transistor turns on and current flows (3). 3. When the FET turns on, the retract/return motor operates in the retracting direction (4) and the outer mirrors retract. IG OFF timer operation • When the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to OFF, the IG OFF timer function inside the power outer mirror control module is turned on and the power outer mirror switch can be operated for approx. 40 s after IG OFF is detected. Operation (Without retractable outer mirror) Outer mirror glass adjustment operation (Example: adjusting left outer mirror upward) • When the upward switch turns on (1), the up/down adjustment motor operates upward (2) and the outer mirror operates upward. IG OFF timer operation • When the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to OFF, the IG OFF timer function inside the power outer mirror control module is turned on and the power outer mirror switch can be operated for approx. 40 s after IG OFF is detected. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The power outer mirror moves the outer mirror glass in the up/down and left/right directions using the up/down adjustment motor and left/right adjustment motor. • The power outer mirror moves the outer mirror in the retract/return directions using the retract/return motor. (with retractable outer mirror) Function • The up/down adjustment motor and left/right adjustment motor turn clockwise (down/right direction) or counterclockwise (up/left direction). • The retract/return motor turns clockwise (retract direction) or counterclockwise (return direction). (With retractable outer mirror) Construction • The up/down adjustment motor and left/right adjustment motor are located on the outer mirror glass. • The retract/return motor is located inside the power outer mirror. (With retractable outer mirror) Operation Up/down adjustment motor (Example: operating outer mirror glass upward) 1. When the motor rotates counterclockwise, the rib projects (1). 2. The rib pushes up the outer mirror glass and the outer mirror glass operates upward (2). Left/right adjustment motor (Example: Operating outer mirror glass in left direction) 1. When the motor rotates counterclockwise, the rib projects (1). 2. The rib pushes up the outer mirror glass and the outer mirror glass operates in the left direction (2). Retract/return motor (Example: retract operation) (with retractable outer mirror) • When the motor rotates clockwise (1), the outer mirror operates in retract direction (2). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The switch turns on/off in conjunction with the driver's switch operation and switches the power outer mirror angle adjustment circuit and retract/return circuit contact points. Function Up-down/left-right adjustment function • The power outer mirror switch switches the contact point according to the switch operation. As a result, the circuit to the up-down/left-right adjustment motor is switched. Left/right selection function • The power outer mirror switch is used to select the side on which adjustment of the power outer mirror glass is desired. Retract/return function (With retractable outer mirror) • The power outer mirror switch switches the contact point according to the switch operation. As a result, the circuit to the retract/return motor is switched. Construction • The power outer mirror switch consists of the following parts. ― Up-down/left-right adjustment switch ― Left/right selection switch ― Retract/return switch (With retractable outer mirror) Operation Ex: Switch is pressed in the upward direction • By operating the power outer mirror switch, up-down/left-right contact points for the power outer mirror can be switched. Ex: Switched from return to retract • By operating the power outer mirror switch, retract/return contact points for the power outer mirror can be switched. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Controls the driver's side power window system based on the power window main switch operation signal and power window motor (driver's side) pulse. • Controls the power outer mirror system based on the power window man switch operation signal. Function • When the power window control module receives a power window main switch operation signal, it turns on/off the open/close relay. • The power window control module detects the power window motor operation status based on the pulse from the power window motor (driver's side). Construction • The power window control module and the power outer mirror control module are built into the power window main switch. Operation Power window control module • The power window control module detects the motor rotation speed and rotation direction based on pulse 1 and 2 from the power window motor (driver's side). Power outer mirror control module • For the power outer mirror control module operation, refer to [POWER OUTER MIRROR SYSTEM]. (See POWER OUTER MIRROR SYSTEM .) Fail-safe • When power window control module detects a pulse (Hall effect switch) error, it switches the power window system to fail-safe mode to prevent incorrect operation. Outline • The rear window defogger and the outer mirror heater remove fogging from the glass surfaces of the rear window glass and the outer mirror glass. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Full-auto air conditioner Manual air conditioner Function • Fogging on the glass surfaces of the rear window glass and the outer mirror glass is removed because the rear window glass and the outer mirror glass are heated by the rear window defogger and outer mirror heater filaments and moisture on the windows is vaporized. • When the rear window defogger and the outer mirror heater have operated for approx. 15 min , the power supply to the rear window defogger relay is stopped by the timer in the BCM and the operation of the rear window defogger and the outer mirror heater is stopped. Construction Rear window defogger • The rear window defogger filaments are positioned on the cabin side of the rear window glass. • The heated outer mirror filament is integrated in the outer mirror glass. Operation Full-auto air conditioner 1. When the rear window defogger switch is turned on with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the climate control unit sends a rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation request signal to the instrument cluster (1) via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster sends the rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation signal to the BCM (2). 3. When the BCM receives the rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation signal, it turns the rear window defogger relay on (3). The rear window defogger timer/outer mirror heater timer operates at the same time the rear window defogger relay turns on. 4. When the rear window defogger relay is turned on, battery voltage is supplied to the rear window defogger and outer mirror heater filaments (4), and the rear window glass and the outer mirror glass are warmed by the heat from the filament. Note • When approx. 15 min have elapsed after the rear window defogger timer/outer mirror heater timer started operation, the BCM turns the rear window defogger relay off and stops the operation of the rear window defogger and the outer mirror heater. Manual air conditioner 1. When the rear window defogger switch is turned on with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the climate control unit sends a rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation request signal to the instrument cluster (1). 2. The instrument cluster sends the rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation signal to the BCM (2). 3. When the BCM receives the rear window defogger/outer mirror heater operation signal, it turns the rear window defogger relay on (3). The rear window defogger timer/outer mirror heater timer operates at the same time the rear window defogger relay turns on. 4. When the rear window defogger relay is turned on, battery voltage is supplied to the rear window defogger and outer mirror heater filaments (4), and the rear window glass and the outer mirror glass are warmed by the heat from the filament. Note • When approx. 15 min have elapsed after the rear window defogger timer/outer mirror heater timer started operation, the BCM turns the rear window defogger relay off and stops the operation of the rear window defogger and the outer mirror heater. Fail-safe • Not applicable

If there is a common connector: • Inspect the common connector and terminals for corrosion, damage, or disconnection and the common wiring harnesses for an open circuit to determine the malfunctioning location. • Repair or replace the malfunctioning location. If there is no common connector: • Repair or replace the wiring harness which has an open circuit. Go to Step 10. 7 INSPECT REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER CIRCUIT FOR SHORT TO GROUND OR OPEN CIRCUIT • Install the rear window defogger relay. • Turn the rear window defogger switch on. • Measure the voltage at rear window defogger terminal 1A (vehicle wiring harness side). • Is the voltage B+? (See REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER REPAIR .) 9 INSPECT BCM CIRCUIT FOR SHORT TO GROUND OR OPEN CIRCUIT • Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). • Measure the voltage at BCM terminal 3K (vehicle wiring harness side). • Is the voltage B+? Purpose • A cabin intrusion is detected. Function • The intruder sensor detects movement in the vehicle by ultrasonic waves and sends the detection signal to the BCM. Construction • The intruder sensor is located in center part of the roof the forward part of the roof. Operation 1. When the theft-deterrent system is stand-by mode, the intruder sensor outputs ultrasonic waves in the passenger compartment. The intruder sensor detects differences in the ultrasonic waves (reflected waves) that are output and bounced off a target object. 2. When a difference in reflected waves occurs by movement in the vehicle (intruder), the CPU calculates the level of difference. 3. If the differences meet certain criteria, the intruder sensor sends a detection signal to the BCM. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Alerts that a door, liftgate, or the bonnet has been opened improperly. Function • The theft-deterrent system activates if a door, the liftgate, or the bonnet is improperly opened. Open Circuit Alert Control Function • If the power or ground lines are cut, the theft-deterrent siren uses the back-up power supply to activate the siren. • If the transmission lines are cut, the theft-deterrent system uses the vehicle's battery power to activate the siren. • If any one of the following conditions are met, the siren is stopped: ― Receives go-to-initial signal from the BCM. Construction • A theft-deterrent siren is located on the inside of the trunk side trim (LH). Operation • The siren beeps when receiving an alert initialization signal from the BCM. When a go-to-initial signal is received the siren is stopped. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The theft-deterrent system operates the theft-deterrent siren or theft-deterrent horn and hazard warning lights if a door, liftgate/trunk lid or the bonnet is improperly opened. • An answer-back function has been adopted which allows visual verification of the theft-deterrent system operation. • Signal input/output of the theft-deterrent system is controlled by the BCM. Structural View With intruder sensor Without intruder sensor System Wiring Diagram With intruder sensor Without intruder sensor Function Answer back function • When a locking operation is performed using the remote transmitter is in stand-by preparation mode, stand-by mode, the hazard warning lights flash once. • When a unlocking operation is performed using the remote transmitter is in initial mode, the hazard warning lights flash twice. Intruder sensor cancel function • An intruder sensor cancel button has been installed on the remote transmitter. If the intruder sensor cancel button is on while the theft-deterrent system is stand-by preparatory mode, intruder sensor ultrasonic wave output is cut, and movement detection is stopped. Operation (With Intruder Sensor) Mode transition • The BCM switches the theft-deterrent system mode based on the ignition switch and door conditions. Operation stop mode • In this mode, all theft-deterrent system operations are stopped. • The system changes to the operation stop mode when any of the following conditions are met. ― Switch the ignition to ACC or ON (engine off). Initial mode • This mode is the preparatory mode before changing to the stand-by mode. The system does not change directly to the alert mode from this mode. Transition condition to the initial mode • The system changes from the operation stop mode to the initial mode if all of the following conditions are met. ― Switch the ignition off • The system transitions from stand-by preparatory mode, stand-by mode, alert mode, and alert preparatory mode to the initial mode if the cancel conditions in each mode are met. Transition condition to the stand-by preparatory mode • The system changes to the stand-by preparatory mode if any of the following conditions are met. ― A lock operation was performed using the remote transmitter lock button with all the doors, liftgate, and bonnet closed. Stand-by preparatory mode • This is mode prior to the stand-by mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the stand-by mode • If the stand-by preparatory mode continues for approx. 20 s , the system changes to the stand-by mode. Cancel conditions • If any of the following conditions are met, the stand-by preparatory mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Any door latch switch on (door is open), or liftgate latch switch on (liftgate is open), or bonnet latch switch off (bonnet is open) ― Any door lock-link switch UNLOCK ― Switch the ignition to ACC or ON (engine off). ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Open the liftgate using the liftgate opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Stand-by mode • The mode monitors for unauthorized door opening/closing approx. 20 s after the doors are locked. If any unauthorized operation is detected, the system changes to alert mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the alert mode • If any of the following conditions are met, the system changes to the alert mode. ― Forced ignition ON or ignition is switched ON without transmitter authorization ― Door latch switch on (door is open) ― Liftgate latch switch on (liftgate is open) ― Bonnet latch switch off (bonnet is open) ― Door lock-link switch UNLOCK ― Intrusion into vehicle is detected by intruder sensor Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the stand-by mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition to ON (engine off), and engine start ― Open the liftgate using the liftgate opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Alert mode • In this mode, the theft-deterrent siren and hazard warning lights are operated to alert the surrounding area. • When the alarm period (approx. 30 s) has elapsed, the system changes to the alert preparatory mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the alert preparatory mode • When the alarm period ( approx. 30 s ) has elapsed, the system changes to the alert preparatory mode. • The alarm period is not extended even if a transition condition to alert mode is met again during an alarm period. Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the alert mode is canceled, and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition to ON (engine off), and engine start ― Open the liftgate using the liftgate opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Alert preparatory mode • In the alert preparatory mode, the theft-deterrent siren and hazard warning light are not operated, however, the alarm triggers immediately if the condition is changed. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to alert mode • The system changes to the alert mode if any of the following conditions are met. ― Forced ignition ON or ignition is switched ON without transmitter authorization ― Door latch switch on (door is open) ― Liftgate latch switch on (liftgate is open) ― Bonnet latch switch off (bonnet is open) ― Door lock-link switch UNLOCK ― Intrusion into vehicle is detected by intruder sensor Transition condition to the stand-by mode • If there is no transition to cancel or alert mode for a period of 5 s after warning stand-by mode is established, the system switches to stand-by mode. Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the alert preparatory mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition ON (engine off), and engine start ― Open the liftgate using the liftgate opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Operation (Without Intruder Sensor) Mode transition • The BCM switches the theft-deterrent system mode based on the ignition switch and door conditions. Operation stop mode • In this mode, all theft-deterrent system operations are stopped. • The system changes to the operation stop mode when any of the following conditions are met. ― Switch the ignition to ACC or ON (engine off). Initial mode • This mode is the preparatory mode before changing to the stand-by mode. The system does not change directly to the alert mode from this mode. Transition condition to the initial mode • The system changes from the operation stop mode to the initial mode if all of the following conditions are met. ― Switch the ignition off • The system transitions from stand-by preparatory mode, stand-by mode, alert mode, and alert preparatory mode to the initial mode if the cancel conditions in each mode are met. Transition condition to the stand-by preparatory mode • The system changes to the stand-by preparatory mode if any of the following conditions are met. ― A lock operation was performed using the remote transmitter lock button or key with all the doors, liftgate/trunk lid, and bonnet closed. Stand-by preparatory mode • This is mode prior to the stand-by mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the stand-by mode • If the stand-by preparatory mode continues for approx. 20 s , the system changes to the stand-by mode. Cancel conditions • If any of the following conditions are met, the stand-by preparation mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Any front door latch switch on (door is open), or any rear door latch switch on (rear door is open), or liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on (liftgate/trunk lid is open), or bonnet latch switch off (bonnet is open) ― Any door lock-link switch UNLOCK ― Switch the ignition to ACC or ON (engine off) ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Open the liftgate/trunk lid using the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Stand-by mode • The system starts monitoring approx. 20 s after the doors are locked for unauthorized door opening/closing. If any unauthorized operation is detected, the system changes to the alert mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the alert mode • If any of the following conditions are met, the system changes to the alert mode. ― Switch the ignition ON (engine off) ― Door latch switch on (door is open) ― Liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on (liftgate/trunk lid is open) ― Bonnet latch switch off (bonnet is open) ― Door lock-link switch UNLOCK ― Unlock operation using front door key cylinder Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the stand-by mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition to ACC or ON (engine off). Alert mode • In this mode, the theft-deterrent horn and hazard warning lights are operated to alert the surrounding area. • When the alarm period ( approx. 30 s ) has elapsed, the system changes to the alert preparatory mode. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to the alert preparatory mode • When the alarm period ( approx. 30 s ) has elapsed, the system changes to the alert preparatory mode. • The alarm period is not extended even if a transition condition to alert mode is met again during an alarm period. Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the alert mode is canceled, and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition ON (engine off), and engine start ― Open the liftgate/trunk lid using the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system) Alert preparatory mode • In the alert preparatory mode, the theft-deterrent horn and hazard warning light are not operated, however, the alarm triggers immediately if the condition is changed. • If the cancel conditions are met, the system changes to the initial mode. Transition condition to alert mode • The system changes to the alert mode if any of the following conditions are met. ― The ignition is switched from ON to off, or from off to ON ― The door latch switch is turned from on (door is open) to off (door is closed), or from off (door is closed) to on (door is open) ― The liftgate/trunk lid latch switch is turned from on (liftgate/trunk lid is open) to off (liftgate/trunk lid is closed), or from off (liftgate/trunk lid is closed) to on (liftgate/trunk lid is open) ― The bonnet latch switch is turned from off (bonnet is open) to on (bonnet is closed) or from on (bonnet is closed) to off (bonnet is open) ― The door lock-link switch is locked from unlock, or unlocked from lock ― The front door key cylinder is locked from unlock, or unlocked from lock Cancel condition • If any of the following conditions are met, the alert preparatory mode is canceled and the system changes to the initial mode. ― Unlock operation using remote transmitter ― Switch the ignition ON, and engine start ― Open the liftgate/trunk lid using the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch (With advanced keyless entry system)

Purpose • Stores the record of the user's operation and the door lock system operation corresponding to the user's operation. Function • The door lock system operation record is stored by the BCM and displayed using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS). • The BCM stores the following when the front/rear door lock actuator operates. ― Time and date ― Part or function which output unlock signal ― Part or function which output lock signal ― Operated actuator ― Vehicle condition Construction • Based on the stored record, the BCM displays the following operation record on the M-MDS screen. Operation • Based on the lock/unlock signal, the BCM sends an operation signal to the front/rear door lock actuator motor, and stores the operation record at the same time. • Because it takes time from when the front/rear door lock actuator motor operates until the lock/unlock is switched, the BCM may store the operation record before the lock/unlock switching is completed. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Transmits the liftgate opener switch operation of the user to the BCM. Function • The liftgate switch on signal is sent to the BCM by operating the liftgate switch. Construction • By locating the liftgate opener switch to the liftgate lower end, the operation for pressing the liftgate opener switch and opening the liftgate can be performed simultaneously. • The shape of the liftgate opener switch allows for uniform application of load using all the fingers of one hand when opening the liftgate. Operation • While the liftgate opener switch is pressed, the switch turns on (contact point: closed). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • By pressing the switch ON/OFF, the push button start notifies the start stop unit of the driver power supply switching operation. Function Push button start indicator light • If the push button start indicator light detects the engine switch condition, a malfunction, or the steering lock cannot be released, it indicates the driver by turning on/flashing the light. START/STOP/ENGINE indicator light • The push button start turns on the characters to improve visibility of the button. Construction • The push button start is located on the meter hood. • Two types of switches are integrated in the push button start. • The push button start has the following integrated indicators. For the illumination/flash condition of the indicator, refer to the [KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM]/[ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] OR [PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM]. (See KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) (See ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) ― ACC indicator ― ON indicator ― Indicator (green) ― Indicator (amber) • The push button start is built into the coil antenna. (See COIL ANTENNA .) Operation • When the push button start is pressed, switches 1 and 2 turn on (contact point: closed), and when released, it turns off (contact point: open). Push button start indicator light Green illumination • Illuminates if the conditions necessary for engine-start are met. Green flashing • Flashes when the steering lock cannot be released. Amber illumination • Turns on when the ignition is switched ON (engine off) or to ACC. Amber flashing • Flashes when a malfunction is detected. START/STOP/ENGINE indicator light • When a door is open/closed, the START/STOP/ENGINE indicator light turns on when the headlights are turned on. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The keyless warning alarm notifies the driver that the presence of the remote transmitter cannot be verified or the steering lock cannot be released. Function • When the instrument cluster receives the keyless warning alarm request signal sent from the start stop unit via CAN communication, the keyless warning alarm sounds. • When any of the following conditions is met, the start stop unit sends a keyless warning alarm request signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. ― Driver's door latch switch on signal (door open) is received with ignition switched to ACC (pattern A) ― Remote transmitter cannot be detected inside vehicle when off signals for all door latch switches (doors closed) are received with ignition not switched OFF (pattern B) ― Steering lock cannot be released (pattern C) • The keyless warning alarm sounds in the pattern shown in the figure. Pattern A Pattern B Pattern C Construction • The keyless warning alarm sounds using the buzzer built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. The start stop unit sends (1) a keyless warning alarm request signal to the instrument cluster. 2. The instrument cluster microcomputer turns the transistor on (2) based on the keyless warning alarm request signal. 3. When the transistor turns on, a ground circuit with the alarm is established and the alarm sounds (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • A liftgate opener system has been adopted in which the liftgate can be opened just by pressing the liftgate opener switch. Function • The BCM operates the liftgate lock actuator and opens the liftgate based on the liftgate opener switch signal. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation • When the BCM detects the liftgate opener switch on signal while the door lock-link switch (driver's side) unlock signal (driver's door lock unlocked) is detected and the theft-deterrent system is not operating with any of the following conditions met, it opens the liftgate. Operation Conditions ― Vehicle speed of 3 km/h {2 mph} or less received ― Ignition switched OFF 1. When the liftgate opener switch is pressed, it turns on (1). 2. When the BCM detects the liftgate opener switch on signal with the liftgate opener system operation conditions met, it sends (2) a liftgate release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU). 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the liftgate release signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the liftgate release relay on (4). 4. When the liftgate release relay turns on, the liftgate lock actuator operates (5). 5. When the liftgate lock actuator operates, the latch lever is released to open the liftgate.

Outline • An advanced keyless entry system has been adopted which performs automatic authorization of the remote transmitter that the customer carries and locking/unlocking of the doors. Function • Remote transmitter authorization is performed if any of the following operations is performed. ― Locking/unlocking using a request switch on an outer handle ― Locking/unlocking using a remote transmitter ― Trunk lid opening using remote transmitter (4SD) ― Opening the liftgate/trunk lid • Each turn light flashes to notify the user that the lock/unlock operation is completed. • The advanced keyless entry system has the following functions in the event that the user operates the system incorrectly or to prevent the user from leaving the vehicle without locking. ― Auto re-lock function: After unlocking, if all doors or the liftgate/trunk lid are not opened and a period of time according to the personalized setting has elapsed, all doors are automatically locked. ― Out-of-area (reception area) type auto lock function * : After closing all doors, when the remote transmitter is brought out of the reception area of the keyless antenna, all doors are automatically locked. ― Remote transmitter pause function: If all doors are locked with a remote transmitter left in the vehicle, the functions of the remote transmitter inside the vehicle are paused. ― Remote transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function: If the liftgate/trunk lid is closed with a remote transmitter left in the vehicle, the liftgate/trunk lid can be opened by pressing the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch. ― Warning function: Warns that there is a malfunction in the advanced keyless entry system or the system is operated incorrectly using any of the following: • Keyless beeper • Keyless warning alarm • KEY warning light (red) * :The initial value for the personalization setting is off. When using the function, turn the personalization setting on. Remote transmitter battery voltage low indication function • This function notifies the driver that the battery voltage of the remote transmitter is low by flashing the KEY indicator light (green). Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Lock/unlock operation using request switch on outer handle Operation Conditions • When the request switch is on with all the following conditions met, lock/unlock operation is performed. ― ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected ― All door latch switch OFF (all doors closed condition) is detected ― Liftgate latch switch OFF (liftgate closed condition) is detected (5HB) *1 ― The remote transmitter is within the reception area outside keyless antenna. *1 :The operation conditions are included depending on the vehicle's period of manufacture. 1. When the driver's or passenger's side request switch is pressed, a request switch on signal is input (1) to the start stop unit via the LF control unit. 2. Based on the request switch on signal, the start stop unit sends (2) a request output signal to the LF control unit to verify that the remote transmitter is inside the reception area. 3. The LF control unit outputs (3) the request signal from the outside keyless antenna of the door in which the request switch was pressed. 4. The remote transmitter receives the request signal from the outside keyless antenna, and sends (4) ID data to the keyless receiver. 5. The keyless receiver transmits (5) the received ID data to the start stop unit. 6. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if it determines a programmed remote transmitter is outside the vehicle, it sends a lock/unlock request signal to the BCM and at the same time, it sends (6) a beeper sound request signal to the LF control unit. 7. When the BCM receives the lock/unlock request signal, it sends (7) a lock/unlock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 8. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the lock/unlock signal, it operates (8) the front/rear door lock actuator motor to lock/unlock the front/rear doors. Note • It takes approx. 1—2 s from when a request switch is pressed until the lock/unlock operation is completed. 9. When the LF control unit receives the beeper sound request signal, it operates (9) the keyless beeper for the following number of times: ― Lock: Sounds once ― Unlock: Sounds twice 10. The BCM flashes (10) each turn light as follows: • Lock: Each turn light flashes once • Unlock: Each turn light flashes twice Lock/unlock operation using remote transmitter Operation Conditions • When door locking is performed ― Lock operation is performed when the lock button of the remote transmitter is operated with all of the following conditions met. • ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected • All door latch switch OFF (all doors closed condition) is detected • Liftgate latch switch OFF (liftgate closed condition) is detected (5HB) *1 *1 :The operation conditions are included depending on the vehicle's period of manufacture. • When door unlocking is performed ― When the unlock button of the remote transmitter is operated with the ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected, unlock operation is performed. 1. When the lock or unlock button of the remote transmitter is pressed, the remote transmitter sends (1) ID data. 2. When the keyless receiver receives ID data, it transmits (2) the data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if the ID data match, it sends (3) a lock/unlock request signal to the BCM and at the same time, it sends (3) a beeper sound request signal to the LF control unit. 4. When the BCM receives the lock/unlock request signal, it sends (4) a lock/unlock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the lock/unlock signal, it operates (5) the front/rear door lock actuator motor to lock/unlock the front/rear doors. 6. When the LF control unit receives the beeper sound request signal, it operates (6) the keyless beeper for the following number of times: ― Lock: Sounds once ― Unlock: Sounds twice 7. The BCM flashes (7) each turn light as follows: • Lock: Each turn light flashes once • Unlock: Each turn light flashes twice Liftgate/Trunk lid open operation Operation Conditions • When the remote transmitter is in outside the keyless antenna reception area, the liftgate/trunk lid is opened by pressing the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch. 1. When the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch is turned on, the liftgate/trunk lid opener signal is input (1) to the BCM. 2. The BCM sends (2) the liftgate/trunk lid open signal to the start stop unit. 3. Based on the liftgate/trunk lid open signal, the start stop unit sends (3) a request output signal to the LF control unit to verify that the remote transmitter is inside the reception area. 4. Based on the request output signal from the start stop unit, the LF control unit outputs (4) a request signal using the keyless antenna inside the rear bumper. 5. The remote transmitter receives the request signal from the antenna (outside, rear), and sends (5) ID data to the keyless receiver. 6. The keyless receiver transmits (6) the received ID data to the start stop unit. 7. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if the ID data matches, it sends (7) a liftgate/trunk lid release request signal to the BCM. 8. When the BCM receives the liftgate/trunk lid release request signal, it sends (8) a liftgate/trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 9. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the liftgate/trunk lid release signal, it operates (9) the liftgate/trunk lid lock actuator motor to open the liftgate/trunk lid. Trunk lid opening operation using remote transmitter Operation Conditions • The trunk lid opens when the trunk lid open button of the remote transmitter is operated with the ACC relay and IG1 relay off (ignition switched OFF condition). 1. When the trunk lid open button is pressed for approx. 0.5 s , the remote transmitter sends (1) the ID data to the keyless receiver. 2. The keyless receiver transmits (2) the received ID data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if the ID data matches, it sends (3) a trunk lid release request signal to the BCM. 4. When the BCM receives the trunk lid release request signal, it sends (4) a trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the trunk lid release signal, it operates (5) the trunk lid release actuator motor to open and opens the trunk lid. Auto re-lock function operation 1. After the start stop unit sends an unlock request signal to the BCM, if any of the following conditions is not met for 30 s *1 , it sends a lock request signal to the BCM. ― Any of door latch switch or liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on signals (any door or liftgate/trunk lid open) received ― Front door lock-link switch lock (driver's door locked) detected ― ACC relay or IG1 relay ON (ignition switched to ACC or ON) detected 2. When the BCM receives the lock request signal, it sends a lock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) and locks the front/rear doors. *1 :Personalization setting time (See SECURITY AND LOCKS PERSONALIZATION .) Out-of-area (reception area) type auto lock function operation 1. The start stop unit goes on auto lock stand-by and operates the keyless beeper once when all of the following conditions are met. • ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected • Front door lock-link switch unlock (driver's door unlocked) detected • Remote transmitter is not within inside keyless antenna reception area • Remote transmitter is within outside keyless antenna reception area • All of door latch switches and liftgate latch switch off signals (all doors and liftgate closed) received from any of door latch switch or liftgate latch switch on signal (any door or liftgate open) received 2. After entering stand-by status, the start stop unit verifies that the remote transmitter is within the keyless antenna reception area. When the remote transmitter is moved out of the keyless antenna reception area or approx. 30 s have elapsed, it performs a lock operation on all of the lock actuators, and operates the keyless beeper once. Remote transmitter pause function operation When door locking is performed 1. If a lock signal is input from the remote transmitter or the request switch while the start stop unit recognizes the remote transmitter inside the vehicle with all the following conditions met, the request signal is output using the inside keyless antenna. It also operates the keyless beeper for 10 s . ― ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected ― All door latch switches and liftgate/trunk lid latch switch off signals (all doors, liftgate/trunk lid closed) received 2. When the remote transmitter inside the vehicle sends the ID data to the keyless receiver, the keyless receiver transmits the received ID data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit receives the ID data, and after approx. 32 s , it suspends the functions of the transmitter inside the vehicle. When the liftgate/trunk lid is closed 1. When the liftgate/trunk lid latch switch off signal (liftgate/trunk lid closed) is received with all the following conditions met, the request signal is output using the inside keyless antenna. It also operates the keyless beeper for 10 s . ― ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected ― All door latch switch off signals (all doors closed) received ― Front door lock-link switch lock (driver's door locked) detected ― Liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on signal (liftgate/trunk lid open) received 2. When the remote transmitter inside the vehicle sends the ID data to the keyless receiver, the keyless receiver transmits the received ID data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit receives the ID data, and after approx. 32 s , it suspends the functions of the remote transmitter inside the vehicle. Remote transmitter pause cancel operation • The functions of the paused remote transmitter are restored when any one of the following conditions is met: ― Remote transmitter with which engine can be started is brought inside vehicle ― Paused lock/unlock button of the remote transmitter is pressed Remote transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function operation 1. When the start stop unit receives the liftgate/trunk lid latch switch off signal (liftgate/trunk lid closed) with all the following conditions met, it operates the keyless beeper for 10 s and the remote transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function operates. ― Liftgate/Trunk lid latch switch on signal (liftgate/trunk lid open) received ― All door latch switch off signals (all doors closed) received ― Front door lock-link switch lock (driver's door locked) detected 2. When the liftgate/trunk lid opener switch is pressed while the remove transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function is operating, the start stop unit verifies the remote transmitter ID data and if it determines that the transmitter is inside the vehicle, it sends a liftgate/trunk lid release request signal to the BCM. 3. When the BCM receives a liftgate/trunk lid release request signal, it sends a liftgate/trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) to open the liftgate/trunk lid. • When any of the following conditions is met while the remote transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function is operating, the remote transmitter left-in-vehicle prevention function is canceled. ― Lock/unlock operation using remote transmitter or request switch ― Any door latch on signal (any door open) received ― Vehicle speed of 10 km/h or more received ― Liftgate/Trunk lid latch switch on signal to off signal (liftgate/trunk lid open to closed) received Alert function operation • Under the following conditions, the start stop unit sends a security warning request signal via CAN transmission to the instrument cluster. It also activates the keyless buzzer. • The instrument cluster turns on/flashes the KEY warning light (red) when it receives the security warning request signal. Remote transmitter battery voltage low indication function operation • When the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to ACC or OFF under the condition indicated in the table, the start stop unit sends a battery voltage low indication request signal to the instrument cluster as a CAN signal. • The instrument cluster flashes the KEY indicator light (green) when it receives the battery voltage low indication request signal.
