Outline • The immobilizer system is a vehicle theft prevention device that only allows remote transmitters that have been previously programmed to the vehicle to start the engine. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Function • The immobilizer system-related parts programmed to the immobilizer system have a programmed key ID number, and starting the engine is only permitted when the key ID number matches. • Immobilizer system-related parts can be programmed using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS). • A maximum 6 remote transmitters can be programmed to one vehicle. • If the following parts are replaced, it is necessary to program them to the immobilizer system. ― Remote transmitter (transponder) ― PCM ― Start stop unit Key code read function • The coil antenna is integrated with the push button start. • When the push button start is touched with the upper part of the remote transmitter with the remote transmitter battery voltage depleted, the coil antenna reads the key code from the transponder built in the remote transmitter and sends the key code to the start stop unit. Operation • Operate in the following order to allow engine starting.

Purpose • Outputs a request signal and specifies the remote transmitter location. Function • The keyless antenna outputs request signals to the inside and outside of the vehicle based on the signals from the LF control unit. Construction/Operation • The antennas for request signal output form the request signal output range at 5 locations. Request signal output range • The keyless antennas for the vehicle exterior (LF, RF, rear) form the request signal output area in the range of an approx. 80 cm radius from each location and communicate with the remote transmitter. • The keyless antennas for the vehicle interior (front, rear) form the output range inside the vehicle. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Outputs a request signal and specifies the remote transmitter location. Function • The keyless antennas output request signals based on the signals from the start stop unit. Construction/Operation • Request signals are output by the keyless antenna installed in the rear console to produce the keyless antenna output range shown in the figure. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • A power door lock system has been adopted in which all doors are locked/unlocked when the driver's door is locked/unlocked using the driver's door lock knob, or the door key cylinder is operated. • A liftgate opener system has been adopted in which the liftgate can be opened just by pressing the liftgate opener switch. • A keyless entry system has been adopted in which locking/locking is performed by operation of the remote transmitter button, even from a location away front the vehicle. (With keyless entry system) • An advanced keyless entry system has been adopted which performs automatic authorization of the remote transmitter that is carried and locking/unlocking of the doors. (With advanced keyless entry system) • A push button start system has been adopted that automatically performs authorization of the remote transmitter brought into the vehicle. • An immobilizer system has been adopted that only allows remote transmitters that have been previously programmed to the vehicle to start the engine. • A theft-deterrent system has been adopted which activates the theft-deterrent siren or theft-deterrent horn if a door, the liftgate/trunk lid, or the hood is opened improperly. (With theft-deterrent system) Structural View Power door lock system Liftgate opener system Trunk lid opener system Keyless entry system/push button start system/immobilizer system Advanced keyless entry system/push button start system/immobilizer system Theft-deterrent system With intruder sensor Without intruder sensor

Outline • All doors lock/unlock when locking/unlocking is performed using the driver's door lock knob or the front door key cylinder. Function Door lock-link switch interlock function • All doors lock/unlock when locking/unlocking is performed using the driver's door lock knob with all doors closed. Door key interlock function • When the front door key cylinder is operated to lock/unlock, all the doors lock/unlock. Double locking function (With double locking) • When the BCM receives the door lock signal two times continuously with all doors closed, it inhibits the lock/unlock operation using the door lock knob. Collision detection unlock function (With collision detection unlock function) • All doors unlock if the vehicle has a collision. Auto door lock function (With auto door lock function) • Doors lock/unlock according to the selector lever position (ATX), vehicle speed, or ignition switch position. The auto door lock function settings can be changed using the personalization feature. For details on the personalization setting, refer to [SECURITY AND LOCKS PERSONALIZATION]. (See SECURITY AND LOCKS PERSONALIZATION .) Structural View System Wiring Diagram Without double locking With double locking Operation Operation Conditions • When the door lock and link switch lock/unlock signal (operation of front door key cylinder or driver's door lock knob) is detected while all the door latch switches and liftgate latch switch off signals (all doors and liftgate closed) are detected, the power door lock system operates. Lock operation using front door key cylinder 1. When the key is inserted in the front door key cylinder and a lock operation is performed, the front door key cylinder switch switches to the lock side. 2. When the BCM detects a front door key cylinder switch lock signal (1), it sends a front door key cylinder switch lock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the front door key cylinder switch lock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door lock relay on (4). 4. When the door lock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform a lock operation (5), and the front and rear doors lock. Lock operation using driver's door lock knob 1. When the driver's door lock knob is locked, the door lock-link switch switches to the lock side. 2. When the BCM detects the door lock link switch lock signal (1), it sends the door lock link switch lock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the door lock link switch lock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door lock relay on (4). 4. When the door lock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform a lock operation (5), and the front and rear doors lock. Lock operation using door lock switch 1. When the door lock switch is operated to lock, the door lock switch switches to the lock side. 2. When the BCM detects the door lock switch lock signal (1), it sends the door lock switch lock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the door lock switch lock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door lock relay on (4). 4. When the door lock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform a lock operation (5), and the front and rear doors lock. Unlock operation using front door key cylinder 1. When the key is inserted in the front door key cylinder and an unlock operation is performed, the front door key cylinder switch switches to the unlock side. 2. When the BCM detects the front door key cylinder switch unlock signal (1), it sends the front door key cylinder switch unlock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the front door key cylinder switch unlock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door unlock relay on (4). 4. When the door unlock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform an unlock operation (5), and the front and rear doors unlock. Unlock operation using the driver's door lock knob 1. When the driver's door lock knob is unlocked, the door lock-link switch switches to the unlock side. 2. When the BCM detects the door lock link switch unlock signal (1), it sends the door lock link switch unlock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the door lock link switch unlock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door unlock relay on (4). 4. When the door unlock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform an unlock operation (5), and the front and rear doors unlock. Unlock operation using door lock switch 1. When the door lock switch is operated to unlock, the door lock switch switches to the unlock side. 2. When the BCM detects the door lock switch unlock signal (1), it sends the door lock switch unlock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the door lock switch unlock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door unlock relay on (4). 4. When the door unlock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform an unlock operation (5), and the front and rear doors unlock. Double locking function (With double locking) 1. When the key is inserted in the front door key cylinder and a lock operation is performed, the front door key cylinder switch switches to the lock side. 2. When the BCM detects a front door key cylinder switch lock signal (1), it sends a front door key cylinder switch lock signal (2) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the front door key cylinder switch lock signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the door lock relay on (4). 4. When the door lock relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform a lock operation (5), and the front and rear doors lock. 5. When lock operation is performed within 3 s after the door lock operation, the front door key cylinder switch switches to the lock side. 6. When the BCM detects a front door key cylinder switch lock signal (6), it sends a double-locking signal (7) to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 7. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the double-locking signal, it turns the transistor on (8) and the door double-locking relay on (9). 8. When the door double-locking relay turns on, the front and rear door lock actuator motors perform a double-locking operation (10), and the front and rear doors lock/unlock operation using door lock knob is inhibited.. Collision detection unlock function operation (With collision detection unlock function) 1. If the vehicle is involved in a collision, the SAS control module sends (1) a collision detection door unlock signal to the BCM via CAN communication and it sends (2) the signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via hard wire. 2. The BCM sends (3) the received collision detection door unlock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. The electrical supply unit (ESU) unlocks all the doors after approx. 6 s it received the collision detection door unlock signal (4). Note • The collision detection unlock function will operate even if only one of the signals is sent. Auto door lock function (With auto door lock function) Selector lever interlock door lock/unlock control (ATX) • The doors lock when the selector lever is shifted to a position other than the P position with all the following conditions met. ― Theft-deterrent system in operation stop-mode, initial mode, or stand-by preparatory mode (See THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM .) ― Ignition switch ON (engine off or on) is detected ― All door latch switch OFF (all doors closed condition) is detected ― Liftgate latch switch OFF (liftgate closed condition) is detected (5HB) ― Vehicle is determined to be driven. • The doors unlock when the selector lever is shifted to the P position with all the following conditions met. ― Theft-deterrent system in operation stop-mode, initial mode, or stand-by preparatory mode (See THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM .) ― Ignition switch ON (engine off or on) is detected Vehicle speed interlock door lock control • The doors unlock when the vehicle speed of 20 km/h {12 mph} or more is detected with all the following conditions met. ― Theft-deterrent system in operation stop-mode, initial mode, or stand-by preparatory mode (See THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM .) ― Ignition switch ON (engine on) is detected ― All door latch switch OFF (all doors closed condition) is detected ― Liftgate latch switch OFF (liftgate closed condition) is detected (5HB) IG interlock door unlock control • The doors unlock when the ignition is switched to ACC or OFF from ON (engine on) with all the following conditions met. ― Theft-deterrent system in operation stop-mode, initial mode, or stand-by preparatory mode (See THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM .) ― Doors locked by selector lever interlock door lock control or vehicle interlock door lock control

Purpose • Performs lock/unlock switching of the front doors electrically based on the signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). Function Lock function • The front door lock actuator operates the built-in motor in the lock direction, and the latch lever will not release even if an inner/outer handle is operated. Unlock function • The front door lock actuator operates the built-in motor in the unlock direction and the latch lever releases when an inner/outer handle is operated. Construction • The front door lock actuator has a built-in motor, and the link installed to the motor moves in the lock/unlock direction in conjunction with the motor rotation. • The link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever can be connected/disconnected by the movement of the link installed to the motor. Operation Lock operation 1. The front door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the lock side. 2. When the motor rotates to the lock side, the link installed to the motor moves in the lock direction, and the link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever release disconnects. 3. When the link connection is disconnected, the latch lever cannot be released even if an inner/outer handle is operated. Unlock operation 1. The front door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the unlock side. 2. When the motor rotates to the unlock side, the link installed to the motor moves in the unlock direction, and the link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever release connects. 3. When the link connects, the latch lever releases by the inner and outer handle operation. Double locking operation 1. The front door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the double locking side based on the double locking operation signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). 2. When the motor rotates to the double locking side, the connection of the door lock knob and front door lock link is disconnected. 3. When the link is disconnected, switching between lock/unlock is not possible even if the door lock knob is operated. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • Turns on/off in conjunction with the latch lever rotation so that the front door open/closed condition is output to the BCM. Construction • The switch is turned on/off by the rotation of the latch lever. Operation Door open (unlatch) operation • When the inner or outer handle is operated, the door opens, the latch lever is in an unlatched condition, and the front door latch switch turns on according to the operation of the latch lever. Door closed (latched) operation 1. When a door is closed, the front door lock striker enters the latch lever groove. 2. When the door is further closed after the latch lever groove enters the front door lock striker, the latch lever is pressed by the front door lock striker and it rotates. 3. When the door is fully closed, the latch lever is in a latched condition, and the front door latch switch turns off according to the operation of the latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Switches on/off in conjunction with the driver's door lock knob lock/unlock, and the driver's front door lock/unlock condition is output to the BCM. Function • The door lock-link switch contact point changes in conjunction with the driver's door lock knob lock/unlock operation. Construction • The driver's door lock knob and door lock-link switch are connected by the door lock-link cable, and are built into the driver's door front door latch and lock actuator. Operation Lock operation • When the driver's door lock knob is turned to the lock position, the door lock-link cable is pressed, and the door lock-link switch is switched to the lock side. Unlock operation • When the driver's door lock knob is turned to the unlock position, the door lock-link cable is pulled, and the door lock-link switch is switched to the unlock side. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Turns on/off in conjunction with the lock/unlock of the front door key cylinder so that the key cylinder operation condition is output to the BCM. Function • The key cylinder switch contact point changes in conjunction with the front door key cylinder lock/unlock operation. Construction • Built into the driver's side front door latch and lock actuator. • The front door key cylinder is connected to the front door latch and lock actuator, and the front door key cylinder is rotated to directly switch the key cylinder switch. • For the front door key cylinder, the switch contacts according to the lock/unlock operation. Operation Lock operation • When the key is inserted in the front door key cylinder and it is rotated in the lock direction, the key cylinder switch switches to the lock side, and the lock-side switch turns on (contact point: Closed). Unlock operation • When the key is inserted in the front door key cylinder and it is rotated in the unlock direction, the key cylinder switch switches to the unlock side, and the unlock-side switch turns on (contact point: Closed). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • The latch of the liftgate latch lever is released based on the signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). Construction • The liftgate lock actuator has a built-in motor, and the liftgate latch lever moves in the release direction in conjunction with the motor rotation. Operation • The liftgate lock actuator rotates the built-in motor based on the liftgate opener system operation signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU), and releases the latch of the liftgate latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • A keyless entry system has been adopted in which locking/locking is performed by operation of the remote transmitter button, even from a location away front the vehicle. Function • When the following operation is performed, the start stop unit verifies the remote transmitter ID data. ― Locking/unlocking using a remote transmitter ― Trunk lid opening using remote transmitter (4SD) • Each light flashes to notify the user that the lock/unlock operation is completed. • The keyless entry system has the following functions in the event that the user operates the system incorrectly or to prevent the user from leaving the vehicle without locking. ― Auto re-lock function: After unlocking, if all doors or the liftgate/trunk lid are not opened and a period of time according to the personalized setting has elapsed, all doors are automatically locked. ― Remote transmitter pause function: All the functions of the remote transmitters inside the vehicle, other than the remote transmitter used for the door lock are paused. ― Warning function: Warns that there is a malfunction in the keyless entry system or the user operates the system incorrectly using any of the following: • Keyless warning alarm • KEY warning light (red) Remote transmitter battery voltage low indication function • This function notifies the driver that the battery voltage of the remote transmitter is low by flashing the KEY indicator light (green). Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Lock/unlock operation using remote transmitter Operation Conditions • When door locking is performed ― Lock operation is performed when the lock button of the remote transmitter is operated with all of the following conditions met. • ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected • All door latch switch OFF (all doors closed condition) is detected • Liftgate latch switch OFF (liftgate closed condition) is detected (5HB) *1 *1 :The operation conditions are included depending on the vehicle's period of manufacture. • When door unlocking is performed ― When the unlock button of the remote transmitter is operated with the ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected, unlock operation is performed. 1. When the lock or unlock button of the remote transmitter is pressed, the remote transmitter sends (1) ID data. 2. The keyless receiver receives ID data and transmits (2) the data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if the ID data matches, it sends (3) a lock/unlock request signal to the BCM. 4. When the BCM receives the lock/unlock request signal, it sends (4) a lock/unlock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the lock/unlock signal, it operates (5) the front/rear door lock actuator motor to lock/unlock the front/rear doors. 6. The BCM flashes (6) each turn light as follows: • Lock: Each turn light flashes once • Unlock: Each turn light flashes twice Trunk lid opening operation using remote transmitter Operation Conditions • The trunk lid opens when the trunk lid open button of the remote transmitter is operated with the ACC relay and IG1 relay off (ignition switched OFF condition). 1. When the trunk lid open button is pressed for approx. 0.5 s , the remote transmitter sends (1) the ID data to the keyless receiver. 2. The keyless receiver transmits (2) the received ID data to the start stop unit. 3. The start stop unit verifies the ID data, and if the ID data matches, it sends (3) a trunk lid release request signal to the BCM. 4. When the BCM receives the trunk lid release request signal, it sends (4) a trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the trunk lid release signal, it operates (5) the trunk lid release actuator motor to open and opens the trunk lid. Auto re-lock function operation 1. After the start stop unit sends an unlock request signal to the BCM, if any of the following conditions is not met for 30 s *1 , it sends a lock request signal to the BCM. ― Any door latch switch or liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on signal (any door or liftgate/trunk lid open) received ― Front door lock-link switch lock (driver's door locked) detected ― ACC relay or IG1 relay ON (ignition switched to ACC or ON) detected 2. When the BCM receives a lock request signal, it sends a lock signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) and locks the front/rear doors. *1 :Personalization setting time Remote transmitter pause function operation When door locking is performed • If a door is locked by the remote transmitter operation when all the following conditions are met, all the functions of the remote transmitter inside the vehicle, other than the remote transmitter used for the door lock operation are paused. ― All door latch switch and liftgate/trunk lid latch switch on signals (all doors, liftgate/trunk lid closed) received ― ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected When the liftgate/trunk lid is closed • When the liftgate/trunk lid latch switch off signal (liftgate/trunk lid closed) is received with all the following conditions met, all the functions of the remote transmitter inside the vehicle are paused. ― Front door lock-link switch lock (driver's door locked) detected ― All door latch switch off signals (all doors closed) received ― ACC relay and IG1 relay OFF (ignition switched OFF) detected Remote transmitter pause cancel operation • The functions of the paused remote transmitter are restored when any one of the following conditions is met: ― Remote transmitter with which engine can be started is brought inside vehicle ― Lock/unlock button on paused remote transmitter is pressed Alert function operation • Under the conditions in the table below, the start stop unit sends a security warning request signal via CAN transmission to the instrument cluster. • The instrument cluster turns on/flashes the KEY warning light (red) when it receives the security warning request signal. Condition Instrument cluster Keyless warning alarm KEY warning light (red) Keyless entry system malfunction *1 ― On The driver's front door is opened with the ignition in ACC. Pattern A *2 Continuous ― The remote transmitter cannot be detected inside the vehicle when all doors are closed with the ignition not switched OFF. Pattern B *2 Flash *1 :For vehicles with the center display, a warning message in the center display is displayed when the KEY warning light (red) is turned on. For the message content and verification method, refer to the [CENTER DISPLAY]. (See CENTER DISPLAY [WITH CENTER DISPLAY] .) *2 :For the keyless warning alarm sound pattern, refer to the [KEYLESS WARNING ALARM]. (See KEYLESS WARNING ALARM .) Remote transmitter battery voltage low indication function operation • When the ignition is switched from ON (engine off or on) to ACC or OFF under the condition indicated in the table, the start stop unit sends a battery voltage low indication request signal to the instrument cluster as a CAN signal. • The instrument cluster flashes the KEY indicator light (green) when it receives the battery voltage low indication request signal. Condition Instrument cluster KEY indicator light (green) Start stop unit receives code for low remote transmitter battery voltage *1 Flash (for approx. 30 s after ignition switched from ON to OFF or ACC) *1 :If the remote transmitter battery power is 0, the remote transmitter battery voltage low indication function does not operate. • For vehicles with the center display, a warning message in the center display is displayed when the KEY indicator light (green) flashes. For the message content and verification method, refer to the [CENTER DISPLAY]. (See CENTER DISPLAY [WITH CENTER DISPLAY] .)

Purpose • Transmits the request switch operation of the user to the LF control unit. Function • The request switch ON signal is sent to the LF control unit by operating the request switch. Construction/Operation • The request switch is located on the outer handle of the driver's/passenger's front door. • While the request switch is pressed, the switch turns on (contact point: closed). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • Notifies the user that the lock/unlock operation of the advanced keyless entry system is completed, and warns if the system is operated incorrectly. Construction/Operation • A keyless beeper is located on the inside of the cowl grille. • The keyless beeper operates based on the LF control unit signal. For details of the beeper operation, refer to the alert function operation in the [ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM]. (See ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • Receives ID data from the remote transmitter and sends the received ID data to the start stop unit. Construction • A keyless receiver is located on the inside of the trunk side trim (RH). (5HB) • A keyless receiver is located on the inside of the tire house trim (RH). (4SD) Operation 1. The ID data sent from the remote transmitter is received by the keyless receiver. 2. The keyless receiver sends the received ID data to the start stop unit. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • Sends the ID data programmed to the electronic transmission device (transponder) in the remote transmitter to the start stop unit. Construction, Operation • The coil antenna built into the push button start sends a signal to the transponder and sends the returned signal to the start stop unit. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Read the SRS air bag system service warnings and cautions before handling the air bag module. (See AIR BAG SYSTEM SERVICE WARNINGS [TWO-STEP DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See AIR BAG SYSTEM SERVICE CAUTIONS [TWO-STEP DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See AIR BAG SYSTEM SERVICE WARNINGS [STANDARD DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) Otherwise, it will cause internal damage and the steering lock cannot be unlocked, resulting in the inability to perform the start-stop unit removal/installation. • If configuration is not performed when the start stop unit is replaced with a new one, the vehicle specification information is not stored in the start stop unit and the system will not operate normally. • When performing configuration, it is necessary to read the vehicle specification information from the start stop unit before replacing it. Connect the M-MDS to the vehicle and perform vehicle identification before removing the start stop unit. The vehicle specification information is temporarily stored in the M-MDS. Note • The start stop unit prior to replacement stores the vehicle specification information. • A new start stop unit does not store any vehicle specification information. • If the vehicle specification information from the start stop unit prior to replacement cannot be read, perform the configuration using As-Built data. • When removing the driver-side air bag module, it is necessary to rotate the steering wheel. If the ignition has been switched off with the driver's door closed, the steering wheel will be locked. Perform the procedure from Steps 2-4 so that the steering wheel will not be locked. 1. When replacing the start stop unit, perform the configuration. (See START STOP UNIT CONFIGURATION (USING READ/WRITE FUNCTION) .) 2. Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). 3. Open the driver's door. 4. Switch the ignition off. 5. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 6. Remove the following parts: (1) Driver-side air bag module (See DRIVER-SIDE AIR BAG MODULE REMOVAL [TWO-STEP DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See DRIVER-SIDE AIR BAG MODULE INSTALLATION [TWO-STEP DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See DRIVER-SIDE AIR BAG MODULE REMOVAL [STANDARD DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See DRIVER-SIDE AIR BAG MODULE INSTALLATION [STANDARD DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (2) Steering wheel (See STEERING WHEEL AND COLUMN REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (3) Column cover (See COLUMN COVER REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (4) Meter hood (See METER HOOD REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (5) Clock spring (See CLOCK SPRING REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [TWO-STEP DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (See CLOCK SPRING REMOVAL/INSTALLATION [STANDARD DEPLOYMENT CONTROL SYSTEM] .) (6) Wiper and washer switch (See WIPER AND WASHER SWITCH REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (7) Light switch (See LIGHT SWITCH REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 7. Disconnect the connector. 8. While pressing the tabs of the clip in the direction of arrow (1) shown in the figure, press it in the direction of arrow (2) to detach the connector tabs from the start stop unit. 9. Remove the wiring harness clip from the start stop unit. 10. Make a groove on the heads of the bolts by punching them with a chisel using a hammer. 11. Remove the bolts by rotating them counterclockwise. 12. Remove the start stop unit from the steering shaft by pulling it in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure. 13. Install in the reverse order of removal. (See Start Stop Unit Installation Note .) 14. Perform the following when replacing the start stop unit. • Start stop unit configuration. (See START STOP UNIT CONFIGURATION (USING READ/WRITE FUNCTION) .) Note • If configuration cannot be performed by reading/writing of the vehicle specification information, perform the configuration using As-Built information after replacing the start stop unit. (See START STOP UNIT CONFIGURATION (USING AS-BUILT DATA) .) • Immobilizer system-related parts programming. (See IMMOBILIZER SYSTEM-RELATED PARTS PROGRAMMING .) Start Stop Unit Installation Note 1. Temporarily install the start stop unit to the steering shaft using new start stop unit installation bolts. 2. Tighten the start stop unit installation bolts until the heads break off.

Purpose, Function • Turns on/off in conjunction with the latch lever rotation so that the rear door open/closed condition is output to the BCM. Construction • The switch is turned on/off by the rotation of the latch lever. Operation Door open (unlatch) operation • When the inner or outer handle is operated, the door opens, the latch lever is in an unlatched condition, and the rear door latch switch turns on according to the operation of the latch lever. Door closed (latched) operation 1. When a door is closed, the rear door lock striker enters the latch lever groove. 2. When the door is further closed after the latch lever groove enters the rear door lock striker, the latch lever is pressed by the rear door lock striker and it rotates. 3. When the door is fully closed, the latch lever is in a latched condition, and the rear door latch switch turns off according to the operation of the latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Switches on/off in conjunction with the rear door lock knob lock/unlock, and detects the rear door lock/unlock condition by the voltage which is changed by the BCM. Function • The door lock-link switch contact point changes in conjunction with the rear door lock knob lock/unlock operation. Construction • The rear door lock knob and door lock-link switch are connected by the door lock-link cable, and are built into the rear door latch and lock actuator. Operation Lock operation • When the rear door lock knob is turned to the lock position, the door lock-link cable is pressed, and the door lock-link switch is switched to the lock side. Unlock operation • When the rear door lock knob is turned to the unlock position, the door lock-link cable is pulled, and the door lock-link switch is switched to the unlock side. Fail-safe • Not applicable.

Outline • The immobilizer system has an on-board diagnostic function to facilitate system diagnosis. Function • The on-board diagnostic function consists of the following functions: ― A malfunction detection function, which detects overall malfunctions in the immobilizer system-related parts. ― A memory function, which stores detected DTCs. ― A display function, which indicates system malfunctions via DTC display. ― A PID/data monitoring function, which reads out specific input/output signals. • Using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS), DTCs can be read out and deleted, and PID/data monitoring can be performed. On-board Diagnostic Function Malfunction detection function • Detects overall malfunctions in the immobilizer system-related parts. • Malfunction diagnosis of the immobilizer system is automatically performed every time the engine is switched from off (ACC) to ON (START). Memory Function • Malfunctions detected by the malfunction detection function are all recorded as DTCs in the following modules. ― Start stop unit ― PCM Caution • Recorded immobilizer system DTCs are cleared when the ignition is switched ON from off/ACC. Display Function • If there is a malfunction in the immobilizer system, the security indicator light in the instrument cluster is illuminated to notify the driver. In addition, DTCs are displayed by the number of times that the security indicator light flashes. Note • If two or more malfunctions are detected as a result of malfunction diagnosis, only the DTC with the lowest number of those detected will be indicated by the security indicator light. • In the approx. 1 min after detecting a malfunction and before displaying the DTC, the security indicator light turns on, flashes, or turns off in the following patterns: Security indicator light flash pattern (before displaying DTC) DTC 09, 11, 13, 15, 16 21 22, 23 • Using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS), DTCs can be read out and deleted. Caution • If the security indicator light itself has a malfunction, it is possible that a DTC may not be indicated properly. Purpose • Performs lock/unlock switching of the rear doors electrically based on the signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). Function Lock function • The rear door lock actuator operates the built-in motor in the lock direction, and the latch lever will not release even if an inner/outer handle is operated. Unlock function • The rear door lock actuator operates the built-in motor in the unlock direction and the latch lever releases when an inner/outer handle is operated. Construction • The rear door lock actuator has a built-in motor, and the link installed to the motor moves in the lock/unlock direction in conjunction with the motor rotation. • The link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever can be connected/disconnected by the movement of the link installed to the motor. Operation Lock operation 1. The rear door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the lock side. 2. When the motor rotates to the lock side, the link installed to the motor moves in the lock direction, and the link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever release disconnects. 3. When the link connection is disconnected, the latch lever cannot be released even if an inner/outer handle is operated. Unlock operation 1. The rear door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the unlock side. 2. When the motor rotates to the unlock side, the link installed to the motor moves in the unlock direction, and the link for the inner/outer handle and latch lever release connects. 3. When the link connects, the latch lever releases by the inner and outer handle operation. Double locking operation 1. The rear door lock actuator rotates the built-in motor to the double locking side based on the double locking operation signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). 2. When the motor rotates to the double locking side, the connection of the door lock knob and rear door lock link is disconnected. 3. When the link is disconnected, switching between lock/unlock is not possible even if the door lock knob is operated. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The keyless buzzer and keyless antenna are controlled by the input/output signals from the start stop unit. Function • The LF control unit controls the keyless buzzer sound based on the signal from the start stop unit. • The LF control unit sends the request signal from the keyless antenna based on the signal from the start stop unit. Construction • The LF control unit is located on the inside of the front side trim. Operation Keyless buzzer control 1. The LF control unit receives (1) a beeper sound request signal from the start stop unit. 2. When the LF control unit receives the beeper sound request signal, it sounds (2) the keyless buzzer. Keyless antenna control 1. The LF control unit receives (1) a request output signal from the start stop unit. 2. When the LF control unit receives the request output signal, it outputs (2) the request signal from the keyless antenna. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • A push button start system has been adopted that automatically performs authorization of the remote transmitter brought into the vehicle. • If the engine stalls due to incorrect operation of the clutch by the driver, an engine restarting by depressing clutch pedal function has been adopted to allow the engine to be restarted by only depressing the clutch pedal.(MTX) Function • When the bush button start is pressed, the push button start system performs authorization of the remote transmitter in the vehicle. ― Engine start: When authorization of the remote transmitter is completed with the engine-start conditions met, the engine starts. • The guidance function is indicated by the KEY warning light (red) and the keyless warning alarm if there are insufficient conditions for starting the engine, remote transmitter authorization issues, or the steering lock cannot be released. Engine restarting function by depressing clutch pedal • If the start stop unit determines that the driver intends to restart the engine because the engine has stalled, the engine restarting by depressing clutch pedal function restarts the engine. • The start stop unit determines that the driver is seated based on the conditions that the driver's seat belt is fastened and the driver's door is closed, and it determines that the driver intends to restart the engine when the clutch pedal is depressed from a released condition within 3 s after the engine stalls. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Remote transmitter authorization, power supply switching 1. When the push button start is pressed, a push button start signal is input (1) to the start stop unit. 2. When the start stop unit detects a push button start signal, it sends (2) a request outgoing command signal to the LF control unit. 3. When the LF control unit detects the request outgoing command signal, it outputs (3) a request signal using all the keyless antennas in the vehicle interior. 4. The remote transmitter receives the request signal from the interior keyless antennas, and sends (4) ID data to the keyless receiver. 5. The keyless receiver transmits (5) the received ID data to the start stop unit. 6. The start stop unit verifies the ID data and if it matches the steering lock in the module is released (6) and the power supply is switched simultaneously to turn the push button start indicator light (amber) on. For details on the power supply switching, refer to the [POWER SUPPLY SWITCHING]. (See POWER SUPPLY SWITCHING .) Engine start • When all the following conditions are met, authorization of the remote transmitter which is being used to press the push button start is performed to start the engine. Engine start conditions ― Clutch pedal position switch and starter interlock switch on signals (clutch pedal depressed) detected (MTX) ― Brake switch on signal (brake pedal depressed) detected (ATX) ― P or N position signal from selector lever (selector lever at P or N position) received (ATX) ― Remote transmitter is within request signal output range of keyless antennas in vehicle interior Engine emergency stop • If a push button start on signal is input for 3 s or more (ignition switch held pressed) or a push button start on signal is input 3 times within 1.5 s with the engine running, the start stop unit switches the ignition to ACC or OFF according to the position of the shift lever (MTX)/selector lever (ATX). Back-up mode (MTX) for engine-start • If the start stop unit determines that either the clutch pedal position switch or starter interlock switch is malfunctioning, the system switches to back-up mode. • If the push button start is pressed when all the following conditions are met while in the back-up mode, the remote transmitter authorization is performed and the engine starts. ― Start stop unit detects that either clutch pedal position switch or starter interlock switch is on ― Neutral switch signal is received via CAN communication from PCM ― Remote transmitter is within request signal output range of keyless antennas in vehicle interior Engine restarting function by depressing clutch pedal 1. The start stop unit enables the engine restarting by depressing clutch pedal function operation when all of the following conditions are met. ― Within 3 s after engine-stall signal is received via CAN communication from PCM (1) ― Driver buckle switch off signal (seat belt fastened) is received via CAN communication from SAS control module (2) ― Driver door latch off signal (door closed) is received via ISO communication from BCM (3) 2. If all of the following are detected, the start stop unit sends an engine starting enabled signal (3) to the PCM via CAN communication and restarts the engine. ― Clutch pedal position switch off to on detected (1) ― Starter interlock switch off to on detected (2) Guidance function Display of methods for resolving issues • Under the following conditions, the start stop unit sends a warning request signal via CAN transmission to the instrument cluster. It also flashes the push button start indicator (green). • When the instrument cluster receives the warning request signal under the following conditions, it flashes the KEY warning light (red). Condition Instrument cluster Push button start Keyless warning alarm KEY warning light (red) Indicator light (green) Indicator light (amber) ID verification is not acceptable ― Flash ― Flash Steering lock cannot be released Pattern C *1 ― Flash for 10 s ― *1 :For the keyless warning alarm sound pattern, refer to the [KEYLESS WARNING ALARM].(See KEYLESS WARNING ALARM .)

Purpose • When the lock button/unlock button of the remote transmitter is pressed, ID data is sent to the keyless receiver. Function • When the remote transmitter sends ID data, the operation indicator light is turned on. Construction • The remote transmitter has a built-in operation indicator light. • The remote transmitter has a built-in electronic communication device (transponder) and specific electronic codes (key ID number). • In case the remote transmitter is inoperable due to battery depletion, the doors can be locked/unlocked using the auxiliary key. Operation • When the remote transmitter button is pressed, ID data is sent to the keyless receiver. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Note • A simple inspection of the remaining battery power of the remote transmitter can be performed by activating the battery voltage low warning. • The battery voltage low warning is performed via transmission between the remote transmitter and the vehicle. If the battery power of the remote transmitter is completely depleted, transmission between the remote transmitter and the vehicle is not established and the battery voltage warning is not activated. • If the remote transmitter is not touching the push button start, the engine cannot be switched ON (engine off), and the battery voltage low warning is not activated, it is likely that the remote transmitter battery power is completely depleted. Operation Procedure For Battery Voltage Low Warning Indication 1. Place the remote transmitter inside the vehicle and close all of the doors. 2. Switch the ignition ON (engine off) and wait approx. 30 s . 3. Switch the ignition off. 4. Verify that the KEY indicator light (green) in the instrument cluster is not flashing. ― If the KEY indicator light (green) flashes for approx. 30 s, replace the remote transmitter battery because the battery power is depleted. (See REMOTE TRANSMITTER DISASSEMBLY/ASSEMBLY .)

Disassembly 1. Press the knob on the remote transmitter and pull the auxiliary key out. 2. Insert a tape-wrapped flathead screwdriver into the notch on the remote transmitter and turn it in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure to detach tabs A from the remote transmitter. 3. Insert a tape-wrapped flathead screwdriver between the remote transmitter and the cover and slide it in the direction of arrow (1) shown in the figure. 4. Turn the screwdriver in the direction of arrow (2) shown in the figure to detach tabs B of the cover from the remote transmitter. 5. Remove the cover. 6. Remove the cap and the battery from the remote transmitter. Assembly 1. Verify that the O-ring is installed to the remote transmitter. Note • If the O-ring is removed, install it before installing the battery. 2. Install a new battery (CR2025) in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure with the negative pole facing down. 3. Install the cap. 4. Align the cover to the transmitter from its end and press it in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure to engage the tabs of the cover with the remote transmitter. 5. Insert the auxiliary key.

Purpose • The theft-deterrent system operation history is a record of the theft-deterrent system operation. Function • The theft-deterrent system operation record is stored by the BCM and displayed using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS). • The BCM records the following when the theft-deterrent system is operated. ― Time and date ― Theft-deterrent system operation time ― Location in theft-deterrent system where operation was triggered Construction • Based on the stored record, the BCM displays the following operation record on the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS) screen. Operation • The BCM sends an alarm sound signal to the theft-deterrent siren or theft-deterrent horn, and records the operation history simultaneously. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • A trunk lid opener system has been adopted in which the trunk lid can be opened just by pressing the trunk lid opener switch. Function • The BCM operates the trunk lid release actuator and opens the trunk lid based on the trunk lid opener switch signal. Structural view System wiring diagram Operation Trunk lid opener switch (exterior) open operation • When the BCM receives a trunk lid opener switch on signal with any of the following conditions met, it opens the trunk lid. Operation Conditions ― Vehicle speed of 3 km/h {2 mph} or less received ― Ignition switched OFF 1. When the trunk lid opener switch is pressed, it turns on (1). 2. When the BCM detects the trunk lid opener switch on signal with the trunk lid opener system operation conditions met, it sends (2) a trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU). 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the trunk lid release signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the trunk lid release relay on (4). 4. When the trunk lid release relay turns on, the trunk lid release actuator operates (5). 5. When the trunk lid release actuator operates, the latch lever is released to open the trunk lid. Trunk lid opener switch (Interior) open operation (with trunk lid opener switch (Interior)) • When the BCM receives a trunk lid opener switch on signal with the theft-deterrent system not activated and any of the following conditions met, it opens the trunk lid. Operation Conditions ― Vehicle speed of 3 km/h {2 mph} or less received ― Ignition switched OFF 1. When the trunk lid opener switch is pressed, it turns on (1). 2. When the BCM detects the trunk lid opener switch on signal with the trunk lid opener system operation conditions met, it sends (2) a trunk lid release signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU). 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the trunk lid release signal, it turns the transistor on (3) and the trunk lid release relay on (4). 4. When the trunk lid release relay turns on, the trunk lid release actuator operates (5). 5. When the trunk lid release actuator operates, the latch lever is released to open the trunk lid.

Purpose, Function • The latch of the trunk lid latch lever is released based on the signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU). Construction • The trunk lid release actuator has a built-in motor, and the trunk lid latch lever moves in the release direction in conjunction with the motor rotation. Operation • The trunk lid release actuator rotates the built-in motor based on the trunk lid opener system operation signal from the electrical supply unit (ESU), and releases the latch of the trunk lid latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable.

Purpose • Transmits the trunk lid opener switch operation of the user to the BCM. Function • The trunk lid opener switch on signal is sent to the BCM by operating the trunk lid opener switch. Construction, Operation • Installed on the trunk lid. • While the trunk lid opener switch is pressed, the switch turns on (contact point: closed). Fail-safe • Not applicable.

Purpose, Function • Turns on/off in conjunction with the latch lever rotation so that the trunk lid open/closed condition is output to the BCM. Construction • The switch is turned on/off by the rotation of the latch lever. Operation Trunk lid closed (latched) operation 1. When the trunk lid is closed, the trunk lid lock striker enters the latch lever groove. 2. When the trunk lid is further closed after the latch lever groove enters the trunk lid lock striker, the latch lever is pressed by the trunk lid lock striker and it rotates. 3. When the trunk lid is fully closed, the latch lever is in a latched condition, and the trunk lid latch switch turns off according to the operation of the latch lever. Trunk lid open (unlatch) operation • When the trunk lid release actuator operates to open the trunk lid, the latch lever is in an unlatched condition, and the trunk lid latch switch turns on according to the operation of the latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable.

Foreword • When replacing immobilizer system-related parts or programming an additional remote transmitter, or clearing a remote transmitter, program the immobilizer system-related parts so that the system operates normally. For immobilizer system-related parts programming, select the programming procedures according to the service. (See Selection of Procedure for Immobilizer System-Related Parts Programming .) Caution • The engine cannot be started if any step or procedure for each service operation is skipped. Perform all procedures in the order of the steps. • If any metallic or magnetic object is near the remote transmitter, communication between the remote transmitter and the vehicle may be obstructed, resulting in a failure to program the immobilizer system-related parts. Remove any metallic or magnetic objects, such as key holders, from the remote transmitter when programming immobilizer system-related parts. • If any of the following devices are inside the vehicle, programming of immobilizer system-related parts may fail. Do not bring any of the following devices or similar products inside the vehicle when programming immobilizer system-related parts. ― M-MDS ― Personal computer ― Devices that can send/receive radio waves • If the engine is started during immobilizer system-related parts programming, the programming mode cancels. Therefore, do not start the engine unless indicated in the procedure. Repeat the procedure from the beginning if the engine is started during the immobilizer system-related parts programming. • If a remote transmitter is near the vehicle during immobilizer system-related parts programming, it may be programmed mistakenly. Keep the remote transmitter 1 m away from the vehicle unless indicated in the procedure. • The SSU in the procedure indicates the start stop unit. In addition, the advanced key indicates the remote transmitter. Note • Two or more remote transmitters must be programmed for the engine to start. • A maximum of six remote transmitters can be programmed to one vehicle. • The number of programmed key ID numbers can be verified using the M-MDS. • Do not select any screen menu other than the ones indicated in the procedure during M-MDS operation. • When programming the immobilizer system-related parts, the incode must be searched. Selection of Procedure for Immobilizer System-Related Parts Programming 1. Verify that the ROOM fuse, AT fuse, and SRS2/ESCL fuse are installed. 2. Select the applicable programming procedure from the service content of the immobilizer system-related parts. Immobilizer System-Related Parts Service and Programming Procedure Table No. Service Programming procedure 1 Additional remote transmitter programming Have remote transmitter that can start engine (See No.1 Additional Remote Transmitter Programming Procedure (Using the M-MDS) .) 2 Programming due to PCM replacement (See No.2 Programming Procedure After PCM Replacement .) 3 Start stop unit replacement and programming due to simultaneous replacement of start stop unit/PCM (See No.3 Start stop unit replacement and programming procedure due to simultaneous replacement of start stop unit/PCM .) 4 Remote transmitter replacement or clearing (See No.4 Remote transmitter replacement or remote transmitter clearing .) 5 Additional remote transmitter programming There is no remote transmitter available that can start engine (See No.5 Additional Remote Transmitter Programming Procedure (If there is no remote transmitter available that can start engine) (Using M-MDS) .) M-MDS Connecting Procedure Note • Do not place the M-MDS in the vehicle while programming the immobilizer system. 1. Fully lower the door glass. 2. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. 3. Place the M-MDS outside the vehicle. Caution • Cover the vehicle body with a rag so as not to damage the vehicle body with the cable. Procedure for communication between coil antenna and remote transmitter • While the push button start indicator light (green) is flashing, press the top part of the remote transmitter against the center of the push button start. Note • The coil antenna is integrated with the push button start. No.1 Additional Remote Transmitter Programming Procedure (Using the M-MDS) Caution • The engine cannot be started if any step or procedure is skipped. Perform all procedures in the order of the steps. Vehicle condition • There is a remote transmitter that can start the engine. Note • If a remote transmitter cannot be programmed, verify the number of programmed remote transmitter using the M-MDS. • Perform the DTC inspection for the start stop unit using the M-MDS. Procedure Step Procedure Action after procedure 1 VERIFY THAT REMOTE TRANSMITTER WHICH CAN START ENGINE IS REMOTE TRANSMITTER 1 1. Switch the ignition ON (engine off) using remote transmitter 1. 2. Verify that the security light illuminates for approx. 3 s , and then turns off. 3. Switch the ignition off. Go to the next step. 2 PERFORM ADDITIONAL PROGRAMMING OF REMOTE TRANSMITTER 2 1. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. (See M-MDS Connecting Procedure .) 2. Switch the ignition ON (engine off) using remote transmitter 1. 3. After vehicle identification, select the following from the M-MDS initial screen. 1. “Body” 2. “Security” 3. “PATS (immobilizer) function” 4. Purpose • Detects the open/closed condition of the bonnet. Function • The bonnet latch switch is utilized in the i-stop control. ― For the i-stop control, refer to the [i-STOP CONTROL]. (See i-stop CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) (See i-stop CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .) ― For the theft-deterrent system, refer to the [THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM]. (See THEFT-DETERRENT SYSTEM .) Construction • Built into the bonnet latch. • Switch turns on and off by the rotation of the latch bar. • When the bonnet is completely closed, the bonnet latch switch is on (contact point: closed). Operation Bonnet close (latch) operation 1. When the bonnet is closed, the bonnet lock striker enters the latch lever groove. 2. When the bonnet is then further closed, the latch lever is pressed by the bonnet lock striker and rotates. 3. When the bonnet is completely closed, the latch lever is in a latched condition and presses the bonnet latch switch which turns the switch on. Bonnet open (unlatch) operation • When the bonnet release lever is pulled, the bonnet opens and the latch lever is in an unlatched condition, and the bonnet latch switch turns off. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • Turns on/off in conjunction with the latch lever rotation so that the liftgate open/closed condition is output to the BCM. Construction • The switch is turned on/off by the rotation of the latch lever. Operation Liftgate closed (latched) operation 1. When the liftgate is closed, the liftgate lock striker enters the latch lever groove. 2. When the liftgate is further closed after the latch lever groove enters the liftgate lock striker, the latch lever is pressed by the liftgate lock striker and it rotates. 3. When the liftgate is fully closed, the latch lever is in a latched condition, and the liftgate latch switch turns off according to the operation of the latch lever. Liftgate open (unlatch) operation • When the liftgate lock actuator operates to open the liftgate, the latch lever is in an unlatched condition, and the liftgate latch switch turns on according to the operation of the latch lever. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The security indicator light notifies the driver that the immobilizer system is operating or there is a malfunction in the system. Function • The instrument cluster flashes the security indicator light based on the system condition display request signal sent via a CAN signal from the start stop unit. • When the immobilizer system is operating, it turns on for 0.1 s every approx. 2 s. • If the immobilizer system is normal, the security indicator light turns on for approx. 3 s and then turns off after the push button start is pressed. • When there is a malfunction in the immobilizer system, the DTC can be verified by the flashing pattern. For details, refer to the [ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM].(See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSIS SYSTEM [IMMOBILIZER SYSTEM] .) Construction • The security indicator light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. The instrument cluster receives (1) the system condition display request signal or warning indication request signal from the start stop unit via CAN communication. 2. When the instrument cluster receives the system condition display request signal or warning indication request signal, it turns the transistor on (2). 3. When the transistor turns on, the security indicator light turns on/flashes (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose KEY warning light (red) • The KEY warning light (red) notifies the driver that the engine cannot be started, the remote transmitter is outside of the vehicle, or that there is a malfunction in the system. KEY indicator light (green) • The KEY indicator light (green) notifies the driver that the engine starting conditions have been met or that the remote transmitter battery voltage is depleted. Function KEY warning light (red) • When a malfunction is detected in the keyless entry system or advanced keyless entry system, the KEY warning light (red) turns on. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSIS SYSTEM [ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSIS SYSTEM [START STOP UNIT] .) ― For vehicles with the center display, a warning message in the center display is displayed when the KEY warning light (red) is turned on. For the message content and verification method, refer to the CENTER DISPLAY. (See CENTER DISPLAY [WITH CENTER DISPLAY] .) • The KEY warning light (red) flashes if the engine cannot be started and when the ignition is switched to ACC or ON (engine off or on) and the transmitter is taken outside of the vehicle. (See KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) (See ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) KEY indicator light (green) • When the engine-starting conditions have been met, the KEY indicator light (green) turns on. (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) (See PUSH BUTTON START SYSTEM [ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM] .) • If the remote transmitter battery voltage is depleted, the KEY indicator light (green) flashes. (See KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) (See ADVANCED KEYLESS ENTRY SYSTEM .) ― For vehicles with the center display, a warning message in the center display is displayed when the KEY indicator light (green) flashes. For the message content and verification method, refer to the CENTER DISPLAY. (See CENTER DISPLAY [WITH CENTER DISPLAY] .) Construction • The KEY warning light (red)/KEY indicator light (green) are built into the instrument cluster. Operation KEY warning light (red) 1. The instrument cluster receives (1) the system condition display request signal or warning indication request signal from the start stop unit via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) intermittently for a system condition display request signal and continuously for a warning indication request signal. 3. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the KEY warning light (red) flashes (3), and when it is turned on continuously, the KEY warning light (red) turns on (3). KEY indicator light (green) 1. The instrument cluster receives (1) the system condition display request signal or battery voltage low indication request signal from the start stop unit via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) intermittently for a battery voltage low indication request signal and continuously for a system conditions indication request signal. 3. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the KEY indicator light (green) flashes (3), and when it is turned on continuously, the KEY indicator light (green) turns on (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Under covers and deflectors have been adopted to straighten the wind flow to the underside of the vehicle. Function/Construction • A deflector is equipped in front of each tire to straighten the wind flow passing around the tire and alongside the vehicle. • By equipping the under covers to the uneven areas on the underside of the vehicle, the underside of the vehicle becomes flat and the wind flow is straightened. Front under cover No.1/front under cover No.2/plate • Prevents wind flow into the engine compartment, allowing it flow to the vehicle rear. Front deflector/rear deflector • Prevents wind flow into the tire housings and straighten wind flow away from the body side, allowing it to flow to the vehicle rear. • Front and rear tire deflectors prevent the wind flow from hitting the rotating tires and reduces aerodynamic drag. Floor under cover • Straightens wind flow under the floor. Fuel tank side cover • Prevents wind flow from swirling between the floor and the fuel tank, allowing it to flow to the vehicle rear. Trunk floor cover • Prevents wind flow from swirling around the underside of the rear bumper, allowing it to flow to the vehicle rear. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • The rear side spoilers have been adopted to smooth the wind flowing to the vehicle rear. Construction • The rear side spoilers are positioned on the left and right of the rear window upper area. Operation • The rear side spoilers smooth wind flow around the C-pillar area to the rear window, suppressing the trailing vortex. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • A cowl grille with a shock-absorbing structure has been adopted to reduce impact to pedestrians in a collision. Function • If a pedestrian contacts the cowl grille in a collision, the cowl grille deforms to reduces impact applied to the pedestrian. Construction L.H.D. • The cowl grille has a slit on the side (RH). R.H.D. • The cowl grille has a slit on the side (LH). • The slit on the side of the cowl grille contributes to facilitated deformation when impact is applied from the upper side of the cowl grille. • When impact is applied from the upper side of the cowl grille, the cowl grille deforms in a V shape, absorbing the impact energy from a collision. • Covers made of soft material are equipped on the both sides of the cowl grille to optimize the rigidity. • The soft-material cover equipped on the both sides of the cowl grille prevents rain from penetrating the engine compartment. In addition, it prevents heat and odors from entering the cabin from the engine compartment. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose, Function • A crushable structure has been adopted to the door trim armrest to reduce impact to the occupants in a collision. Construction • A slit has been made in the door armrest panel. • If the door trim hits an occupant due to a side collision, the slit in the armrest panel deforms and the armrest crushes, reducing impact applied to the occupant. • A bottle holder which has a storage space of approx. 1.5 L capacity has been adopted to the front door trim. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • A front console box has been adopted which allows storage of small objects such as a Smartphone. Function • Effective vibration and sound absorbing material has been adopted on the front console box to reduce vibration transmitted to small items and noise caused by movement of small items. Construction • The front console box is located in the front console. Fail-safe • Not applicable
