Outline • The High Beam Control (HBC) system performs automatic switching to low beams when the forward sensing camera (FSC) installed to the windshield recognizes a vehicle ahead and when traveling through towns and cities while the vehicle is being driven with the headlights in the high beam position. Due to this, blinding of other vehicles from headlight glare is prevented and driver visibility is assured. Caution • Under the following conditions, the ability of the forward sensing camera (FSC) to detect light-emitting objects decreases, which could result in the system not operating normally and the inability to detect vehicles ahead. ― Brightness of moonlight in surrounding area ― Poor visibility due to rain and fog ― Scratches or dirt on the camera lens or windshield glass • Do not rely solely on the High Beam Control (HBC) system, and perform the appropriate switching operation based on a visual determination of the conditions. • If the forward sensing camera (FSC) aiming is not completed correctly, the forward sensing camera (FSC) cannot record the camera shooting angle and the High Beam Control (HBC) system may not operate normally. When performing the following servicing, always perform the forward sensing camera (FSC) aiming. In addition, for the forward sensing camera (FSC) aiming procedure, refer to the [FORWARD SENSING CAMERA (FSC) AIMING] in the Workshop Manual. ― Forward sensing camera (FSC) replacement ― Forward sensing camera (FSC) clip replacement ― Windshield replacement Function • If the forward sensing camera (FSC) recognizes light-emitting objects (vehicles ahead, street lights (driving in town/city)) while the vehicle is being driven with the light switch in the AUTO and the dimmer switch in the HI position (headlights HI on condition), it automatically switches to low beams. • For details of the forward sensing camera (FSC), refer to the [FORWARD SENSING CAMERA (FSC)]. (See FORWARD SENSING CAMERA (FSC) .) Setting function for control order of precedence • If several light-emitting objects are recognized (vehicles ahead, street lights (driving in town/city)), control is conducted according to the following order of precedence. 1. Closest on-coming vehicle 2. Closest vehicle ahead (no on-coming vehicles) 3. Street lights (driving in town/city) System conditions display function • The forward sensing camera (FSC) displays the system status using the HBC indicator light (green) and HBC warning light (amber) in the instrument cluster, and the warning display on the center display. For the warning display content on the center display, refer to the [CENTER DISPLAY]. (See CENTER DISPLAY [WITH CENTER DISPLAY] .) Condition HBC indicator light (green) HBC warning light (amber) Center display Light switch is in AUTO and dimmer switch is in position other than HI Off Off No display Headlights off While vehicle is stopped System set to off by personalization Light switch is in AUTO and dimmer switch is in HI and headlights turned on On Forward sensing camera (FSC) detects camera fogging Off On Warning display Forward sensing camera (FSC) detects that the camera is dirty Malfunction in HBC occurs Malfunction in forward sensing camera (FSC) occurred Structural View System Wiring Diagram Block Diagram Operation Low beam switching operation • With the light switch in the AUTO position and the dimmer switch in the HI position and when the headlights are turned on, the headlights are switched to low beams when any of the following conditions are met: Operation conditions ― Vehicles ahead, street lights (driving in town/city) are recognized ― Vehicle speed is 20 km/h {12 mph} or less (vehicle speed signal of 20 km/h {12 mph} or less is received) 1. When any of the operation conditions is met, the forward sensing camera (FSC) sends (1) a headlight low beam switching request signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. When the BCM receives the headlight low beam switching request signal, it sends (2) the headlight HI off request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight HI off request signal, it turns the headlights HI off (3). High beam return operation • When the following condition is met, the headlights are switched to high beams. Operation Conditions ― Vehicle speed is 30 km/h {19 mph} or more (vehicle signal of 30 km/h {19 mph} or more is received) and vehicles ahead or street lights (driving in town/city) are not recognized On-coming vehicles 1. When the forward sensing camera (FSC) determines that a recognized on-coming vehicle moves away from the camera range, it sends (1) a headlight high beam switching request signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. When the BCM receives the headlight high beam switching request signal, it sends (2) the headlight HI on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight HI on request signal, it turns the headlights HI on (3). Vehicles ahead or street lights (driving in town/city) 1. If the forward sensing camera (FSC) no longer detect a recognized vehicle ahead moves away from the camera range, or street lights (driving in town/city) in the camera range, it maintains (1) low beams for a certain period of time. 2. If the forward sensing camera (FSC) does not detect vehicles ahead or street lights (driving in town/city) after the certain period of time has elapsed, it sends (2) a headlight high beam switching request signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the headlight high beam switching request signal, it sends (3) the headlight HI on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight HI on request signal, it turns the headlights HI on (4). Forward sensing camera (FSC) loses sight of vehicle ahead which is cornering • If the forward sensing camera (FSC) loses sight of a recognized vehicle which is cornering, the forward sensing camera (FSC) maintains the low beams until reaching the locus at which the forward sensing camera (FSC) lost sight of it. • If the vehicle ahead is not detected at the locus at which the forward sensing camera (FSC) had lost sight of it, the headlights are switched to high beams. If the vehicle ahead is detected, the low beams are maintained. Forward sensing camera (FSC) suddenly loses sight of light-emitting object (vehicles ahead, town/city streets (street lights)) • If the forward sensing camera (FSC) suddenly loses sight of a recognized light-emitting object in the camera range, the low beams are maintained for a certain period of time. • Depending on whether a light-emitting object is detected or not after the certain period of time has elapsed, the headlights are switched to high beams or the system determines that the low beams are to be maintained. Fail-safe • If a malfunction is detected in the system, control is inhibited and the headlights are switched to high beams.

Purpose HBC indicator light (green) • The HBC indicator light (green) notifies the driver that the High Beam Control (HBC) system is operating. HBC warning light (amber) • The HBC warning light (amber) warns the driver that a malfunction is occurring in the High Beam Control (HBC) system. Function HBC indicator light (green) • The instrument cluster turns the HBC indicator light (green) on based on the system conditions display request signal sent via a CAN signal from the forward sensing camera (FSC). HBC warning light (amber) • The instrument cluster turns the HBC warning light (amber) on based on the system conditions display request signal sent via a CAN signal from the forward sensing camera (FSC). • The instrument cluster flashes the HBC warning light (amber) based on the system malfunction display request signal sent via a CAN signal from the forward sensing camera (FSC). • The flash pattern of the HBC warning light (amber) is as indicated in the table. Construction • The HBC indicator light (green) and HBC warning light (amber) are built into the instrument cluster. Operation HBC indicator light (green) 1. When the high beam control (HBC) system operates, the forward sensing camera (FSC) sends (1) a system conditions display request signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) based on the system conditions display request signal. 3. When the transistor turns on, a ground circuit with the HBC indicator light (green) is established, and the HBC indicator light (green) turns on (3). HBC warning light (amber) 1. If there is a malfunction in the high beam control (HBC) system, the forward sensing camera (FSC) sends (1) a system malfunction display request signal or system conditions display request signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) intermittently for a system malfunction display request signal and continuously for a system conditions display request signal. 3. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the HBC warning light (amber) flashes, and when it is turned on continuously, the HBC warning light (amber) turns on (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • When the FLASH-TO-PASS operation is performed with the ignition switched off or ACC, the coming home light system turns on the headlights LO for a specified time after leaving the vehicle. • When leaving the vehicle in a parking lot where the area surrounding the vehicle is dark, the system is used for assuring visibility at the front of the vehicle by turning the headlights LO on. Function • The coming home light system controls the headlights LO using the following two functions: ― Coming home light stand-by function: Turns on the headlights LO until the user gets out of the vehicle after operating the FLASH-TO-PASS. ― Coming home light off timer function: Operates when the user gets out of the vehicle and closes all of the doors while the coming-home-light stand-by function is operating. Coming home light stand-by function • When the BCM receives a FLASH-TO-PASS signal with the ignition switched off or ACC, it turns the headlights LO on. After 3 min have elapsed since going on coming home light stand-by or a FLASH-TO-PASS signal is received during stand-by, the BCM turns the headlights LO off. Coming home light off timer function • The BCM operates the coming home light off timer at the point in time the following conditions occur: ― Off signals for all door latch switches (doors closed) are detected after detecting any on signal for the door latch switches (door open) while on coming home light stand-by. ― When any on signal for the door latch switches (door open) is detected, it goes on coming home light stand-by, and then off signals for all door latch switches (doors closed) are detected. • After the coming home light off timer has elapsed, the BCM turns the headlights LO off. Personalization features • The coming home light off timer setting for the coming home light system can be changed (initial setting is 30 s ). For details on the personalization features, refer to the [LIGHTING SYSTEM PERSONALIZATION]. (See LIGHTING SYSTEM PERSONALIZATION .) Structural View System Wiring Diagram Timing chart Operation Coming home light stand-by operation • When a FLASH-TO-PASS signal (light switch signal) is received with all of the following conditions met, it goes on coming home light stand-by. Coming home light stand-by operation conditions ― IG1 relay is off (ignition is switched off or ACC) ― Coming home light off timer (personalization setting) not set at 0 s (OFF) 1. When the light switch is moved to the FLASH-TO-PASS position, the start stop unit detects (1) a FLASH-TO-PASS signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the FLASH-TO-PASS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the FLASH-TO-PASS signal with all operation conditions met, it sends (3) a headlight LO on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU). 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight LO on request signal, it turns the headlights LO on (4) and goes on coming home light stand-by. Coming home light off timer operation • When the following condition is met while on coming home light stand-by, the coming home light off timer operates. Coming home light off timer operation condition ― All off signals for the door latch switches (doors closed) are detected after detecting any on signal for the door latch switches (door open). 1. When the BCM detects (1) all off signals for the door latch switches (doors closed) after detecting any on signal for the door latch switches (door open) during coming home light stand-by, it operates (2) the coming home light off timer. 2. After the coming home light off timer has elapsed, the BCM stops the headlight LO on request signal. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) no longer receives the headlight LO on request signal, it turns the headlights LO off (3).

When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight LO on request signal, it turns the headlights LO on (4). 5. Outline • Front combination lights have been adopted with parts related to the front exterior lights grouped and housed together. • The following systems have been adopted to the headlights. ― Auto light system (With auto light system) ― Headlight manual leveling system (With headlight manual leveling system) ― Headlight auto leveling system (With headlight auto leveling system) ― Running light system (With running light system) ― High beam control (HBC) system (With high beam control (HBC) system) ― Coming home light system ― Leaving home light system • LEDs have been adopted for the following lights: ― Headlight (front combination light (LED type)) ― Parking light/running light (front combination light (LED type)) ― Brake light/taillight (rear combination light (LED type)) ― Side turn light ― High-mount brake light • Front fog lights have been adopted. Purpose Bulb type • The front combination light groups and houses together the parts related to the front exterior lights such as the headlight, parking light, front turn light, headlight leveling actuator (with headlight manual leveling system), wiring harnesses, and connectors. LED type • The front combination light groups and houses together the parts related to the front exterior lights such as the headlight, parking light, front turn light, headlight leveling actuator, wiring harnesses, and connectors. • Energy consumption reduction and maintenance-free design been achieved with the adoption of LEDs on the headlights LO and HI. • Visibility of road signs positioned higher up has been improved by blurring the cut lines of the headlights between light and dark to the extent possible. • Visibility of pedestrians and roadside zones has been improved by expanding the light distribution of the headlights. Function • Each light turns on or flashes when the light switch, turn switch, or hazard warning switch is operated. Construction • A bulb type or LED type is available for the front combination light. Bulb type • The front combination light groups the following parts: ― Headlight HI/LO bulb ― Parking light bulb (without running light system) ― Parking light/running light bulb (with running light system) ― Front turn light bulb • The front combination light is integrated with the headlight leveling actuator. (with headlight manual leveling system) Note • Fogging or condensation may occur inside the front combination lights, however, it is a natural phenomenon occurring as a result of a temperature difference between the interior and exterior of the front combination lights and it does not affect the light performance. • Fogging or condensation occurring as a natural phenomenon will dissipate when the temperature inside the front combination lights rises after the headlights are turned on and a period of time has elapsed. LED type • The front combination light groups the front turn light bulb. • The front combination light is integrated with the following parts: ― Headlight LO (LED) ― Headlight HI (LED) ― Parking light/running light (LED) ― Headlight leveling actuator • A projector type headlight has been adopted to the headlight LO. • Heat generated by the illumination of the LEDs is absorbed and dispersed by the heat radiation plates installed to the back of the headlight LO and HI reflectors. Note • Fogging or condensation may occur inside the front combination lights, however, it is a natural phenomenon occurring as a result of a temperature difference between the interior and exterior of the front combination lights and it does not affect the light performance. • Fogging or condensation occurring as a natural phenomenon will dissipate when the temperature inside the front combination lights rises after the headlights are turned on and a period of time has elapsed. • The optimized shape of the headlight LO and HI reflectors emits light over a wide area. Operation Headlight LO 1. When the light switch is moved to the HEAD position and the dimmer switch is moved to the LO position, the start stop unit detects (1) a TNS signal and headlight LO signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the TNS signal and headlight LO signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the TNS signal and headlight LO signal with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), it sends (3) a TNS illumination request signal and headlight LO illumination request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS illumination request signal and headlight LO illumination request signal, it turns the TNS and headlight LO on (4). Headlight HI 1. When the light switch is moved to the HEAD position and the dimmer switch is moved to the HI position, the start stop unit detects (1) a headlight HI signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the headlight HI signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the headlight HI signal with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), it sends (3) a headlight HI illumination request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight HI illumination request signal, it turns the headlights HI on (4). Flash-to-pass 1. When the dimmer switch is moved to the FLASH-TO-PASS position, the start stop unit detects (1) a FLASH-TO-PASS signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the FLASH-TO-PASS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the FLASH-TO-PASS signal with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), it sends (3) headlight LO and HI illumination request signals to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the headlight LO and HI illumination request signals, it turns the headlights LO and HI on (4). Parking light 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS position, the start stop unit detects (1) a TNS signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the TNS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the TNS signal, it sends (3) a TNS illumination request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS illumination request signal, it turns the parking lights on (4). Front turn light Turn light system 1. When the turn switch is moved to the LH or RH position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) a turn switch LH or RH signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the turn switch LH or RH signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH or RH signal. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH or RH signal, it flashes (3) the front turn light (LH) or (RH). Hazard warning system 1. When the hazard warning switch is turned on (1), the start stop unit detects (2) a hazard warning switch on signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (3) the hazard warning switch on signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH and RH signal. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH and RH signal, it flashes (4) the front turn lights (LH) and (RH). Headlight leveling actuator • Refer to the [HEADLIGHT LEVELING ACTUATOR]. (See HEADLIGHT LEVELING ACTUATOR .) Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The auto light system automatically turns the TNS, headlight LO, and panel light on/off according to the illumination level above and in front of the vehicle. Function • The BCM sends each light on/off request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) based on the signal from the auto light sensor and the electrical supply unit (ESU) turns each light on/off. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Note • When the ignition is switched ON (engine on or off), the auto light sensor detects the illumination level above and in front of the vehicle regardless of the light switch position. • The auto light system operates when the ignition is switched ON (engine on or off) and the light switch is in the AUTO position. • The following illumination level is a reference. The illumination level varies depending on the surrounding conditions (weather, reflection off buildings). • The illumination level sensitivity of the auto light sensor can be changed. The illumination level in the explanation for the following operations is the value when setting to [Standard (All Others)]. (See LIGHTING SYSTEM PERSONALIZATION .) Panel light on operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the AUTO position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) an auto light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the auto light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the auto light sensor detects (3) the average 700 lux or less per 1 min for upward illumination, it sends (4) a panel light illumination request signal to the BCM via LIN communication. 4. When the BCM receives the auto light signal and panel light illumination request signal, it sends (5) the panel light illumination request signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 5. When the instrument cluster receives the panel light illumination request signal, it turns the panel light on (6). Panel light off operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the AUTO position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) an auto light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the auto light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the auto light sensor detects (3) the average 1,400 lux or more per 1 min for upward illumination, it sends (4) a panel light off request signal to the BCM via LIN communication. 4. When the BCM receives the auto light signal and panel light off request signal, it sends (5) the panel light off request signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 5. When the instrument cluster receives the panel light off request signal, it turns the panel light off (6). Headlight LO on operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the AUTO position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) an auto light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the auto light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the auto light sensor detects (3) the average 2,000 lux or less per 1 min for upward illumination, it sends (4) a TNS and headlight LO illumination request signal to the BCM via LIN communication. 4. When the BCM receives the auto light signal, TNS and headlight LO illumination request signal, it sends (5) the TNS and headlight LO illumination request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS and headlight LO illumination request signal, it turns the TNS and headlights LO on (6). Headlight LO off operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the AUTO position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) an auto light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the auto light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the auto light sensor detects (3) the average 4,000 lux or more per 1 min for upward illumination, it sends (4) a TNS and headlight LO off request signal to the BCM via LIN communication. 4. When the BCM receives the auto light signal, TNS and headlight LO off request signal, it sends (5) the TNS and headlight LO off request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 5. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS and headlight LO off request signal, it turns the TNS and headlights LO off (6).

Purpose • The auto light sensor detects the illumination level above and in front of the vehicle and outputs it to the BCM. Function • The auto light sensor uses the upward illumination level sensor to detect the illumination level above the vehicle, and uses the forward illumination level sensor to detect the illumination level in front of the vehicle. Illumination level adjustment function • The illumination level sensitivity can be switched between 5 levels using the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS) or center display (with center display). (See LIGHTING SYSTEM PERSONALIZATION .) On-board diagnostic function • If there is a malfunction in the auto light sensor, notifies the BCM and outputs a DTC from the BCM. • For details on DTCs, refer to the DTC table [ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM [BODY CONTROL MODULE (BCM)]]. (See ON-BOARD DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM [BODY CONTROL MODULE (BCM)] .) Construction • The auto light sensor is integrated with the rain sensor as a single unit. • The auto light sensor consists of the lens, upward illumination level sensor (photodiode), forward illumination level sensor (photodiode), and microcomputer. Operation Caution • The auto light sensor cannot detect the illumination level correctly under the following conditions, which could cause the auto light system to operate improperly. ― Stickers or labels are attached to the auto light sensor detection area on the windshield. ― The auto light sensor detection area on the windshield is dirty. 1. When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on), the auto light sensor detects (1) the illumination level above and in front of the vehicle. 2. The auto light sensor outputs (2) a panel light or TNS and headlight LO illumination request signal and panel light or TNS and headlight LO off request signal to the BCM via LIN communication according to the detected illumination level. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Changes the resistance value according to the position the headlight leveling switch has been changed. Function • The position of the headlight leveling switch can be switched between 11 levels: 0—5. Construction • The headlight leveling switch is integrated with the cluster switch. Operation 1. When the headlight leveling switch is turned (1) upward, the resistance value in the switch decreases (2). When the switch is turned (3) downward, the resistance value in the switch increases (4). 2. The headlight leveling switch applies (5) current to the headlight leveling actuator, which flows according to the position the switch is switched to. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The headlight auto leveling system automatically adjusts the headlight LO optical axis in response to changes in load and passenger conditions to prevent blinding of oncoming vehicles from headlight glare and to assure a range of visibility. Function • The headlight auto leveling system is controlled by the auto leveling control module. Optical axis adjustment function • If there is a vehicle height change with the ignition switched ON (engine on or off) and the headlights LO turned on, the auto leveling control module automatically adjusts the headlight LO optical axis. • The auto leveling control module controls the optical axis adjustment function based on the following signals. Signal name Sending module/part name Communication method Vehicle speed signal PCM HS-CAN Ignition switch position signal Instrument cluster Headlight LO on condition signal BCM Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation Vehicle height changes while vehicle is stopped Operation conditions • Operates when all of the following conditions are met: ― Vehicle speed is 0 km/h {0 mph} ( 0 km/h {0 mph} vehicle speed signal is received) ― Ignition is switched ON (engine off or on) (ignition switch status signal (ON) is received) ― Headlights LO on (headlight LO on condition signal reception) ― Detects change in vehicle height amount * at specified value or more Operation 1. When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on), the auto leveling sensor sends (1) a vehicle height signal to the auto leveling control module. 2. When the auto leveling control module receives (2) a headlight LO on condition signal from the BCM via CAN communication, it calculates (3) the amount of change in the vehicle height * based on the vehicle height signal. 3. When the auto leveling control module detects (4) the amount of change in the vehicle height * at the specified value or more, it calculates the target optical axis (5) based on the calculated amount of change in the vehicle height * . 4. The auto leveling control module sends (6) the calculated target optical axis signal to the headlight leveling actuator. 5. When the target optical axis signal is received, the headlight leveling actuator drives (7) the motor. * :The change in the amount of vehicle height is the calculated 1 s average value of the vehicle height signal which the auto leveling control module detects every 0.1 s . Vehicle height changes while vehicle is moving Operation conditions • Operates when all of the following conditions are met: ― Vehicle speed is 30 km/h {19 mph} or more (vehicle speed signal of 30 km/h {19 mph} or more is received) ― Headlight LO on (headlight LO on condition signal reception) ― Detects change in vehicle speed of 3 km/h {2 mph} or less for continuous period of 25 s ― Detects change in vehicle height amount * at specified value or more Operation 1. The auto leveling sensor sends (1) a vehicle height signal to the auto leveling control module while the vehicle is being driven. 2. When the auto leveling control module receives (2) a headlight LO on condition signal from the BCM via CAN communication, it calculates (3) the amount of change in the vehicle height * based on the vehicle height signal. 3. When the auto leveling control module detects (4) the vehicle speed of 30 km/h {19 mph} or more , change in vehicle speed of 3 km/h {2 mph} or less for a continuous 25 s , and the change in the amount of vehicle height * at the specified value or more, it calculates (5) the target optical axis based on the calculated change in the amount of vehicle height * . 4. The auto leveling control module sends (6) the calculated target optical axis signal to the headlight leveling actuator. 5. When the target optical axis signal is received, the headlight leveling actuator drives (7) the motor. * :The change in the amount of vehicle height is the calculated 1 s average value of the vehicle height signal which the auto leveling control module detects every 0.1 s .

Purpose • The auto leveling control module calculates the target optical axis based on the vehicle height signal from the auto leveling sensor and outputs the target optical axis signal to the headlight leveling actuator. Function • The auto leveling control module controls the headlight auto leveling system and detects a malfunction in the headlight (LED type) circuit. Vehicle height record function while vehicle is unoccupied • When the auto leveling control module performs the headlight auto leveling system initial setting, it inputs the vehicle height from the auto leveling sensor and records the vehicle height while the vehicle is unoccupied. • The vehicle height in the unloaded condition recorded by the auto leveling control module is not cleared even if the battery is disconnected. Automatic configuration function • When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on) after the auto leveling control module is replaced, the auto leveling control module reads the vehicle specification information sent via CAN communication from the instrument cluster, and stores the vehicle specification information. On-board diagnostic function • The auto leveling control module is equipped with an on-board diagnosis function which records DTCs in the event of a malfunction. Malfunction detection function • The auto leveling control module detects a malfunction of the headlight auto leveling system related parts. • The auto leveling control module detects a malfunction in the headlight (LED type) circuit based on the circuit for the malfunction detection equipped in the front combination light. Display function • If any malfunction is detected, the LED headlight warning light in the instrument cluster flashes to notify the driver of a system malfunction. Burnt out bulb check function • When the ignition is switched ON (engine off or on), the auto leveling control module turns the LED headlight warning light on for approx. 3 s and performs a burnt out bulb check. Construction • The auto leveling control module is located inside the dashboard. Purpose • The auto leveling sensor detects the vehicle height and outputs it to the auto leveling control module. Function • The auto leveling sensor changes the detected vehicle height into a voltage value and outputs it to the auto leveling control module. Construction • The auto leveling sensor is located on the rear shock absorber and rear side frame. • The auto leveling sensor consists of link No. 1, link No.2, and the Hall sensor. Operation 1. Purpose, Function Vehicles with headlight manual leveling system • The headlight leveling actuator drives the motor and changes the headlight LO optical axis using current which flows according to the position to which the headlight leveling switch is switched. Vehicles with headlight auto leveling system • The headlight leveling actuator drives the motor based on the target optical axis voltage, which is input from the auto leveling control module, to change the headlight LO optical axis. Construction • The headlight leveling actuator is integrated with the front combination lights. • The headlight leveling actuator consists of a motor which expands/contracts the shaft, a shaft, and a microcomputer which calculates the shaft expansion/contraction amount. Operation Vehicle with headlight manual leveling system 1. The headlight leveling actuator calculates the motor drive amount based on the current (1) which flows according to the position the headlight leveling switch is switched to, and it drives (2) the motor until the optical axis reaches the target optical axis. 2. When the motor is driven, the shaft moves (3) back and forth and the reflector moves to change (4) the optical axis. Vehicles with headlight auto leveling system 1. The headlight leveling actuator calculates the motor drive amount based on the target optical axis signal (1) from the auto leveling control module and drives (2) the motor until the optical axis reaches the target optical axis. 2. When the motor is driven, the shaft moves (3) back and forth and the reflector moves to change (4) the optical axis. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • Visibility during poor weather conditions such as rain and fog has been improved by the front fog lights emitting light over a wider angle than the light from the headlights. In addition, the visibility of the vehicle by on-coming vehicles, pedestrians, and other people has been improved. Function • When the BCM receives the front fog light signal sent via CAN communication from the start stop unit, it turns the front fog lights on. Construction • The front fog lights are positioned in the front bumper. • Round-type front fog lights have been adopted. Operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS or HEAD position and the fog light switch is moved to the F.FOG position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) a front fog light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the front fog light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the front fog light signal, it turns the front fog light relay on (3). 4. When the front fog light relay turns on, the front fog light turns on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

The start stop unit sends (2) the turn switch LH or RH signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH or RH signal. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH or RH signal, it flashes the side turn light (LH) or (RH). Hazard warning system 1. When the hazard warning switch is on (1), the start stop unit detects (2) a hazard warning switch on signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (3) the hazard warning switch on signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH and RH signals. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH and RH signals, it flashes (4) the side turn lights (LH) and (RH). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Outline • The emergency signal system (ESS) warns the driver of a vehicle following behind of an emergency braking situation by automatically and rapidly flashing the hazard warning lights when the vehicle decelerates suddenly while traveling at high speeds. Function • The BCM gives priority to the emergency signal system (ESS) operation even if the turn switch signal is received during the emergency signal system (ESS) operation. • When the BCM receives a hazard warning switch on signal during the emergency signal system (ESS) operation, it stops the emergency signal system (ESS) operation and gives priority to the hazard warning light flashing operation. • The BCM controls the emergency signal system (ESS) based on the following signals: Signal name Sending module/part name Communication method Vehicle speed signal PCM HS-CAN Brake switch condition signal Wheel speed (LF, RF, LR, RR) signal DSC HU/CM ABS operation condition signal Vehicle acceleration speed signal Turn switch signal Start stop unit Hazard warning switch signal • The emergency signal system (ESS) has two warning modes; the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode in which the hazard warning lights flash rapidly, and the emergency stop hazard warning mode in which the hazard warning lights flash normally. Sudden deceleration hazard warning mode • The sudden deceleration hazard warning mode operates when the brake pedal is depressed while driving at a vehicle speed of 60 km/h {37 mph} or more and emergency braking is determined based on the vehicle's deceleration. • When the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode operates the hazard warning lights flash at 3.5 Hz . Emergency stop hazard warning mode • When the brake pedal is depressed at a vehicle speed of 10 km/h {6.2 mph} or less after the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode operates, the modes switches to the emergency stop hazard warning mode. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation 1. If the brake pedal is depressed and the vehicle is decelerated while the vehicle is driven, the BCM calculates (1) the vehicle deceleration speed based on the wheel speed signal and the vehicle acceleration speed signal. 2. If the vehicle speed is approx. 60 km/h {37 mph} or more when the calculation is finished, and the calculated deceleration speed is the set value or more for the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode (2), the BCM controls (3) the flashing of the hazard warning lights at 3.5 Hz (sudden deceleration hazard warning mode) and sends (4) a turn signal to the instrument cluster simultaneously. 3. The BCM stops (6) the operation of the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode if it receives (5) a brake switch off (brake pedal not depressed) signal or if the estimated deceleration value is the set value or less for stopping the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode. 4. When the BCM receives (7) a brake switch on (brake pedal depressed) signal at a vehicle speed of 10 km/h {6.2 mph} or less after the sudden deceleration hazard warning mode operates, it controls (8) the flashing of the hazard warning lights at 1.5 Hz (same as normal flashing) (emergency stop hazard warning mode). 5. When the BCM receives the brake switch off (brake pedal not depressed) signal and vehicle speed signal and determines that the vehicle has started, it stops the operation of the emergency stop hazard warning mode and turns the hazard warning lights off. Prevention of emergency signal system (ESS) unnecessary operation • If the braking force inspection is performed, unnecessary operation of the emergency signal system (ESS) can be prevented if necessary. • The operation of the emergency signal system (ESS) can be canceled by performing the procedure for preventing unnecessary operation of the brake override system. For the procedure to prevent unnecessary operation of the brake override system, refer to the [DRIVE-BY-WIRE CONTROL]/[FUEL INJECTION AMOUNT CONTROL]. (See DRIVE-BY-WIRE CONTROL [SKYACTIV-G 1.3, SKYACTIV-G 1.5] .) (See FUEL INJECTION AMOUNT CONTROL [SKYACTIV-D 1.5] .)

Purpose • The rear combination lights are used to signal the following conditions to vehicles/people at the rear. ― Rear turn lights: Signals a left or right turn of the vehicle. ― Brake lights: Signals a vehicle deceleration or stop. ― Taillights: Signals the presence of the vehicle to vehicles/people at the rear during nighttime. Function • The BCM turns each light on or flashes each light based on each switch signal. Operation switch Related light Operation status Light switch (TNS) Taillight On Brake switch Brake light On Turn switch Rear turn light Flash Hazard warning switch Construction • The rear combination light groups the following parts: ― Rear turn light bulb ― Brake light/taillight bulb (rear combination light (bulb type)) • The rear combination light is integrated with the brake light/taillight (LED). (Rear combination light (LED type)) • LEDs have been adopted for the brake light/taillight. (Rear combination light (LED type)) Note • Fogging or condensation on the inside of the rear combination lights may occur, however, it is a natural phenomenon occurring as a result of a temperature difference between the interior and exterior of the combination lights and it does not affect the light performance. • Fogging or condensation occurring as a natural phenomenon will dissipate when the temperature inside the rear combination lights rises after the rear turn lights are turned on and a period of time has elapsed. Operation Taillight 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS or HEAD position, the start stop unit detects (1) a TNS signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the TNS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the TNS signal, it sends (3) the TNS on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS on request signal, it turns the taillights on (4). Brake light Operation due to brake pedal operation Vehicles without smart city brake support (SCBS) 1. When the brake pedal is depressed, the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on (1). 2. When the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on, the brake lights are turned on (2). Vehicles with smart city brake support (SCBS) 1. When the brake pedal is depressed, the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on (1). 2. When the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on while the smart city brake support (SCBS) is not operating, the brake light turns on (2). Operation due to operation request signal from BCM Note • For the operation conditions, refer to the [SMART CITY BRAKE SUPPORT (SCBS)]. (See SMART CITY BRAKE SUPPORT (SCBS) .) 1. When all the operation conditions are met, the BCM turns the transistor on (1) in the BCM. 2. When the transistor in the BCM turns on, the brake light relay turns on (2). 3. When the brake light relay turns on, the brake lights turns on (3). Rear turn light Turn light system 1. When the turn switch is moved to the LH or RH position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) a turn switch LH or RH signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the turn switch LH or RH signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH or RH signal. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH or RH signal, it flashes (3) the rear turn light (LH) or (RH). Hazard warning system 1. When the hazard warning switch is on (1), the start stop unit detects (2) a hazard warning switch on signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (3) the hazard warning switch on signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH and RH signals. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH and RH signals, it flashes (4) the rear turn lights (LH) and (RH). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The high-mount brake light signals vehicles to the rear that the vehicle is decelerated or stopping. Function • The high-mount brake light turns on in conjunction with the operation of the brake switch. Construction • The high-mount brake light is positioned on the rear package trim (4SD)/rear spoiler (5HB). • LEDs have been adopted for the high-mount brake light. Note • Fogging or condensation on the inside of the high-mount brake light may occur, however, it is a natural phenomenon occurring as a result of a temperature difference between the interior and exterior of the high-mount brake light and it does not affect the light performance. • Fogging or condensation occurring as a natural phenomenon will dissipate when the temperature inside the high-mount brake light rises after the high-mount brake light is turned on and a period of time has elapsed. Operation Operation due to brake pedal operation Vehicles without smart city brake support (SCBS) 1. When the brake pedal is depressed, the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on (1). 2. When the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on, the high-mount brake light turns on (2). Vehicles with smart city brake support (SCBS) 1. When the brake pedal is depressed, the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on (1). 2. When the brake switch (No.1 signal) turns on, the high-mount brake light turns on (2). Operation due to operation request signal from BCM Note • For the operation condition, refer to the [SMART CITY BRAKE SUPPORT (SCBS)]. (See SMART CITY BRAKE SUPPORT (SCBS) .) 1. When all the operation conditions are met, the BCM turns the transistor on (1) in the BCM. 2. When the transistor in the BCM turns on, the brake light relay turns on (2). 3. When the brake light relay turns on, the high-mount brake light turns on (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The license plate light turns on when the light switch is moved to the TNS or HEAD position. Function • The electrical supply unit (ESU) turns the license plate light on based on the TNS on request signal sent via CAN communication from the BCM. Construction • The license plate light is positioned on the trunk lid (4SD)/rear bumper (5HB). Operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS or HEAD position, the start stop unit detects (1) a TNS signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the TNS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the TNS signal, it sends (3) the TNS on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the TNS on request signal, it turns the license plate light on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The cargo compartment light illuminates the cargo room interior when the liftgate is opened. Function • When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives a cargo compartment light on request signal from the BCM, the cargo compartment light turns on by turning the cargo compartment light switch on. Construction • The cargo compartment light is positioned on the trunk side trim. Operation 1. When the liftgate is opened, the liftgate latch switch is on (1) and the BCM detects (2) a liftgate latch switch on signal. 2. When the BCM detects the liftgate latch switch on signal, it sends (3) the cargo compartment light on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the cargo compartment light on request signal, it turns the transistor on (4). 4. When the cargo compartment switch is on (5), the cargo compartment light bulb turns on (6). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The lights-on indicator light notifies the driver that the TNS is turned on. Function • When the instrument cluster receives the TNS signal sent from the BCM via CAN communication, it turns the lights-on indicator light on. Construction • The lights-on indicator light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS position, the start stop unit sends (1) a TNS signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. The BCM sends (2) the TNS signal to the instrument cluster. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) based on the TNS signal. 4. When the transistor turns on, a ground circuit with the lights-on indicator light is established and the lights-on indicator light turns on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The headlight high-beam indicator light notifies the driver that the headlights HI are turned on. Function • When the instrument cluster receives the headlight HI signal sent from the BCM via CAN communication, it turns the headlight high-beam indicator light on. Construction • The headlight high-beam indicator light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. When the light switch is moved to any of the following positions, the start stop unit sends (1) a headlight HI signal to the BCM via CAN communication. ― Light switch at HEAD position and dimmer switch at HI position ― Dimmer switch at FLASH-TO-PASS position 2. When the BCM receives the headlight HI signal with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), it sends (2) a headlight HI signal to the instrument cluster. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) based on the headlight HI signal. 4. When the transistor turns on, a ground circuit with the headlight high-beam indicator light is established, and the headlight high-beam indicator light turns on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The rear fog light indicator light notifies the driver that the rear fog light is turned on. Functions • When the instrument cluster receives a rear fog light signal sent from the BCM via CAN communication, it turns the rear fog light indicator light on. Construction • The rear fog light indicator light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. When the fog light switch is turned to the R.FOG position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on) and headlight LO or HI signal received, the start stop unit sends (1) a rear fog light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. The BCM sends (2) the rear fog light signal to the instrument cluster. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) based on the rear fog light signal. 4. When the transistor is turned on, the rear fog light indicator light ground circuit is established and the rear fog light indicator light turns on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The rear fog light enhances the visibility of the vehicle from vehicle rear during poor weather conditions such as rain and fog. Functions • When the BCM receives a rear fog light signal sent via CAN communication from the start stop unit, it turns the rear fog light on. Construction • The rear fog light is located on the rear bumper. Operation 1. When the fog light switch is turned to R.FOG position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on) and the headlight LO or HI signal received, the start stop unit detects (1) a rear fog light signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the rear fog light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 3. When the BCM receives the rear fog light signal, it sends (3) a rear fog light on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the rear fog light on request signal, it turns the rear fog light on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Construction • The LED headlight warning light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. When the auto leveling control module detects the headlight auto leveling system non-initialization, headlight auto leveling system malfunction, or LED headlight malfunction, it sends (1) a headlight auto leveling system non-initialization signal or headlight auto leveling system malfunction signal/LED headlight malfunction signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 2. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (2) intermittently based on each signal. 3. When the transistor turns on intermittently, the LED headlight warning light flashes (3). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The front fog light indicator light notifies the driver that the front fog lights are turned on. Function • When the instrument cluster receives the front fog light signal sent from the BCM via CAN communication, it turns the front fog light indicator light on. Construction • The front fog light indicator light is built into the instrument cluster. Operation 1. When the light switch is moved to the TNS position and the fog light switch is moved to the F.FOG position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit sends (1) a front fog light signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. The BCM sends (2) the front fog light signal to the instrument cluster. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) based on the front fog light signal. 4. When the transistor turns on, a ground circuit with the front fog light indicator light is established, and the front fog light indicator light turns on (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The direction indicator/hazard warning indicator lights notify the driver that the turn lights are flashing. Function • When the instrument cluster receives a turn signal or hazard warning indicator signal sent from the BCM via CAN communication, it flashes the direction indicator/hazard warning indicator lights. Construction • The direction indicator/hazard warning indicator lights are built into the instrument cluster. Operation Turn light system 1. When the turn switch is moved to the LH or RH position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit sends (1) a turn switch LH or RH signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. The BCM sends (2) the turn switch LH or RH signal to the instrument cluster as a turn signal. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) intermittently based on the turn signal. 4. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the direction indicator light flashes (4). Hazard warning system 1. When the hazard warning switch is turned on, the start stop unit sends (1) a hazard warning switch on signal to the BCM via CAN communication. 2. The BCM sends (2) the hazard warning switch on signal to the instrument cluster as a hazard warning indicator signal. 3. The instrument cluster turns the transistor on (3) intermittently based on the hazard warning indicator signal. 4. When the transistor is turned on intermittently, the hazard warning indicator lights flash (4). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The turn light system controls the turn lights to flash according to the turn switch operation. Function • The BCM performs control as follows based on the turn light RH or LH signal sent from the start stop unit via CAN communication. ― Period of time turn switch on signal is received is less than 0.7 s : Controls the turn lights to flash three times automatically ― Period of time turn switch on signal is received is 0.7 s or more : Controls the turn lights to flash according to the reception period Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation 1. When the turn switch is moved to the LH or RH position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the start stop unit detects (1) a turn switch LH or RH signal. 2. The start stop unit sends (2) the turn switch LH or RH signal to the BCM via CAN communication as a turn light LH or RH signal. 3. When the BCM receives the turn light LH or RH signal, it flashes (3) the front turn light (LH) or (RH). 4. When the BCM receives the turn light LH or RH signal from the start stop unit for less than 0.7 s , it flashes the turn light (LH) or (RH) three times automatically. 5. When the BCM receives a turn light signal for the opposite side while the turn light (RH) or (LH) is flashing three times automatically, it cancels the current automatic flashing. However, when the BCM receives the turn light signal for the opposite side for 0.2 s or more , it flashes the turn light while the turn light signal is being received.

Purpose, Function • The steering angle sensor detects the steering angle and sends it to the start stop unit as a steering angle (absolute steering angle) signal. Note • The steering angle sensor is installed to vehicles with the smart city brake support (SCBS). Construction • The steering angle sensor is located on the clock spring. • Consists of a sensor unit in which a photo transistor and LED are positioned opposite each other, and a slit disc which moves together with the steering wheel. Operation 1. As the disc moves with the steering wheel operation, the LED light received by the photo transistor varies due to the slits on the disc. 2. The photo transistor reads the variation of the light and outputs the steering angle (absolute steering angle) signal to the start stop unit. Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The front map lights illuminate the area at the front of the vehicle interior. Function • When the front map light switch is on or the room light switch is in the ON position, the front map lights turn on. • The front map lights turn on according to the lock condition of the driver's door and open/close conditions of the doors under the BCM control when the room light switch is in the DOOR position. Construction • The front map light is positioned in the front part of the headliner. Operation Front map light switch operation 1. When the front map light switch is on (1), the front map light turns on (2). Room light switch operation ON position 1. When the room light switch is in the ON position (1), the front map lights turn on (2). Note • When the BCM receives a lock signal on the remote transmitter with the ignition switched off and all doors/ trunk lid (4SD)/liftgate (5HB) closed, it automatically turns the front map light off. DOOR position 1. When any door is opened (2) with the room light switch at the DOOR position (1), the BCM detects (3) a door open signal. 2. When the BCM detects the door open signal, it sends (4) the front map light on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 3. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the front map light on request signal, it turns the transistor on (5). 4. When the transistor is on, the front map lights turn on (6). Note • When the room light switch is in the DOOR position, the room light control system controls the timing for turning the front map light on and off. For details, refer to the [ROOM LIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM]. (See ROOM LIGHT CONTROL SYSTEM .) Fail-safe • Not applicable

Purpose • The rear map light illuminates the center of the vehicle interior. Function • When the room light switch for the front map light is in the ON position, the rear map light turns on. • The rear map light turns on according to the lock condition of the driver's door and open/close conditions of the doors under the BCM control when the room light switch for front map light is in the DOOR position. Construction • The rear map light is positioned in the center part of the headliner. Operation Room light switch for front map light operation ON position 1. DOOR position 1. When any door is opened (2) with the room light switch for the front map light in the DOOR position (1), the BCM detects (3) a door open signal. 2. Outline • The headlight manual leveling system changes the headlight LO optical axis according to the operation of the headlight leveling switch to prevent driver dazzle from the headlight glare of oncoming vehicles and to assure a range of visibility. Function • When the headlight leveling switch is turned upward, the headlight LO optical axis moves upward. When the switch is turned downward, the axis moves downward. Structural View System Wiring Diagram Operation 1. When the headlight leveling switch is operated (1) with the headlights LO turned on, the resistance value changes according to the changed position, and electric current flows (2) to the headlight leveling actuator. 2. When electric current flows to the headlight leveling actuator, the motor inside the actuator operates (3) and the headlight LO optical axis changes (4).

Note • If the following servicing is done, perform the headlight aiming adjustment. ― Front combination light replacement ― Suspension replacement and removal/installation, servicing requiring vehicle height to be changed • If servicing was done which changes the vehicle height, perform the headlight auto leveling system initial setting first to record the vehicle height under the unloaded condition to the auto leveling control module, then perform headlight aiming. (With headlight auto leveling system) (See HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM INITIALIZATION .) • For the headlight (bulb type), perform the aiming adjustment on the low beams only because the same bulb is used for the low and high beams. • For the headlight (LED type), perform the aiming adjustment on the low beams only because the reflectors of the low and high beams operate together. • When using a aiming tester, set the percentage inclination value (tilt angle) to 1.0 % and follow the instructions of the aiming tester manufacturer. 1. Empty the vehicle except for the spare tire, jack and vehicle tools. 2. Adjust the tire pressure to the specification. (See WHEEL AND TIRE SPECIFICATION .) 3. Move the vehicle to level ground. 4. Sit on the driver-side seat alone. 5. Make an adjustment-use screen as shown in the figure using double-weight, white paper. 6. Line up the vehicle with the wall so that the distance to the headlights is 3 m {118 in} from the wall. 7. Measure the height at the center point of the headlight. Note • Measure the height at the center point of the headlight in which the aiming is being adjusted because the vehicle height differs depending on vehicle conditions. 8. Align the center of the headlight to be adjusted with the center of the headlight on the adjustment screen. 9. Set a partition in front of the headlight which is not being adjusted to block the light. 10. Start the engine and charge the battery. 11. Set the headlight leveling switch to the [0] position. (With headlight manual leveling system) 12. Turn on the headlight low beams. Note • For the LED type, if the headlight low beams are turned on, the light as shown in the figure is emitted to the adjustment screen. 13. Cover the upper part of the headlight with a clean rag so that the brightness border line becomes transparent. (Headlight (LED type)) Note • If the headlight is covered with a clean rag from the upper part of the headlight in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure, the yellow line disappears and the brightness border line becomes transparent. 14. Verify that the actual elbow point of the headlight is at the elbow point position indicated by the adjustment-use screen. • If the actual elbow point of the headlight is not at the elbow point position indicated by the adjustment-use screen, adjust by turning the aiming adjustment screw.

Adjust the tire pressure to the specification. (See WHEEL AND TIRE SPECIFICATION .) 3. Move the vehicle to level ground. 4. Sit on the driver-side seat alone. 5. Make an adjustment-use screen as shown in the figure using double-weight, white paper. (Common to both left and right) 6. Line up the vehicle with the wall so that the distance to the front fog lights is 3 m {118 in} from the wall. 7. Measure the height at the center point of the front fog lights. Note • Measure the height at the center point of the front fog light in which the aiming is being adjusted because the vehicle height differs depending on vehicle conditions. 8. Align the center of the front fog light to be adjusted with the center of the front fog light on the adjustment screen. 9. Set a partition in front of the front fog light which is not being adjusted to block the light. 10. Start the engine and charge the battery. 11. Turn on the front fog lights. 12. Verify that the actual brightness borderline of the fog light is at the brightness borderline position indicated by the adjustment-use screen. • If the actual brightness borderline is not in the position indicated on the adjustment-use screen, perform the following adjustment: (1) Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) (2) Partially peel back the front mudguard. (See MUDGUARD REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (3) Remove the front fog light before cutting the front fog light hole cover located on the bolt installation hole. (See FRONT FOG LIGHT REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (4) Cutout the hatch-marked area of the front fog light hole cover shown in the figure. Note • Remove all the shaded area shown in the figure so that the front fog light hole cover does not interfere with the bolt. (5) Temporarily tighten the bolt. (6) Install the screw. (7) Install the front fog light and the bracket to the front bumper. (8) Connect the connector. (9) Move the front fog light in the direction of the arrow shown in the figure and adjust the brightness borderline. (10) Tighten the bolt. (11) Install the front mudguard. (See MUDGUARD REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) (12) Connect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) Front Fog Light (RH) (With Headlight Cleaner System) 1. Empty the vehicle except for the spare tire, jack and vehicle tools. 2. Adjust the tire pressure to the specification. (See WHEEL AND TIRE SPECIFICATION .) 3. Move the vehicle to level ground. 4. Verify that the actual brightness borderline of the fog light is at the brightness borderline position indicated by the adjustment-use screen. • If the actual brightness borderline is not in the position indicated on the adjustment-use screen, perform the following adjustment: (1) Disconnect the negative battery cable. Note • The auto leveling control module stores the vehicle specification information. • A new auto leveling control module does not store any vehicle specification information. • When the ignition is switched ON after the auto leveling control module is replaced, the auto leveling control module reads the vehicle specification information sent via CAN transmission from the instrument cluster, and stores the vehicle specification information. • The auto leveling control module records the vehicle height while it is unoccupied. • Even if the battery is disconnected, the unoccupied vehicle height recorded by the auto leveling control module is not erased. • The new auto leveling control module does not record the vehicle height while it is unoccupied. • The auto leveling control module reads the vehicle height information from the auto leveling sensor and records the vehicle height while it is unoccupied when the headlight auto leveling system initial setting is performed after the auto leveling control module is replaced. 1. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Remove the following parts: L.H.D. 1. Front scuff plate (LH) (See FRONT SCUFF PLATE REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 2. Front side trim (LH) (See FRONT SIDE TRIM REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 3. Bonnet release lever (See BONNET RELEASE LEVER AND RELEASE CABLE REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 4. Fuel-filler lid opener lever (See FUEL-FILLER LID OPENER AND LEVER REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 5. Driver-side lower panel (See DRIVER-SIDE LOWER PANEL REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) R.H.D. 1. Front scuff plate (LH) (See FRONT SCUFF PLATE REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 2. Front side trim (LH) (See FRONT SIDE TRIM REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 3. Glove compartment (See GLOVE COMPARTMENT REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 4. Center panel (See CENTER PANEL REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 5. Dashboard under cover (See DASHBOARD UNDER COVER REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 6. Passenger-side lower panel (See PASSENGER-SIDE LOWER PANEL REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 3. Disconnect the connector. 4. Remove the nut. 5. Remove the auto leveling control module. 6. Install in the reverse order of removal. 7. Perform the auto leveling control module automatic configuration using the following procedure. (1) Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on) and wait for 1 min or more. (2) Switch the ignition off and wait for 3 s or more. (3) Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on) and complete the auto leveling control module automatic configuration. 8. Using the M-MDS, verify that DTCs U2300:54, U2300:55, or U2300:56 is not displayed. • If DTC U2300:54, U2300:55, or U2300:56 is displayed, go to the DTC troubleshooting procedure. (See DTC U2300:54 [HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM] .) (See DTC U2300:55 [HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM] .) (See DTC U2300:56 [HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM] .) 9. If the auto leveling control module is replaced with a new one, perform the headlight auto leveling system initialization. (See HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM INITIALIZATION .)

1. Disconnect the negative battery cable. (See NEGATIVE BATTERY CABLE DISCONNECTION/CONNECTION .) 2. Remove the auto leveling sensor. (See AUTO LEVELING SENSOR REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .) 3. Prepare three dry cell batteries (1.5 V). 4. Connect the three dry cell batteries in a series. 5. Connect the positive pole of the dry cell batteries to auto leveling sensor terminal C, and the negative pole to terminal A. 6. Connect the tester as shown in the figure with approx. 4.5 V of voltage applied between auto leveling sensor terminals A and C, and measure the voltage at auto leveling sensor terminal B. 7. Verify that the voltage fluctuates linearly between 0.5—4.5 V as shown in the figure when slowly moving the auto leveling sensor link upward or downward. • If the voltage cannot be verified as indicated in the figure, replace the auto leveling sensor. (See AUTO LEVELING SENSOR REMOVAL/INSTALLATION .)

Note • The auto leveling control module records the vehicle height in unoccupied condition by performing the headlight auto leveling system initialization. • Perform headlight auto leveling system initialization if any of the following services is performed. ― Auto leveling control module replacement ― Auto leveling sensor replacement or removal/installation ― Any service which changes vehicle height, such as suspension replacement or removal/installation • Two different procedures are available for the headlight auto leveling system initialization; one which uses the M-MDS, and one which does not. Procedure Using M-MDS Caution • Perform Steps 5 and 6 within 30 s. 1. Empty the vehicle except for the spare tire, jack and vehicle tools. 2. Adjust the tire pressure to the specification. (See WHEEL AND TIRE SPECIFICATION .) 3. Move the vehicle to level ground. 4. Connect the M-MDS to the DLC-2. 5. Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). Note • The LED headlight warning light continues flashing during the first initialization, however, continue the work because it does not indicate an improper procedure. 6. After vehicle identification, the following can be selected from the M-MDS initial screen. (1) "Electrical" (2) "ExteriorLighting" (3) "Headlamp" (4) "Auto Leveling Sensor" (5) "Auto Leveling Sensors Calibration" 7. Verify the LED headlight warning light. • The initialization is completed if the LED headlight warning light flashes three times every 0.25 s and turns off. Go to the next step. • If the LED headlight warning light flashes at 0.25 s intervals, the procedure may have been performed incorrectly. Repeat the procedure from Step 5. • If the LED headlight warning light flashes at 0.5 s intervals, the headlight auto leveling system may have a malfunction. Perform DTC inspection. (See DTC INSPECTION [HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM] .) ― Repair or replace the malfunctioning location, then repeat the procedure from Step 5. 8. Adjust the headlight aiming. (See HEADLIGHT AIMING .) Procedure Not Using M-MDS Caution • Perform Steps 4 and 5 within 30 s. 1. Empty the vehicle except for the spare tire, jack and vehicle tools. 2. Adjust the tire pressure to the specification. (See WHEEL AND TIRE SPECIFICATION .) 3. Move the vehicle to level ground. 4. Switch the ignition ON (engine off or on). Note • The LED headlight warning light continues flashing during the first initialization, however, continue the work because it does not indicate an improper procedure. Caution • If the terminals are mistakenly connected, vehicle damage or fire could occur. When connecting with the jumper wire, thoroughly verify what terminals are being connected to prevent a miss-connection. 5. Using a jumper wire, connect DLC-2 terminals B and J (ground) three times at 0.5—1.5 s intervals as shown in the figure. 6. Verify the LED headlight warning light. • The initialization is completed if the LED headlight warning light flashes three times every 0.25 s and turns off. Go to the next step. • If the LED headlight warning light flashes at 0.25 s intervals, the procedure may have been performed incorrectly. Repeat the procedure from Step 4. • If the LED headlight warning light flashes at 0.5 s intervals, the headlight auto leveling system may have a malfunction. Perform DTC inspection. (See DTC INSPECTION [HEADLIGHT AUTO LEVELING SYSTEM] .) ― Repair or replace the malfunctioning location, then repeat the procedure from Step 4. 7. Adjust the headlight aiming. (See HEADLIGHT AIMING .)

Function • The BCM sends the back-up light on request signal sent from the instrument cluster to the electrical supply unit (ESU) and the electrical supply unit (ESU) turns the back-up light on. Construction • The trunk lid light (4SD)/liftgate light (5HB) stores the back-up light bulb. Note • Fogging or condensation may occur inside the trunk lid lights (4SD)/liftgate lights (5HB), however, it is a natural phenomenon occurring as a result of a temperature difference between the interior and exterior of the trunk lid lights (4SD)/liftgate lights (5HB) and it does not affect the light performance. • Fogging or condensation occurring as a natural phenomenon will dissipate when the temperature inside the trunk lid light (4SD)/liftgate light (5HB) rises after the back-up light bulb is turned on and a period of time has elapsed. Operation Back-up lights (ATX) 1. When the selector lever is in the R position with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the TCM sends (1) an R position signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 2. When the instrument cluster receives the R position signal, it sends (2) a back-up light on request signal to the BCM. 3. The BCM sends (3) the back-up light on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 4. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the back-up light on request signal, it turns the back-up light on (4). Back-up lights (MTX) 1. When the shift lever is in the reverse position, the back-up light switch turns on (1). 2. When the back-up light switch is on with the ignition switched ON (engine off or on), the PCM detects (2) a back-up light switch on signal. 3. The PCM sends (3) the back-up light switch on signal to the instrument cluster via CAN communication. 4. When the instrument cluster receives the back-up light switch on signal, it sends (4) a back-up light on request signal to the BCM. 5. The BCM sends (5) the back-up light on request signal to the electrical supply unit (ESU) via LIN communication. 6. When the electrical supply unit (ESU) receives the back-up light on request signal, it turns the back-up light on (6). Fail-safe • Not applicable

Malfunction Detection Function • Detects malfunctions in input/output signals. • If a malfunction occurs, the auto leveling control module records the malfunction as a DTC. A recorded DTC can be read by the Mazda Modular Diagnostic System (M-MDS). Outline • The following wiper and washer systems have been adopted. ― Windshield wiper and washer system ― Rear wiper and washer system (5HB) ― Auto wiper system (With auto wiper system) Specification • A windshield wiper and washer system with continuous (low/high), auto-stop, one-touch wiper, intermittent wiper, and auto wiper (with auto wiper system), and a windshield washer and synchronized washer have been adopted. ― CAN communication has been adopted to the windshield wiper and washer system. ― A windshield washer nozzle has been adopted in which the area where the washer fluid is sprayed can be adjusted. • A rear wiper and washer system with continuous, auto-stop, and intermittent wiper, and synchronized washer have been adopted.
